definition_zh: 测试；检验；试验；化验；考查；测验
definition_en: to try something to see whether it works or is true, or an examination and similar trial used to measure quality or knowledge
core_image: 把东西放进火里、放进仪器里，看它到底行不行
scene: 实验台上摆着新电池和一盏小灯。 The engineer used the lamp to test the battery.
sceneCN: 这里 test 是「检验、测试」（第 1 个义项：试验某物以看其性能）；句意：工程师用小灯来测这块电池。

pos.zh: 测验；检验；化验；试验
测试；检验；化验；考查

derivatives.zh: 测试员；测试器（test 加表人或表物后缀构成）
测试；检测（动名词，指测试这件事）
易怒的（与 test 无词源关系，仅形近；源自法语 teste「头」）
证明；圣约（源自拉丁 testari「作证」，与 test 同出「见证」意象）

senses.title: Try something to see if it works
senses.definition: to try or examine something in order to discover whether it works or has the wanted quality
senses.definitionCN: 试用或检查某物，以发现其是否有效或具备想要的品质
senses.example: Engineers test every bridge model before building it.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师在建桥之前会测试每一个桥梁模型。
senses.why: The core image is the trial: something is put under stress so that its hidden quality shows itself.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是「试炼」：把东西置于压力之下，让隐藏的品质显形。

senses.title: Check a person's knowledge or skill
senses.definition: to give someone questions or tasks in order to measure their knowledge or ability
senses.definitionCN: 给某人出题或任务以衡量其知识或能力
senses.example: The final test covers all five units of the book.
senses.exampleCN: 期末测验涵盖本书全部五个单元。
senses.why: A trial applied to a person becomes an exam: stress is questions instead of weights.
senses.whyCN: 施加于人的「试炼」就成了考试：压力从重物换成了题目。

senses.title: Medically examine a sample
senses.definition: to examine a sample of blood, urine or other material for signs of illness or substances
senses.definitionCN: 检查血液、尿液等样本以发现疾病或物质
senses.example: Nurses will test the blood sample this afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 护士今天下午会化验这份血样。
senses.why: Examination under controlled conditions is still a trial, only run in a laboratory.
senses.whyCN: 在受控条件下检查仍是「试炼」，只是搬进了实验室。

senses.title: An examination as an event
senses.definition: a written or spoken examination of knowledge or ability
senses.definitionCN: 对知识或能力的笔试或口试
senses.example: She stayed up all night before the driving test.
senses.exampleCN: 驾照考试前她熬了通宵。
senses.why: The act of testing becomes the name of the event in which the act happens.
senses.whyCN: 测试行为转而命名其发生的那场事件。

senses.title: A trial that reveals true quality
senses.definition: a difficult situation that shows what someone or something is really like
senses.definitionCN: 显示出人或物真实品质的困难处境
senses.example: The long delay put everyone's patience to the test.
senses.exampleCN: 漫长的延误考验了每个人的耐心。
senses.why: Difficulty works like the laboratory stress: it separates real quality from claimed quality.
senses.whyCN: 困难起到实验室压力的作用：把真实品质与宣称的品质分开。

intro.en: Test comes from Latin testum, an earthen pot used by alchemists to heat metals. Trying metal in the pot became trying anything, and the word drifted through Old French into English.
intro.cn: test 源自拉丁语 testum——炼金术士焙烧金属用的陶罐。在罐中试炼金属演变为试炼一切，这个词经古法语进入英语。

items.en: Testum meant an earthen vessel, especially the cupel in which gold and silver were refined by fire.
items.cn: testum 意为陶器，尤指用火提炼金银的灰皿。

items.en: Assaying metal in the pot gave the metaphor: purity is what survives the fire.
items.cn: 在罐中检验金属形成了隐喻：纯度就是经火之后剩下的东西。

items.en: Old French test kept both the vessel and the trial of metal, and added the sense of proving a claim.
items.cn: 古法语 test 同时保留器皿与试金之义，并加上「证明主张」的义项。

items.en: English took test in the 14th century as a vessel for refining metal, used by alchemists.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入 test，指炼金术士提炼金属的容器。

items.en: By the 16th to 17th century the metaphor had won: tests of loyalty, of courage, and finally school tests.
items.cn: 至十六七世纪，隐喻占了上风：忠诚的考验、勇气的考验，最终是学校的考试。

note.en: The first group shows words that only look like test; the second ranks the words English uses for measuring trials.
note.cn: 第一组是形近词；第二组排列英语中各种「测验类」词。

entries.definition: irritable and quick-tempered; the spelling is a coincidence, from a French word for head
entries.definitionCN: 易怒的；拼写巧合，源自法语「头」一词，与 test 无关

entries.definition: proof or evidence; from Latin testari to witness, sharing the idea of proving, not the pot
entries.definitionCN: 证明；圣约；源自拉丁 testari「作证」，共享「证明」意象而非陶罐

entries.definition: to give evidence in court; from the same Latin proving family as testament
entries.definitionCN: 作证；与 testament 同出拉丁「见证」词族

entries.definition: a formal test, often longer and more official; exam is the short form
entries.definitionCN: 正式考试；常更长更正式，exam 为缩略

entries.definition: a short informal test, often for fun or quick checking
entries.definitionCN: 简短随意的测验，常用于娱乐或快查

entries.definition: a test in real conditions, often of endurance rather than knowledge
entries.definitionCN: 现实条件下的试用，常考验耐力而非知识

normalIntro.en: Real links: the alchemist's pot, the gold that survives fire, the blood test, and the driving test.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：炼金术士的陶罐、经火犹存的真金、血液化验、驾照考试。

normal.en: Test began as a pot in which metal was tried by fire.
normal.cn: test 最初是火中试金的容器。

normal.en: Only pure gold survives the fire, so test means finding what is real.
normal.cn: 只有真金经得住火，所以 test 就是找出真货。

normal.en: A blood test is the old pot in modern glass tubes.
normal.cn: 血液化验就是装进现代玻璃管的旧陶罐。

normal.en: Test the water first: dip a toe before diving in.
normal.cn: test the water：下水前先用脚尖试水。

normal.en: Put your patience to the test: the fire now burns your temper.
normal.cn: 「put one's patience to the test」：这一回火烧的是你的脾气。

abstract.en: Every test is a small fire that burns away the claims and leaves the facts.
abstract.cn: 每场测试都是一小簇火，烧掉宣称，留下事实。

abstract.en: Pressure does not create quality; it reveals it.
abstract.cn: 压力不创造品质，它只是显影品质。

abstract.en: A question is a weight placed on the mind to see if it holds.
abstract.cn: 问题就是压在头脑上的重物，看它撑不撑得住。

examples.en: The lab will test the water samples for lead.
examples.cn: 实验室将检测水样中的铅。

examples.en: He passed his driving test on the first attempt.
examples.cn: 他一次就通过了驾照考试。

examples.en: Months of delays tested the team's patience.
examples.cn: 数月的拖延考验着团队的耐心。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「贴死它」——考试时把答案死死贴在桌上也考不过，还得老老实实测 → test 测试、考验

root: 拉丁语 testum「陶罐、试金灰皿」→ 古法语 test → 英语；由「火中试金」引申出一切测试、考试与考验。

sensesIntro.en: From the alchemist's pot, test grew into trying things, examining people, checking samples, naming the exam itself, and finally any hardship that reveals true quality.
sensesIntro.cn: 从炼金陶罐出发，test 长出试物、考人、验样本、命名考试，最终指一切显露真实品质的艰难处境。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: metal tried in fire, purity revealed by what survives.
core.cn: 核心意象：火中试金，靠剩下来的东西显出纯度。

branches.en: Trying an object under stress is the oldest branch.
branches.cn: 对物件施压试验是最老的一支。

branches.en: The same trial pointed at a person becomes an exam.
branches.cn: 同一试炼指向人便成了考试。

branches.en: Laboratory checks and exam events carry the pot into modern life.
branches.cn: 化验与考试把陶罐带进现代生活。

branches.en: Hardship is the fire; character is the gold.
branches.cn: 困难是火，品格是真金。

branches.en: What survives the trial is the only honest answer.
branches.cn: 经试炼而存者，才是唯一诚实的答案。

intro.en: Test is short and mostly stands alone; the family adds -er, -ing, and the separate Latin witness family of testify and testament.
intro.cn: test 本身短小、多独立使用；词族加上 -er、-ing，另有源自拉丁「见证」的 testify 与 testament 一族。

latinIntro.en: Latin testum is the pot; a different Latin root, testis meaning witness, gives testify, testament and attestation. The two families share spelling, not origin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 testum 是陶罐；另一个拉丁词根 testis「见证人」给出 testify、testament 与 attestation。两族拼写相近，来源不同。

items.meaning: a person or device that tests
items.example: A breath tester checks the driver.
items.exampleCN: 呼气检测仪检查司机。

items.meaning: the act or process of testing
items.example: Testing of the vaccine took two years.
items.exampleCN: 疫苗测试历时两年。

items.meaning: to give evidence as a witness
items.example: She testified in court for three hours.
items.exampleCN: 她在法庭作证三小时。

items.example: His testimony freed the innocent man.
items.exampleCN: 他的证词洗清了无辜者的罪名。

items.meaning: proof; also a will; the Bible's two covenants
items.example: The ruins are a testament to the old city's wealth.
items.exampleCN: 遗迹是古城富庶的证明。

items.meaning: to confirm that something is true
items.example: Experts attested the painting's age.
items.exampleCN: 专家证实了这幅画的年代。

items.example: Students protested the fee rise.
items.exampleCN: 学生抗议学费上涨。

items.meaning: a glass tube for laboratory tests
items.example: The baby was conceived in a test tube.
items.exampleCN: 这个婴儿是试管受孕的。

items.meaning: a case tried to set a legal precedent
items.example: The court chose it as a test case.
items.exampleCN: 法院选它作判例案件。

to bear witness, to make a will

definition_zh: 脆弱性；易受伤害性；弱点；漏洞
definition_en: the state of being easily harmed, or a particular point where harm can get in
core_image: 一块木板上有一道细缝，水正从缝里一点点渗进来
scene: 这里指「脆弱性」。 A single weak password created a vulnerability that exposed the whole network.
sceneCN: 这里 vulnerability 指「系统中的一个弱点，可被利用而造成损害」（第 7 个义项：软件或网络中的安全漏洞）；句意为一个弱密码造成漏洞，使整个网络暴露。图中可辨识物件：带缝的板、渗入的水线、密码输入框、向外扩散的连线。

pos.zh: 脆弱性；易受伤害性；弱点；漏洞（可数或不可数，复数 vulnerabilities）

senses.title: The state of being easily harmed
senses.definition: the condition of being open to harm because of weakness or lack of protection
senses.definitionCN: 因脆弱或缺少保护而处于可能受害的状态
senses.example: The storm exposed the vulnerability of the low-lying villages.
senses.exampleCN: 这场风暴暴露了低洼村庄的脆弱。
senses.why: vulnerability is the noun of vulnerable, and both rest on the Latin word for a wound, so the state named is one of being woundable.
senses.whyCN: vulnerability 是 vulnerable 的名词，二者都基于拉丁语「伤口」一词，因此所命名的状态就是「可被伤到」。

senses.title: A specific weak point
senses.definition: a particular point in a system, plan or defence where harm can enter
senses.definitionCN: 系统、计划或防御中可让损害进入的具体一点
senses.example: The report identified three vulnerabilities in the supply chain.
senses.exampleCN: 报告指出供应链中的三处薄弱环节。
senses.why: a state can be counted once it is located, so the noun also names the individual gap rather than the general condition.
senses.whyCN: 状态一旦能被定位便可计数，因此这个名词也指一个个具体的缺口，而非笼统的状况。

senses.title: Ecological vulnerability
senses.definition: the likelihood that an ecosystem or species will suffer from a disturbance
senses.definitionCN: 生态系统或物种在受到干扰时受损的可能性
senses.example: Small range and slow breeding raise the bird's ecological vulnerability.
senses.exampleCN: 分布窄、繁殖慢，提高了这种鸟的生态脆弱性。
senses.why: ecology turns the state into a probability, asking how much damage a given shock would do.
senses.whyCN: 生态学把这个状态变成概率，追问一次冲击会造成多大损伤。

senses.title: Social vulnerability
senses.definition: the greater likelihood that some groups will be harmed by a hazard because of poverty, age or discrimination
senses.definitionCN: 某些群体因贫困、年龄或歧视而更可能被灾害伤害
senses.example: Social vulnerability explains why the same flood hurt some neighbourhoods more.
senses.exampleCN: 社会脆弱性解释了为何同一场洪水对某些街区伤害更重。
senses.why: a hazard is not shared equally, so the noun is attached to groups whose circumstances leave them more exposed.
senses.whyCN: 同一灾害并非平均分配，因此这个名词被接到处境使其更暴露的群体上。

senses.title: Climate vulnerability
senses.definition: the degree to which a place or system can be hurt by climate hazards and cannot adapt
senses.definitionCN: 某地或某系统受气候灾害影响且难以适应的程度
senses.example: The atlas maps climate vulnerability along the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 这份图集标出了沿海的气候脆弱性。
senses.why: climate science needed a combined measure of exposure and inability to adapt, and this noun supplies it.
senses.whyCN: 气候科学需要一个把暴露程度与无力适应合并起来的度量，这个名词正好提供。

senses.title: Emotional openness
senses.definition: the willingness to let others see one's feelings and weaknesses
senses.definitionCN: 愿意让他人看到自己的情感与弱点
senses.example: Her vulnerability in the interview made the story believable.
senses.exampleCN: 她在访谈中的坦诚示弱让这个故事可信。
senses.why: psychology gave the same word a positive turn: letting the guard down is what allows trust to form.
senses.whyCN: 心理学给同一个词加了正面转向：放下防备，信任才有可能形成。

senses.title: A flaw that can be exploited
senses.definition: a weakness in software or a network that an attacker can use to gain access
senses.definitionCN: 软件或网络中可被攻击者利用以取得访问权的弱点
senses.example: A single weak password created a vulnerability that exposed the whole network.
senses.exampleCN: 一个弱密码造成漏洞，使整个网络暴露。
senses.why: security borrowed the wound image literally: a flaw is an opening through which something hostile gets in.
senses.whyCN: 安全领域字面借用了「伤口」意象：缺陷就是让敌意之物进入的开口。

senses.title: Legal exposure of a person
senses.titleCN: 法律上个人的易受伤害状态
senses.definition: the condition of a person who cannot protect their own interests and may be exploited
senses.definitionCN: 指无法维护自身利益、可能被利用的个人处境
senses.example: The court considered the vulnerability of the witness.
senses.exampleCN: 法庭考虑了证人的易受伤害处境。
senses.why: law needs a neutral term for someone who cannot guard their own interests, and vulnerability supplies that description.
senses.whyCN: 法律需要一个中性词来描述无法维护自身利益的人，vulnerability 正好提供这一描述。

intro.en: Vulnerability is Latin vulnerabilis plus the noun suffix -ity; the base is vulnus 'wound'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: vulnerability 是拉丁 vulnerabilis 加名词后缀 -ity；基底是 vulnus「伤口」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Vulnus 'wound' supplies the stem vulner-; its own earlier origin is uncertain and the Indo-European links proposed for it are reconstructions.
items.cn: vulnus「伤口」提供词干 vulner-；它更早的来源不确定，为其提出的印欧关联均属重构。

items.en: Vulnerabilis meant 'that can be wounded', formed with the suffix -abilis 'able to be'.
items.cn: vulnerabilis 意为「能被伤到的」，由后缀 -abilis「能够被」构成。

items.en: The abstract noun vulnerability is recorded in English from the seventeenth century, at first in the literal sense of being woundable.
items.cn: 抽象名词 vulnerability 自 17 世纪在英语中有记录，最初用「可被伤到」的字面义。

items.en: The twentieth century applied the noun to groups exposed to hazards and to ecosystems likely to be damaged.
items.cn: 20 世纪把这个名词用于暴露于灾害的群体，以及可能受损的生态系统。

items.en: The security sense of a weakness that can be exploited spread in the 1990s with networked computing and formal vulnerability databases.
items.cn: 指可被利用的弱点的安全义，在 1990 年代随网络计算与正式的漏洞数据库而扩散。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates): the earliest citation for the social sense and the exact date of the computing sense are not precisely recorded, and the origin of vulnus remains unsettled.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：社会义的最早书证与计算义的准确年代都没有精确记录；vulnus 的来源仍无定论。

note.en: Group one holds forms of the same vulner- family that are easily mixed; group two holds nouns for weakness and exposure.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 vulner- 词族、容易混用的形式；第二组是表示软弱与暴露的名词。

entries.definition: Describes the thing that can be harmed; vulnerability names the state or the specific flaw.
entries.definitionCN: 描述可能受损的事物本身；vulnerability 指状态或具体缺陷。

entries.definition: Modifies how an action is done, as in speaking vulnerably; it cannot replace the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 修饰动作的方式，如坦诚示弱地说话；不能替代名词。

entries.definition: In- 'not' plus vulnerability: the state of being impossible to harm. It is a claim, often a false one.
entries.definitionCN: in-「不」加 vulnerability：不可能受伤的状态。这种说法常属虚妄。

entries.definition: From the same wound stem but means a remedy for wounds, so it belongs to medicine rather than risk.
entries.definitionCN: 同出「伤口」词干，但意为治伤的药物，属医学而非风险领域。

entries.definition: Any lack of strength; vulnerability adds the idea that the weakness can be exploited or will be hit.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指力量不足；vulnerability 添上「可被利用、会被击中」的意思。

entries.definition: The state of being left open to something; it explains the source of a vulnerability.
entries.definitionCN: 指处于毫无遮挡的状态；它解释脆弱性的来源。

entries.definition: The likelihood of being affected, especially by disease; it stresses receptiveness.
entries.definitionCN: 指容易受影响的可能性，尤指疾病；强调易接受。

entries.definition: The quality of being easily broken; it concerns the object's make rather than an attacker.
entries.definitionCN: 指容易破碎的性质；关注构造本身，而非外来攻击者。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: vulnerable 'woundable' + -ity 'state': the state of being woundable.
normal.cn: vulnerable「能被伤到」+ -ity「状态」：可被伤到的状态。

normal.en: The family runs vulnerable, vulnerability, vulnerably, invulnerable, vulnerary.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 vulnerable、vulnerability、vulnerably、invulnerable、vulnerary。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the fields: social vulnerability, climate vulnerability, security vulnerability.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各领域：社会脆弱性、气候脆弱性、安全漏洞。

normal.en: In computing, a vulnerability is a door left unlocked, not a burglar.
normal.cn: 在计算领域，漏洞是没锁的门，而不是贼。

normal.en: The plural vulnerabilities is standard for a list of flaws.
normal.cn: 列出一串缺陷时用复数 vulnerabilities。

abstract.en: Picture water finding one thin crack in a plank.
abstract.cn: 想象水找到了木板上一道细缝。

abstract.en: Picture a chain that fails at its single weakest link.
abstract.cn: 想象一条链子从最弱的一环断开。

abstract.en: Picture a person saying I need help, and meaning it.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人说出「我需要帮助」，而且当真。

examples.en: The assessment ranks vulnerability by district and by income.
examples.cn: 这项评估按地区与收入排列脆弱程度。

examples.en: Patch the vulnerability before the server goes live.
examples.cn: 在服务器上线之前修补这个漏洞。

examples.en: Reducing vulnerability is cheaper than rebuilding after a flood.
examples.cn: 降低脆弱性比洪水后重建更便宜。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「vulner（伤口）+ ability（能力）」——有「被划伤的能力」 → 脆弱性、弱点、漏洞

root: 拉丁 vulnerabilis「能被伤到的」（vulnerare「使受伤」，词干 vulnus「伤口」）+ -ity（状态）；vulnus 更深来源不确定。英语 vulnerability。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one condition: an opening exists, and it is then read as a general state, a located flaw, an ecosystem, a social group, a coastline, an open heart, a network and a witness in court.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个处境展开：存在一个开口，这个开口再被读成总体状态、被定位的缺陷、生态系统、社会群体、海岸线、敞开的心、网络与法庭上的证人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: water seeping through one thin crack in a plank.
core.cn: 核心意象：水从木板上一道细缝渗进来。

branches.en: STATE AND POINT: the condition first, then the countable spot where it lives.
branches.cn: 状态与点位：先是总体状况，再是可数的具体所在。

branches.en: ENVIRONMENTAL RISK: ecosystems and coastlines are scored by what a shock would do.
branches.cn: 环境风险：生态系统与海岸线按一次冲击的破坏力计分。

branches.en: PEOPLE AT RISK: social groups and individual witnesses can be exposed.
branches.cn: 人处于风险：社会群体与单个证人都可能暴露。

branches.en: OPEN HEART: showing weakness is the same opening, taken voluntarily.
branches.cn: 敞开的心：显露弱点也是同一个开口，只是自愿打开。

branches.en: EXPLOITABLE GAP: a network flaw is an unlocked door.
branches.cn: 可被利用的缺口：网络缺陷就是一扇没锁的门。

intro.en: Vulnerability is root plus two suffixes; the same wound root appears across the family, and -ity turns the adjective into a countable or mass noun.
intro.cn: vulnerability 是词根加两个后缀；同一「伤口」词根贯通整个词族，-ity 把形容词变成可数或不可数名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin vulnus and vulnerare give vulnerable, vulnerability and vulnerary; in- negates and -ity abstracts.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 vulnus 与 vulnerare 衍生 vulnerable、vulnerability 与 vulnerary；in- 表否定，-ity 表抽象。

items.example: The stem vulner- runs through the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 词干 vulner- 贯穿整个词族。

items.example: The verb supplies the action behind the noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供名词背后的动作。

items.example: The suffix turns a verb into a possibility.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词变成一种可能性。

items.example: The bridge is vulnerable to corrosion.
items.exampleCN: 这座桥容易受腐蚀。

items.example: The suffix makes an abstract noun of the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把形容词变成抽象名词。

items.example: The audit found one vulnerability.
items.exampleCN: 审计发现一处漏洞。

items.example: The scanner lists known vulnerabilities.
items.exampleCN: 扫描器列出已知漏洞。

items.example: No system can claim invulnerability.
items.exampleCN: 没有系统能自称无懈可击。

items.example: The bark served as a vulnerary.
items.exampleCN: 这种树皮被用作伤药。

definition_zh: （北美）草原；大草原；高草草原；草原带
definition_en: the extensive temperate grassland of North America, especially the treeless plain of the interior
core_image: 春天火烧过后，黑色残茬之上抽出新绿，平原一直铺到天边，中间没有一棵树
scene: 春季火烧之后，嫩芽从黑色残茬里钻出，一直铺到地平线。 After the spring burn, new shoots rise through the black stubble across the prairie.
sceneCN: 这里 prairie 指「北美内陆广阔的无树草原」（第 1 个义项：北美温带大草原）；句意为春季火烧之后，新芽从黑色残茬中钻出，铺满整片草原。图中可辨识物件：黑色残茬、嫩绿新芽、低平天际线、远处无树。

pos.zh: 北美草原；大草原（可数或不可数）
草原的（多作定语）

collocations.zh: 草原壶穴（冰蚀洼地湿地）

derivatives.zh: 草原大篷车（拓荒者马车）

senses.title: The North American treeless plain
senses.definition: the vast interior grassland of North America, largely treeless and once covered in perennial grasses
senses.definitionCN: 北美内陆广阔草地，基本无树，曾覆盖多年生草类
senses.example: After the spring burn, new shoots rise through the black stubble across the prairie.
senses.exampleCN: 春季火烧之后，嫩芽从黑色残茬中钻出，铺满整片草原。
senses.why: English borrowed the French word for meadow and applied it to a grassland on a scale French meadows never had.
senses.whyCN: 英语借来法语「草地」一词，却用在一个远比法国草地辽阔的草原上。

senses.title: Tallgrass prairie
senses.definition: the moist eastern prairie where grasses grow taller than a person, rooted in deep dark soil
senses.definitionCN: 较湿润的东部草原，草高过人，扎根于深厚黑土
senses.example: Big bluestem can reach two metres in a tallgrass prairie.
senses.exampleCN: 在高草草原上，大须芒草能长到两米。
senses.why: rainfall along the eastern margin lets the same biome grow tall, so the type is named by the grass height.
senses.whyCN: 东缘降水较多，让同一生物群系长出高草，于是按草高命名类型。

senses.title: Shortgrass prairie
senses.definition: the dry western prairie where grazing and low rainfall keep grasses short and the ground partly bare
senses.definitionCN: 干旱的西部草原，放牧与低降水使草保持低矮，地面部分裸露
senses.example: Shortgrass prairie survives on less than forty centimetres of rain.
senses.exampleCN: 短草草原靠不足四十厘米的降水存活。
senses.why: the same formation thins westward, and the height of the grass becomes the diagnostic feature.
senses.whyCN: 同一群系向西变稀，草的高度成了鉴别特征。

senses.title: Mixed-grass prairie
senses.definition: the transitional prairie between tall and short types, where both height classes grow together
senses.definitionCN: 介于高草与短草类型之间的过渡草原，两个高度级混生
senses.example: Mixed-grass prairie shifts its balance with each wet or dry decade.
senses.exampleCN: 混草草原的平衡随每个湿润或干旱的十年而移动。
senses.why: where rainfall is intermediate, neither height class wins, so the type is named for the mixture itself.
senses.whyCN: 降水居中之处，两个高度级都不占绝对优势，于是类型按混合本身命名。

senses.title: Prairie soil and the farm belt
senses.definition: the deep, dark, nutrient-rich soil formed under prairie grass, and the farmland that uses it
senses.definitionCN: 草原草类下形成的深厚、暗色、富养分的土壤，以及利用它的农田
senses.example: Prairie soil still yields some of the world's highest maize crops.
senses.exampleCN: 草原土至今仍产出世界上最高的玉米产量之一。
senses.why: centuries of grass roots built the soil, so the land's name transferred to the soil and then to the crops grown on it.
senses.whyCN: 数百年的草根造出这种土，于是地名先转到土壤，再转到其上种的作物。

senses.title: Prairie restoration and reconstruction
senses.definition: the replanting of native prairie species on former farmland to rebuild the grassland community
senses.definitionCN: 在退耕地上补种原生草原物种，以重建草原群落
senses.example: Volunteers hand-collect seed for prairie restoration each August.
senses.exampleCN: 志愿者每年八月手工采集种子，用于草原恢复。
senses.why: restoration distinguishes a reconstructed prairie from a remnant one, a difference the word alone does not show.
senses.whyCN: 恢复工作把重建草原与残存草原区分开，而单词本身并不显示这一区别。

senses.title: Prairie pothole wetlands
senses.definition: the shallow ice-formed depressions that hold water within the prairie and support breeding ducks
senses.definitionCN: 草原上由冰蚀形成、积水的浅洼地，供养繁殖的鸭类
senses.example: Each prairie pothole can raise dozens of ducklings a year.
senses.exampleCN: 每个草原壶穴每年能养大几十只小鸭。
senses.why: the prairie is not uniform: small wetlands embedded in it carry a name built from the grassland word.
senses.whyCN: 草原并不均质：嵌入其中的小湿地也带着草原之名的构造。

senses.title: The Canadian Prairies as a region
senses.definition: the wheat-growing provinces of Manitoba, Saskatchewan and Alberta, named after their grassland cover
senses.definitionCN: 以草原覆盖得名的曼尼托巴、萨斯喀彻温与艾伯塔三省农业区
senses.example: Grain from the Prairies moves by rail to the lake ports.
senses.exampleCN: 草原三省的谷物经铁路运往湖港。
senses.why: a cover word became a proper regional name, so capitalised Prairies now means a political and economic unit.
senses.whyCN: 覆盖词变成了专有地区名，因此大写的「草原三省」现在指一个政治与经济单元。

intro.en: Prairie is a French loan: Old French praerie and Medieval Latin prataria both go back to Latin pratum 'meadow', so the word has a clear Latin line.
intro.cn: prairie 是法语借词：古法语 praerie 与中世纪拉丁 prataria 都上溯拉丁 pratum「草地」，因此有清楚的拉丁线索。

items.en: Pratum meant 'meadow'. Its further origin is debated; a link to a root meaning 'bent, spread out' is offered as a hypothesis, not a proof.
items.cn: pratum 意为「草地」。其更早来源有争论，有人提出与表示「弯曲、铺展」的词根相关，但那只是假说，并非证明。

items.en: Prataria 'meadow land' extended pratum to the ground rather than the crop of grass.
items.cn: prataria「草地」把 pratum 从草产扩展到土地本身。

items.en: Old French praerie passed into English in the seventeenth century as prairie, at first simply 'meadow'.
items.cn: 古法语 praerie 在 17 世纪以 prairie 进入英语，最初只是「草地」。

items.en: Explorers applied the familiar French word to the immense treeless grasslands of the interior, and the American sense displaced the older one.
items.cn: 探险者把这个熟悉的法语词用在内陆广袤无树的草原上，美洲义逐渐取代旧义。

items.en: Source uncertain: the pre-Latin origin of pratum is unsettled, and the exact date when prairie narrowed to the North American plain is not securely attested.
items.cn: 来源不确定：pratum 在拉丁语之前的来源无定论；prairie 收窄为北美平原的确切年代亦无可靠书证。

note.en: Group one collects the regional names for grasslands that are easily swapped; group two collects the general and local grass-cover words.
note.cn: 第一组是易被互换的各地草原名称；第二组是通用的与局部的草覆盖词。

entries.definition: The short-grass plain of Eurasia, from Ukrainian step; similar in form to prairie but a different continent and climate.
entries.definitionCN: 欧亚短草平原，来自乌克兰语 step；形态与 prairie 相近，但属不同大陆与气候。

entries.definition: The fertile grass plains of Argentina and Uruguay, from Quechua pampa 'plain'; often used in the plural.
entries.definitionCN: 阿根廷与乌拉圭的肥沃草原，来自克丘亚语 pampa「平原」；常用复数。

entries.definition: Tropical grassland with scattered trees; it has a dry season and a tree layer that prairie lacks.
entries.definitionCN: 带散生树的热带草原；有旱季与 prairie 所无的乔木层。

entries.definition: Open grassland of southern Africa, from Afrikaans veld 'field'; it ranges from sweet to sour grass types.
entries.definitionCN: 南部非洲开阔草地，来自南非荷兰语 veld「田野」；分甜草与酸草类型。

entries.definition: Any land dominated by grass; prairie is the North American member of this class.
entries.definitionCN: 任何以草为主的土地；prairie 是该类中的北美成员。

entries.definition: A small grass field kept for hay or flowers; the scale is a field, not a subcontinent.
entries.definitionCN: 用于干草或观花的小片草地；尺度是一块田，而非次大陆。

entries.definition: A flat expanse of land, which may be grass, desert or even ice; it names shape, not cover.
entries.definitionCN: 平坦的大片土地，可能是草地、荒漠甚至冰面；命名的是地形，不是覆盖。

entries.definition: Open land used for grazing, in North America often shortened from rangeland; it stresses use.
entries.definitionCN: 用于放牧的开阔地，在北美常为 rangeland 的简称；强调用途。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: prairie is French for meadow, applied to a whole continent's grass.
normal.cn: prairie 本是法语「草地」，却被用在一整块大陆的草上。

normal.en: The Latin line: pratum 'meadow' → prataria → praerie → prairie.
normal.cn: 拉丁线索：pratum「草地」→ prataria → praerie → prairie。

normal.en: Height names the types: tallgrass, mixed-grass, shortgrass.
normal.cn: 高度命名类型：高草、混草、短草。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: prairie soil, prairie fire, prairie pothole, prairie dog.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：草原土、草原火、草原壶穴、草原犬鼠。

normal.en: Capitalised Prairies names the Canadian wheat provinces.
normal.cn: 大写的 Prairies 指加拿大草原三省。

abstract.en: Think of a lawn the size of a sea, mown by fire instead of a machine.
abstract.cn: 想象一片海那么大的草坪，由火而非机器来修剪。

abstract.en: Think of soil built upward over centuries by roots that never stop reaching down.
abstract.cn: 想象土壤被从不停止向下伸的根，用几百年时间向上造出。

abstract.en: Think of a name for a meadow that grew until the meadow became a country.
abstract.cn: 想象一个「草地」之名不断长大，直到草地变成一个地区。

examples.en: Less than one per cent of the original tallgrass prairie remains.
examples.cn: 原有高草草原留存不足百分之一。

examples.en: The prairie wind carries seed for kilometres.
examples.cn: 草原风能把种子带出数公里。

examples.en: They planted prairie strips between the maize fields to hold soil.
examples.cn: 他们在玉米田之间种下草原草带以保住土壤。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「prairie」听起来像「 prairie 铺到天边」——法语「草地」被用来称北美大草原

root: 拉丁 pratum「草地」→ 中世纪拉丁 prataria「草地」→ 古法语 praerie → 英语 prairie。pratum 的拉丁语之前来源有争议，相关词根联系仅为假说。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses divide the North American grassland by grass height, soil, restoration, embedded wetlands and finally by the Canadian region it named.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项按草高、土壤、恢复、嵌入式湿地，最后按它所命名的加拿大地区，把北美草原分切开。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an unbroken grass plain reaching the horizon with no tree in sight.
core.cn: 核心意象：一片不断的草平原直到天边，望不见一棵树。

branches.en: BASE: the borrowed word fixes on a treeless plain of continental scale.
branches.cn: 基底：这个借词固定在大陆尺度的无树平原上。

branches.en: RAINFALL: wet east grows tall grass, dry west short grass, and the middle mixes both.
branches.cn: 降水：湿润的东部长大草，干旱的西部长短草，中间两者混合。

branches.en: SOIL: grass roots become deep dark earth, and the earth becomes a farm belt.
branches.cn: 土壤：草根变成深厚黑土，黑土又变成农业带。

branches.en: FRAGMENTS: what remains is restored by hand or survives as potholes inside farmland.
branches.cn: 残片：所剩者或靠人工恢复，或作为农田中的壶穴存留。

branches.en: NAME: the cover word hardens into the proper name of three provinces.
branches.cn: 名称：覆盖词固化为三个省的专名。

intro.en: Prairie is a borrowed simplex, not a prefixed word; its family grows through compounds such as prairie dog and prairie fire.
intro.cn: prairie 是借来的单纯词，不带前缀；其词族靠 prairie dog、prairie fire 这类复合词扩展。

latinIntro.en: Latin pratum and Medieval Latin prataria are the documented ancestors; the French form praerie is the immediate source.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 pratum 与中世纪拉丁 prataria 是有文献的祖先；法语形式 praerie 是直接来源。

items.example: The prairie lay flat to the west.
items.exampleCN: 草原向西平铺而去。

items.example: Latin pratum names a mown grass field.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁 pratum 指可割草的田。

items.example: Prataria widened the crop word to the ground.
items.exampleCN: prataria 把这个作物词扩到土地。

items.meaningCN: 一种穴居草原啮齿动物
items.example: A prairie dog town can hold thousands of burrows.
items.exampleCN: 一个草原犬鼠聚落可有上千个洞穴。

items.example: A prairie fire moves faster than a person can run.
items.exampleCN: 草原火的速度快过人跑。

items.meaning: dark fertile soil formed under grass
items.meaningCN: 草下形成的暗色肥沃土壤
items.example: Prairie soil is deep and high in humus.
items.exampleCN: 草原土深厚且腐殖质高。

items.example: Ducks nest around every prairie pothole.
items.exampleCN: 鸭子在每个草原壶穴周围筑巢。

items.example: Tallgrass prairie needs periodic fire.
items.exampleCN: 高草草原需要周期性火烧。

definition_zh: 骨骼；人体或动物的全部骨与软骨；一副骨架；骸骨、骷髅；建筑或船体的框架；梗概、纲要；骨干人员（最低限度的人手）；万能钥匙；化学中的碳骨架；极瘦的人（比喻）
definition_en: the bony or hard supporting framework of an animal body; also any bare supporting structure, an outline, a minimum staff or a thin person
core_image: 博物馆库房里，一副骨架按编号逐块摆开，肋骨弯成半圆，头骨垫在软布上
scene: 博物馆库房里，一副骨架按编号逐块摆开，头骨垫在软布上。 In the store room, a skeleton is laid out bone by bone on padded cloth.
sceneCN: 这里 skeleton 指「动物体内起支撑作用的全部骨与软骨」（第 1 个义项：骨骼）；句意为库房里的骨架被逐块按编号摆开，头骨垫在软布上。可辨识物件：肋骨半圆、头骨、编号标签、软布。

pos.zh: 骨骼；骨架；（建筑等的）框架；梗概；骨干人员；万能钥匙
骨架的；梗概的（作定语）

collocations.zh: 最低限度的人手；骨干班子
骨干船员；值班最少人员

senses.title: The bony framework of a body
senses.definition: the whole set of bones and cartilage that supports and shapes an animal body
senses.definitionCN: 支撑并塑造动物身体的全部骨与软骨
senses.example: In the store room, a skeleton is laid out bone by bone on padded cloth.
senses.exampleCN: 库房里的骨架被逐块摆开，头骨垫在软布上。
senses.why: The core sense is anatomical: the frame that remains when soft tissue is removed.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是解剖学的：去掉软组织后留下的那副支架。

senses.title: A set of remains
senses.definition: the bones of a dead person or animal, especially when found or buried
senses.definitionCN: 死者或死动物的骨头，尤指被发现或埋葬时
senses.example: Police found a skeleton buried beneath the floor.
senses.exampleCN: 警方在地板下发现了一具埋着的骸骨。
senses.why: The same object seen as a person's remains rather than as a structure, which shifts the tone toward death.
senses.whyCN: 同一物件被看作某人的遗骸而非结构，语气因此转向死亡。

senses.title: A hard supporting structure
senses.definition: any rigid supporting structure of an animal, including the shell of a crab or the plates of a starfish
senses.definitionCN: 动物身上任何坚硬的支撑结构，包括蟹壳或海星骨板
senses.example: The crab's skeleton is on the outside, so it must moult.
senses.exampleCN: 蟹的骨架长在外面，所以必须蜕皮。
senses.why: Comparative anatomy widened the word beyond bones, which is why exoskeleton and endoskeleton both exist.
senses.whyCN: 比较解剖学把这个词扩展到骨头之外，exoskeleton 与 endoskeleton 因此都存在。

senses.title: The frame of a building or ship
senses.definition: the bare structural frame that carries loads before cladding or plating is added
senses.definitionCN: 在覆面或铺板装上之前承担荷载的裸框架
senses.example: The steel skeleton of the tower was finished before winter.
senses.exampleCN: 这座塔的钢骨架在入冬前完工。
senses.why: Engineering borrows the anatomical word because a frame, like bones, holds everything in place.
senses.whyCN: 工程学借用解剖词，因为框架如骨骼一样把一切都固定在位。

senses.title: An outline or plan
senses.definition: the bare outline of a document, argument or course, with details still to be filled in
senses.definitionCN: 文件、论证或课程的裸轮廓，细节仍留空
senses.example: She drafted a skeleton of the report before writing it out.
senses.exampleCN: 她在正式动笔前先写出了报告的提纲。
senses.why: The metaphor treats structure as bones and detail as flesh, a very old rhetorical habit.
senses.whyCN: 比喻把结构当作骨、细节当作肉，是一种很古老的修辞习惯。

senses.title: The minimum staff needed
senses.titleCN: 最低限度的人手；骨干班子
senses.definition: the smallest number of workers required to keep a service running, as in a skeleton staff
senses.definitionCN: 维持运转所需的最少人手，如「skeleton staff」
senses.example: Only a skeleton crew stayed aboard during the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴期间船上只留了一个骨干班组。
senses.why: Here skeleton means stripped to essentials, the same idea as an outline but applied to people.
senses.whyCN: 此处 skeleton 指削到最基本的程度，与提纲同一思路，只是用于人。

senses.title: A master key
senses.definition: a key filed down so that it opens many locks, historically called a skeleton key
senses.definitionCN: 被锉成能开许多锁的钥匙，历史上称作「skeleton key」
senses.example: The caretaker opened every door with a skeleton key.
senses.exampleCN: 管理员用一把万能钥匙打开了每一扇门。
senses.why: The name comes from the key's bare, bone-like shaft rather than from any lock mechanism.
senses.whyCN: 这个名字来自钥匙光秃、似骨的柄杆，而非任何锁具机关。

senses.title: A carbon framework in chemistry
senses.definition: the arrangement of carbon atoms in a molecule, shown without most hydrogen atoms
senses.definitionCN: 分子中碳原子的排列，通常省略大部分氢原子
senses.example: The carbon skeleton decides whether the molecule is a chain or a ring.
senses.exampleCN: 碳骨架决定这个分子是链状还是环状。
senses.why: Chemistry borrows the image of a bare frame, because the skeleton is what remains when hydrogens are stripped away.
senses.whyCN: 化学借用「裸框架」的意象，因为去掉氢之后留下的正是骨架。

senses.title: An extremely thin person
senses.definition: a person so thin that bones show, described as a walking skeleton
senses.definitionCN: 瘦到骨头显露的人，被说成行走的骨架
senses.example: After the illness he was a walking skeleton.
senses.exampleCN: 病后他瘦得像一副行走的骨架。
senses.why: The metaphor is blunt rather than kind, and it works by removing flesh from the image.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻直白而不客气，靠从形象中抽掉肉来成立。

intro.en: Skeleton comes from Greek skeleton, the neuter of skeletos 'dried up', first used of a mummy or a withered body. English borrowed it through Latin and narrowed it to the bony frame.
intro.cn: skeleton 来自希腊 skeleton，是 skeletos「干枯的」的中性形式，最初用于木乃伊或干瘪的尸体。英语经拉丁借入，后收窄为骨性支架。

items.en: Skeletos meant 'dried up, withered'; the noun skeleton named a dried body, a mummy, not a living frame.
items.cn: skeletos 意为「干枯的、干瘪的」；名词 skeleton 指干瘪的尸体、木乃伊，而非活体的支架。

items.en: Latin sceleton or skeleton took the Greek noun over unchanged in meaning, and medieval anatomy kept the 'dried body' sense.
items.cn: 拉丁 sceleton 或 skeleton 原义不变地接过希腊名词，中世纪解剖学保留了「干尸」义。

items.en: In sixteenth-century anatomy the word came to mean the bony framework of a living body, and the older mummy sense faded.
items.cn: 在 16 世纪解剖学中，这个词转指活体的骨性支架，较早的木乃伊义逐渐消失。

items.en: From the eighteenth century skeleton named the bare frame of a building or ship, and later any stripped-down structure.
items.cn: 从 18 世纪起，skeleton 指建筑或船体的裸框架，后来指任何削简的结构。

items.en: Skeleton key, skeleton staff and skeleton in the closet all exploit the idea of something reduced to its bare minimum.
items.cn: 万能钥匙、骨干班子与家丑这三条短语都利用「削到最低限度」的想法。

items.en: Source uncertain (detail and first date): the exact route from the Greek 'dried body' to the modern anatomical sense is not fully documented, and the earliest English citation is a matter of record rather than certainty.
items.cn: 来源不确定（细节与首见年代）：从希腊「干尸」到现代解剖义的具体路径缺乏完整文献，最早的英语书证属于记录问题而非确定结论。

note.en: Group one separates skeleton from its adjective and from the two positional variants; group two lists the frameworks and outlines people compare with it.
note.cn: 第一组把 skeleton 与形容词及两种位置变体分开；第二组列出人们拿来比较的框架与纲要。

entries.definition: Skeletal describes what belongs to a skeleton; skeleton is the thing itself.
entries.definitionCN: skeletal 描述属于骨架之物；skeleton 是物本身。

entries.definition: An exoskeleton is a skeleton outside the soft tissue, as in insects.
entries.definitionCN: exoskeleton 是位于软组织之外的骨架，如昆虫。

entries.definition: An endoskeleton is a skeleton inside the soft tissue, as in vertebrates.
entries.definitionCN: endoskeleton 是位于软组织之内的骨架，如脊椎动物。

entries.definition: Skeleton key is a fixed compound for a master key, not a kind of bone.
entries.definitionCN: skeleton key 是万能钥匙的固定复合词，不是某种骨头。

entries.definition: Framework is the general word for any supporting structure, including building frames and conceptual ones.
entries.definitionCN: framework 是任何支撑结构的通称，包括建筑框架与概念框架。

entries.definition: Outline is the ordinary word for a bare plan; skeleton is its more figurative, structural cousin.
entries.definitionCN: outline 是裸计划的日常说法；skeleton 是更形象、更结构化的近亲。

entries.definition: Carcass names the body of a dead animal, including its flesh, so it is not limited to bones.
entries.definitionCN: carcass 指死动物的躯体，含肉，因此不限于骨头。

entries.definition: Skull is only the head part of a skeleton, not the whole frame.
entries.definitionCN: skull 只是骨架的头部，而非整副支架。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Greek skeletos 'dried up' gave a word for a mummy, which anatomy later narrowed to bones.
normal.cn: 希腊 skeletos「干枯的」给出一个指木乃伊的词，解剖学后来把它收窄为骨头。

normal.en: The family runs skeleton, skeletons, skeletal, skeletally and skeletonize.
normal.cn: 词族包括 skeleton、skeletons、skeletal、skeletally 与 skeletonize。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: skeleton key, skeleton staff, skeleton in the closet.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：万能钥匙、骨干班子、家丑。

normal.en: The positional pair is exoskeleton outside, endoskeleton inside.
normal.cn: 位置配对是：外骨骼在外，内骨骼在内。

normal.en: A skeleton crew is a crew reduced to its bones.
normal.cn: 骨干船员就是把船员削减到只剩骨架。

abstract.en: Picture a building stripped of every panel, showing only its girders.
abstract.cn: 想象一座拆掉所有面板的建筑，只剩梁架。

abstract.en: Picture a document reduced to headings with no sentences.
abstract.cn: 想象一份文件只剩标题，没有句子。

abstract.en: Picture a key filed down to a bare stem that fits many locks.
abstract.cn: 想象一把被锉成光杆、能开许多锁的钥匙。

examples.en: The museum mounted the dinosaur skeleton in a walking pose.
examples.cn: 博物馆把这具恐龙骨架装成行走的姿态。

examples.en: A skeleton staff kept the library open during the holidays.
examples.cn: 假期里一个骨干班子维持着图书馆开放。

examples.en: The report's skeleton was approved before any data were collected.
examples.cn: 报告的提纲在任何数据收集之前就通过了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「skeleton（斯凯利顿）」——只剩干骨头、别的一概没有 → 骨架、梗概

root: 希腊 skeletos「干枯的」→ 名词 skeleton 原指干尸、木乃伊；经拉丁进入英语，16 世纪解剖学收窄为骨性支架。更早的来源与确切首见年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses move from the anatomical frame to remains, hard shells, buildings, outlines, minimum staff, a master key, a carbon frame and a very thin person.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从解剖学的支架走到遗骸、硬壳、建筑、纲要、最少人手、万能钥匙、碳骨架与极瘦的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bare frame laid out bone by bone, ribs in arcs, everything soft removed.
core.cn: 核心意象：一副裸框架被逐块摆开，肋骨成弧，柔软部分全部除去。

branches.en: THE BODY: a living frame and the same frame as remains.
branches.cn: 身体：活的支架与作为遗骸的同一支架。

branches.en: MATERIAL WIDENED: shells and plates are skeletons too, if they support the body.
branches.cn: 材料放宽：只要支撑身体，壳与骨板也算骨架。

branches.en: BARE STRUCTURE: buildings, documents and molecules are all reduced to a frame.
branches.cn: 裸结构：建筑、文件与分子都被削成框架。

branches.en: REDUCED TO ESSENTIALS: minimum staff and a filed-down key keep the same image.
branches.cn: 削到基本：最少人手与被锉薄的钥匙沿用同一意象。

branches.en: FLESH REMOVED: a thin person is described as what is left without flesh.
branches.cn: 去肉：极瘦的人被描述成去掉肉之后剩下的部分。

intro.en: Skeleton is a Greek-derived noun; English adds -al for the adjective, -ize for the verb, and prefixes exo- or endo- to mark position.
intro.cn: skeleton 是希腊来源名词；英语加 -al 构成形容词、加 -ize 构成动词，并以前缀 exo- 或 endo- 标出位置。

latinIntro.en: Greek skeleton gives skeletal and skeletonize; Greek exō and endon attach to the same base in exoskeleton and endoskeleton.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 skeleton 给出 skeletal 与 skeletonize；希腊 exō 与 endon 在同一词基上构成 exoskeleton 与 endoskeleton。

items.example: The skeleton was complete except for one hand.
items.exampleCN: 这具骨架除一只手外完整。

items.example: Two skeletons lay side by side.
items.exampleCN: 两具骨架并排躺着。

items.example: Skeletal muscle pulls on bone.
items.exampleCN: 骨骼肌牵动骨头。

items.example: The two animals are skeletally similar.
items.exampleCN: 这两种动物在骨骼上相似。

items.meaning: to reduce to a skeleton; to strip down
items.example: Editors skeletonized the long report.
items.exampleCN: 编辑把冗长的报告大幅删减。

items.example: A skeleton key opened the cellar.
items.exampleCN: 一把万能钥匙打开了地窖。

items.example: A skeleton staff ran the office in August.
items.exampleCN: 八月由一个骨干班子维持办公室。

items.meaningCN: 骨干船员；最少值班人员
items.example: The skeleton crew kept the ship at anchor.
items.exampleCN: 骨干船员让船留在锚地。

items.example: The exoskeleton is shed twice a year.
items.exampleCN: 这层外骨骼一年蜕两次。

definition_zh: 水文的；水文学的；水文循环的；水文情势的；水文模型的；水文极值的
definition_en: relating to the study of water, to the water cycle or to the water conditions of a place
core_image: 一张图上并排画着雨量柱、径流曲线与地下水位线，三条线互相呼应
scene: 工程队的桌面上摊着整年的雨量柱与水位曲线，技术员用尺比对着两个峰值。 The engineers compared hydrological records from the last century.
sceneCN: 这里指「与水文学或水文情势有关的」（第 1 个义项：属于水文学研究范围、用于描述水的分布与运动）；句意为工程师比较了上个世纪的水文记录。场景物件：雨量柱、水位曲线、尺、桌面图纸。

pos.zh: 水文的；水文学的（无比较级；美式变体 hydrologic）

senses.title: Relating to hydrology
senses.definition: relating to the study of water, to the water cycle or to the water conditions of a place
senses.definitionCN: 与水的研究、水文循环或某地水文情势有关
senses.example: The engineers compared hydrological records from the last century.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师比较了上个世纪的水文记录。
senses.why: The adjective adds the Latin-derived -ical to hydrology, so it marks anything that belongs to the science or its data.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词给 hydrology 加上拉丁来源的 -ical，标记属于这门科学或其数据的事物。

senses.title: Of the water cycle
senses.definition: describing the movement of water between air, land, ocean and living things
senses.definitionCN: 描述水在空气、陆地、海洋与生物之间运动
senses.example: Hydrological models link rainfall to river flow.
senses.exampleCN: 水文模型把降雨与河流流量联系起来。
senses.why: The cycle is the central object of the science, so the adjective most often modifies cycle or model.
senses.whyCN: 循环是这门科学的核心对象，因此这个形容词最常修饰 cycle 或 model。

senses.title: Of a regional water regime
senses.definition: describing the actual water conditions of a catchment, wetland or region
senses.definitionCN: 描述某流域、湿地或区域的实际水文条件
senses.example: The wetland's hydrological regime depends on seasonal flooding.
senses.exampleCN: 湿地的水文情势取决于季节性淹水。
senses.why: When the noun is regime or condition, the adjective points to measured local behaviour rather than the discipline.
senses.whyCN: 当名词是 regime 或 condition 时，这个形容词指向实测的地方行为，而不是学科。

senses.title: Of models and data
senses.definition: describing the datasets, models and projections used to represent water systems
senses.definitionCN: 描述用来表示水系统的数据集、模型与预测
senses.example: Hydrological data are stored as daily gauge readings.
senses.exampleCN: 水文数据以每日水位读数储存。
senses.why: Modern work is largely model-based, so the adjective often means computational rather than field-based.
senses.whyCN: 现代工作大量基于模型，因此这个形容词常指计算性的，而非野外的。

senses.title: Of monitoring and measurement
senses.definition: describing gauges, stations and networks that measure water
senses.definitionCN: 描述测量水的尺度、站点与网络
senses.example: The hydrological station recorded a new high-water mark.
senses.exampleCN: 水文站记录了一个新的高水位标记。
senses.why: Observation is the empirical base of the science, so the adjective can point to the instruments themselves.
senses.whyCN: 观测是这门科学的经验基础，因此这个形容词可指仪器本身。

senses.title: Of extremes
senses.definition: describing floods, droughts and low flows that define design and risk
senses.definitionCN: 描述决定工程设计与风险的洪水、干旱与低流量
senses.example: Hydrological drought begins when river flow falls below normal.
senses.exampleCN: 当河流流量低于常年，水文干旱就开始了。
senses.why: Planning turns on rare events, so the adjective frequently names the extremes rather than the average.
senses.whyCN: 规划取决于稀有事件，因此这个形容词常指极值而非平均值。

senses.title: Of ecohydrology
senses.definition: describing the links between water and plants, animals and ecosystems
senses.definitionCN: 描述水与植物、动物及生态系统之间的联系
senses.example: Hydrological change can decide which wetland plants survive.
senses.exampleCN: 水文变化能决定哪些湿地植物存活。
senses.why: When the question is which species live where, the adjective joins water science to ecology.
senses.whyCN: 当问题变成哪些物种住在哪里，这个形容词就把水科学与生态学连起来。

senses.title: Of the hydrological year
senses.definition: describing the annual accounting period that begins when storage is lowest
senses.definitionCN: 描述从储水最低时开始的一年核算周期
senses.example: The hydrological year starts before the first snowmelt.
senses.exampleCN: 水文年在第一次融雪之前开始。
senses.why: Water budgets cannot follow the calendar year, so water managers fixed a separate year and the adjective names it.
senses.whyCN: 水的收支不能按日历年计算，因此管水者另立一个年度，形容词便用来指它。

intro.en: Hydrological is hydrology plus the adjective suffix -ical, which reaches Latin -icus and Greek -ikos. The word is a modern technical derivative. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: hydrological 是 hydrology 加形容词后缀 -ical，后者上溯拉丁 -icus 与希腊 -ikos。这个词是近代技术派生词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Hydōr 'water' is the root; its deeper origin is often linked to a reconstructed *wed- 'water', which is a reconstruction rather than a proven form.
items.cn: hydōr「水」是词根；其更深来源常被联系到重构的 *wed-「水」，那是重构而非已证实形式。

items.en: Hydrology, the study of water, was formed from hydro- plus -logy and entered English in the eighteenth century.
items.cn: hydrology 是对水的研究，由 hydro- 加 -logy 构成，十八世纪进入英语。

items.en: Greek -ikos made adjectives meaning 'of or belonging to'; Latin -icus and French -ique carried it into English.
items.cn: 希腊 -ikos 构成「属于……的」形容词；拉丁 -icus 与法语 -ique 把它带入英语。

items.en: English -ical became the fuller adjective ending, producing hydrological alongside the shorter hydrologic.
items.cn: 英语 -ical 成为较完整的形容词词尾，产生 hydrological，与较短的 hydrologic 并存。

items.en: In the twentieth century the adjective spread into hydrology, engineering and ecology, attaching to models, data and regimes.
items.cn: 到二十世纪，这个形容词扩散到水文学、工程与生态学，附着于模型、数据与情势等名词。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Greek source of hydōr is uncertain and *wed- remains a reconstruction; the first use of hydrological is not precisely dated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：hydōr 的前希腊语来源不确定，*wed- 仍属重构；hydrological 最早的使用没有精确年代。

note.en: Group one holds spelling and grammar variants of the same adjective; group two holds other water-related adjectives that describe different things.
note.cn: 第一组是同一形容词的拼写与语法变体；第二组是描述不同事物的其他水相关形容词。

entries.definition: The shorter American spelling of the same adjective; it carries no different meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 同一形容词的较短美式拼写；意义没有差别。

entries.definition: The science itself; the adjective must attach to a noun such as cycle or model.
entries.definitionCN: 学科本身；形容词必须附着于 cycle 或 model 等名词。

entries.definition: A practitioner of the science; it is a person, not a quality of data or cycles.
entries.definitionCN: 从事这门科学的人；它指人，而不是数据或循环的性质。

entries.definition: Relating to fluid power and pressure, from Greek hydraulikos; it is mechanics, not the study of the whole cycle.
entries.definitionCN: 与流体动力和压力有关，出自希腊 hydraulikos；它属力学，不是对整个循环的研究。

entries.definition: Relating to the atmospheric part of the water cycle; it is narrower than hydrological.
entries.definitionCN: 与水文循环中大气部分有关；它比 hydrological 窄。

entries.definition: Relating to the interaction of water with ecosystems; it is a specialized branch of hydrological work.
entries.definitionCN: 与水及生态系统相互作用有关；它是水文工作的专门分支。

entries.definition: Relating to the measurement and mapping of water bodies; it describes surveying, not the science of movement.
entries.definitionCN: 与水体的测量与制图有关；它描述测绘，而不是运动科学。

entries.definition: Containing or resembling water; it describes a medium, not a scientific field or cycle.
entries.definitionCN: 含水或像水的；它描述介质，而不是科学领域或循环。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real adjective endings, real technical collocations and real spelling variants.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实形容词词尾、真实技术搭配与真实拼写变体。

normal.en: Hydrology plus -ical makes the adjective hydrological.
normal.cn: hydrology 加 -ical 构成形容词 hydrological。

normal.en: The shorter hydrologic is the American spelling.
normal.cn: 较短的 hydrologic 是美式拼写。

normal.en: Hydrological cycle, model and data are the common collocations.
normal.cn: 水文循环、水文模型与水文数据是常见搭配。

normal.en: Hydrological drought is about flow, not rainfall alone.
normal.cn: 水文干旱讲的是流量，不只是降雨。

normal.en: A hydrological year starts when storage is lowest.
normal.cn: 水文年从储水最低时开始。

abstract.en: Picture three lines on one graph: rain bars, river curve and groundwater level.
abstract.cn: 想象一张图上三条线：雨量柱、河流曲线与地下水位。

abstract.en: Picture a model that turns today's rain into next week's river height.
abstract.cn: 想象一个模型，把今天的雨变成下周的河高。

abstract.en: Picture a year that begins not in January but when the water is lowest.
abstract.cn: 想象一个不在正月开始、而在水最低时开始的年份。

examples.en: Hydrological models predict how fast the flood will arrive.
examples.cn: 水文模型预测洪水到达的速度。

examples.en: The wetland's hydrological regime was altered by drainage.
examples.cn: 排水改变了湿地的水文情势。

examples.en: Hydrological stations send data every hour during the monsoon.
examples.cn: 季风期间水文站每小时发送数据。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「hydrology（水文学）+ -ical（形容词后缀）」——属于水文学的 → 水文的

root: 希腊 hydōr「水」+ -logia「研究」→ hydrology；再加希腊 -ikos / 拉丁 -icus 形成的形容词后缀 -ical → hydrological。hydōr 的更深来源不确定，*wed- 为重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one adjective: of the science, of the cycle, of a local regime, of models, of monitoring, of extremes, of ecology and of the water year.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着同一个形容词展开：属于学科、属于循环、属于地方情势、属于模型、属于观测、属于极值、属于生态、属于水文年。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: rainfall bars, a river curve and a groundwater line drawn side by side on one sheet.
core.cn: 核心意象：雨量柱、河流曲线与地下水位线并排画在同一张纸上。

branches.en: SCIENCE TO LOOP: the adjective marks both the field and its central object, the cycle.
branches.cn: 从学科到闭环：这个形容词既标记领域，也标记其核心对象——循环。

branches.en: REGIME TO GAUGE: a local pattern is known only through stations and measurements.
branches.cn: 从情势到水尺：地方格局只有通过站点与测量才被知道。

branches.en: MODEL TO EXTREME: models are tested most sharply on floods and droughts.
branches.cn: 从模型到极值：模型在洪水与干旱中受到最尖锐的检验。

branches.en: ECO USE: the same water pattern decides which species can live in a wetland.
branches.cn: 生态用法：同一套水格局决定哪些物种能在湿地生存。

branches.en: THE WATER YEAR: accounting runs on its own calendar, fixed by the lowest storage.
branches.cn: 水文年：水的核算按自己的年度，以最低储水为界。

intro.en: Hydrological is a derived adjective with a transparent base and a productive ending; the base hydrology is itself a Greek compound.
intro.cn: hydrological 是派生形容词，基词透明、词尾能产；基词 hydrology 本身又是希腊语复合词。

latinIntro.en: The adjective ending reaches Latin -icus and Greek -ikos; the root is Greek, so the Latin layer here is the ending rather than the stem.
latinIntro.cn: 形容词词尾上溯拉丁 -icus 与希腊 -ikos；词根属希腊语，因此这里的拉丁层是词尾而非词干。

items.example: Hydrology supplies the base of the adjective.
items.exampleCN: hydrology 提供这个形容词的基词。

items.example: Hydrologic is the shorter form.
items.exampleCN: hydrologic 是较短形式。

items.example: Hydrological is the fuller form.
items.exampleCN: hydrological 是较完整形式。

items.example: Hydrological data guide the design.
items.exampleCN: 水文数据指导设计。

items.example: The hydrologic cycle is a closed loop.
items.exampleCN: 水文循环是一个闭环。

items.meaning: from a hydrological point of view
items.example: Hydrologically, the two basins differ.
items.exampleCN: 从水文角度看，两个盆地不同。

items.example: A hydrologist checked the gauge.
items.exampleCN: 一位水文学家检查了水尺。

items.example: The hydrograph peaks after the rain.
items.exampleCN: 过程线在雨后达到峰值。

items.example: The hydrosphere includes ice and vapour.
items.exampleCN: 水圈包括冰与水汽。

definition_zh: 实证证据；由观察、测量或实验得到、而非仅靠推理得出的证据
definition_en: evidence gained by observation, measurement or experiment rather than by reasoning alone
core_image: 田野外一本记录册摊开，页上是手写的观测数字，旁边的仪器还带着露水
scene: 论文的方法一节说明，结论不是从模型推出来的，而是从三百次实地测量中得来的。 The claim is backed by empirical evidence from ten years of field records.
sceneCN: 这里指从实际观测中得来的证据（第 1 个义项：来自观察与测量的证据）；句意为该主张有十年野外记录形成的实证证据支撑。

pos.zh: 实证证据（不可数）

derivatives.zh: 由希腊语「经验」经拉丁语而来的形容词，义为「实证的；经验的」
加副词尾，义为「以实证方式」
加表示主义的名词尾，义为「经验主义」
加表示从事者的名词尾，义为「经验论者」
同词干名词，义为「经验主义者；江湖医生（旧义）」

senses.title: Evidence from observation or experiment
senses.titleCN: 来自观察或实验的证据
senses.definition: material produced by watching, measuring or testing rather than by argument
senses.definitionCN: 通过观察、测量或试验产生、而非由论证产生的材料
senses.example: The theory has empirical evidence behind it at last.
senses.exampleCN: 这个理论终于有了实证证据支撑。
senses.why: Empirical names what rests on experience, and evidence from the senses is the form experience takes in research.
senses.whyCN: 「实证的」指建立在经验之上，而感官所得的证据就是经验在研究中的形态。

senses.title: Field data
senses.definition: records collected in the setting where the phenomenon actually occurs
senses.definitionCN: 在现象真实发生的场景中收集的记录
senses.example: The team spent two seasons gathering empirical evidence in the delta.
senses.exampleCN: 团队在三角洲花了两个季节收集实证证据。
senses.why: The field is where conditions are uncontrolled and therefore real, which is the point of this kind of evidence.
senses.whyCN: 野外条件不受控制因而真实，这正是这类证据的意义。

senses.title: Measurement results
senses.definition: readings taken with instruments under stated conditions
senses.definitionCN: 在规定条件下用仪器取得的读数
senses.example: The empirical evidence includes pressure readings taken every hour.
senses.exampleCN: 这些实证证据包括每小时记录的气压读数。
senses.why: A measurement is experience turned into a number, and numbers can be checked by others.
senses.whyCN: 测量是把经验变成数字，而数字可被他人核对。

senses.title: Clinical trial data
senses.definition: outcomes recorded from patients under a controlled treatment protocol
senses.definitionCN: 在受控治疗方案下记录的患者结果
senses.example: Regulators asked for empirical evidence from a randomised trial.
senses.exampleCN: 监管机构要求提供随机试验产生的实证证据。
senses.why: Medicine insists on evidence produced by treated bodies, since reasoning about the body is not enough.
senses.whyCN: 医学坚持采用由受治身体产生的证据，因为对身体仅作推理并不够。

senses.title: Survey data
senses.definition: responses collected systematically from a defined group of people
senses.definitionCN: 从界定人群系统收集的回答
senses.example: The survey supplied empirical evidence about household spending.
senses.exampleCN: 这项调查提供了关于家庭支出的实证证据。
senses.why: Asking many people the same question turns scattered experience into a dataset.
senses.whyCN: 向许多人问同一个问题，就把分散的经验变成数据集。

senses.title: Evidence that can be reproduced
senses.definition: findings that another team can obtain again by repeating the procedure
senses.definitionCN: 另一团队重做同一程序仍可得到的发现
senses.example: No empirical evidence survived the replication attempt.
senses.exampleCN: 没有任何实证证据经受住重复实验。
senses.why: Experience that only one person has is testimony, but experience that repeats becomes evidence.
senses.whyCN: 只有一人拥有的经验是证词，能够重复的经验才成为证据。

senses.title: Statistical evidence from samples
senses.definition: estimates and tests computed from a sample drawn from a larger population
senses.definitionCN: 从较大总体中抽取样本后计算出的估计与检验结果
senses.example: The empirical evidence came from a sample of four hundred firms.
senses.exampleCN: 这些实证证据来自四百家企业的样本。
senses.why: Sampling lets a small observed part speak for a whole that was never seen.
senses.whyCN: 抽样让被观察到的一小部分替从未被看见的整体说话。

senses.title: Evidence used to test, not illustrate
senses.titleCN: 用于检验而非说明的证据
senses.definition: observations brought in to challenge a theory rather than to decorate it
senses.definitionCN: 用来挑战理论、而非给理论作装饰的观察
senses.example: A good study seeks empirical evidence that could prove it wrong.
senses.exampleCN: 好的研究会去寻找能证明自己错了的实证证据。
senses.why: The strongest use of experience is the attempt to falsify, since a claim that cannot fail is not tested.
senses.whyCN: 经验最强的用法是试图证伪，因为不会失败的主张并未被检验。

intro.en: Empirical evidence joins a Greek word for experience, which entered English through Latin medicine, to a Latin word for clearness. The pair insists that what is seen and measured, not what is merely argued, makes a fact clear.
intro.cn: 这个词组把希腊语中表示「经验」的词（经拉丁语医学用语进入英语），与拉丁语中表示「清楚」的词接在一起：使事实清楚的是被看见与被测量的东西，而不是仅凭论证。

items.en: Peira meant a trial or attempt, and it stands behind the word for experience; its deeper origin is not established.
items.cn: 这个词意为「尝试、试验」，是「经验」一词的来源；它更早的来源尚未确立。

items.en: With the prefix meaning in, the noun meant experience gained by trying things, as against pure reasoning.
items.cn: 加上表示「在内」的前缀后，这个名词指通过尝试得到的经验，与纯推理相对。

items.en: Latin named the physician who worked from observed cases rather than from theory, and English empiric followed.
items.cn: 拉丁语用这个词指凭观察病例而非理论行医的医生，英语的「经验主义者」随之出现。

items.en: The adjective shifted to the neutral sense of based on observation, especially in natural philosophy.
items.cn: 这个形容词转向中性含义「以观察为基础的」，尤用于自然哲学。

items.en: Evidentia meant clearness, and evidence became the material that makes a fact clear to a observer.
items.cn: 这个词意为「清楚」，「证据」遂指使事实对观察者变得清楚的材料。

items.en: The two words were fixed together in nineteenth-century science writing; the exact first record of the phrase is uncertain.
items.cn: 这两个词在十九世纪的科学写作中被固定组合；该短语确切的最早记录不确定。

note.en: The first group belongs to the experience family or looks similar; the second group names evidence by its role or its strength.
note.cn: 第一组属于「经验」同族或形近；第二组按作用或强度给证据分类。

entries.definition: Based on observation or experiment rather than theory.
entries.definitionCN: 指以观察或实验而非理论为基础的。

entries.definition: In a way that rests on observed data.
entries.definitionCN: 指以依赖观测数据的方式。

entries.definition: The philosophical view that knowledge comes from experience.
entries.definitionCN: 指知识来自经验的哲学观点。

entries.definition: A person who holds that knowledge comes from experience.
entries.definitionCN: 指主张知识来自经验的人。

entries.definition: A group of territories under one ruler; it starts from a word for command, not experience.
entries.definitionCN: 指由一位统治者统辖的领土群；起首是表示命令的词，与经验无关。

entries.definition: Relating to an empire; the resemblance is only in sound.
entries.definitionCN: 指与帝国有关的；相似仅在读音。

entries.definition: Evidence from watching without intervening, a narrower source.
entries.definitionCN: 指不介入地观察所得的证据，来源更窄。

entries.definition: Evidence from deliberate manipulation and control.
entries.definitionCN: 指经有意操作与控制所得的证据。

entries.definition: Evidence expressed as numbers, whatever its source.
entries.definitionCN: 指以数字表达的证据，不论来源。

entries.definition: Evidence from personal stories, casual and unsystematic.
entries.definitionCN: 指来自个人讲述的证据，随意且不系统。

entries.definition: Reasoning from principles without observational support.
entries.definitionCN: 指由原理推出、没有观测支撑的推理。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the field notebook, the trial and measurement, and the test-not-illustrate role.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用野外记录册、试验与测量，以及「用于检验而非装饰」的作用。

normal.en: Empirical means from experience, so empirical evidence is what the senses and instruments report.
normal.cn: 「实证的」意为来自经验，所以实证证据就是感官与仪器报告的内容。

normal.en: Field records, trial data and survey answers are all real sources of this kind of evidence.
normal.cn: 野外记录、试验数据与调查回答都是这类证据的真实来源。

normal.en: Empirical is the adjective, empirically the adverb, empiricism the philosophy behind it.
normal.cn: 「实证的」是形容词，「以实证方式」是副词，「经验主义」是它背后的哲学。

normal.en: A randomised trial is the clearest case, because the comparison is built into the design.
normal.cn: 随机试验是最清楚的情形，因为比较被写进了设计。

normal.en: The strongest empirical work tries to find evidence that would defeat its own claim.
normal.cn: 最强的实证研究试图找到能击败自身主张的证据。

abstract.en: Experience is the world answering back, and empirical evidence is the record of that answer.
abstract.cn: 经验是世界在回话，实证证据就是那句回话的记录。

abstract.en: A theory that cannot be embarrassed by data is not really a theory but a belief.
abstract.cn: 不会被数据弄得难堪的理论，其实不是理论而是信念。

abstract.en: The field notebook is humble, yet it outranks the elegant model when the two disagree.
abstract.cn: 野外记录册很不起眼，可它一与漂亮模型冲突就压过模型。

examples.en: There is little empirical evidence that the policy changed behaviour.
examples.cn: 几乎没有实证证据表明该政策改变了行为。

examples.en: The argument is elegant but lacks empirical evidence.
examples.cn: 这个论证很漂亮，却缺少实证证据。

examples.en: They collected empirical evidence from forty schools over three years.
examples.cn: 他们用三年时间从四十所学校收集实证证据。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「实证」来自「经验」，「证据」来自「看清」：亲手试过、量过，把事实看清，就是实证证据

root: 「实证的」源自希腊语 empeiria「经验」，由 en-「在内」与 peira「尝试」构成，经拉丁语医学用语 empiricus 进入英语，十七世纪转为「以观察为基础」的中性义。「证据」来自拉丁语 evidentia「清楚」。该短语在十九世纪科学写作中固定；最早记录不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from the field to the test: observation, field data, measurements, trial data, survey data, reproducible findings, sample statistics, and evidence used to try to falsify.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从野外延伸到检验：观察、野外数据、测量、试验数据、调查数据、可重复的发现、样本统计、用于证伪的证据。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a notebook of hand-written readings lies open in a field, dew still on the instrument beside it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一本手写读数的记录册在野外摊开，旁边仪器上还挂着露水。

branches.en: THE OBSERVED WORLD: evidence taken from settings where the phenomenon is real.
branches.cn: 被观察的世界：从现象真实发生的场景取得的证据。

branches.en: THE INSTRUMENT AND THE TRIAL: readings and controlled patient outcomes.
branches.cn: 仪器与试验：读数与受控的患者结果。

branches.en: THE ASKED AND SAMPLED: survey answers and estimates from a sample.
branches.cn: 提问与抽样：调查回答与由样本得出的估计。

branches.en: THE REPEATABLE FINDING: a result another team can obtain again.
branches.cn: 可重复的发现：另一团队能再次得到的结果。

branches.en: THE FALSIFYING USE: observations brought in to defeat a claim.
branches.cn: 证伪的用法：用来击败主张的观察。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Greek experience word, which reached English through Latin medicine, to a Latin clearness word.
intro.cn: 这个词组把希腊语的经验词（经拉丁语医学进入英语）与拉丁语的「清楚」词接起来。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies empiricus and evidentia; Greek peira stands behind the first, and its deeper root is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了「经验论的」与「清楚」；前者背后是希腊语「尝试」，其更深词根不确定。

items.example: It turns a trial into experience held inside a person.
items.exampleCN: 它把「尝试」变成留在人之内的经验。

items.example: The root behind experience.
items.exampleCN: 这是「经验」背后的词根。

items.example: It passed through Latin into learned English.
items.exampleCN: 它经拉丁语进入学术英语。

items.example: It gave English empiric and empirical.
items.exampleCN: 它给英语提供了「经验论的」与「实证的」。

items.example: It marks empirical as an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它把「实证」标为形容词。

items.example: The root of evidence.
items.exampleCN: 这是「证据」的词根。

items.example: It became the word for evidence.
items.exampleCN: 它成为「证据」一词。

items.example: It marks the noun evidence.
items.exampleCN: 它标出名词「证据」。

derivatives.zh: 希腊语「经验」经拉丁语而来，义为「实证的」
加副词尾，义为「以实证方式」
加主义名词尾，义为「经验主义」
加从事者名词尾，义为「经验论者」
拉丁语「清楚」经法语而来，义为「证据」

definition_zh: 压制；镇压；抑制；忍住；隐瞒；抑制（生理反应）
definition_en: to put something down by force, to hold it back from expression or release, and to keep it from being known
core_image: 桌上立着一根弹簧，一只手把它压到桌面，弹簧在掌下弯成扁弧，一松手就会弹起
scene: 桌上立着一根弹簧，一只手把它压到桌面，弹簧在掌下弯成扁弧，一松手就会弹起。 The officer tried to suppress the disturbance before it spread.
sceneCN: 这里指以力量制止、镇压（第 1 个义项：用武力压住骚乱）；句意为那名官员试图在骚乱扩散之前把它压制住。

pos.zh: 压制；镇压；抑制；忍住；隐瞒

derivatives.zh: 由该动词加表示动作结果的名词尾构成，义为「压制；抑制；隐瞒」
由该动词加表示施动者或装置的名词尾构成，义为「压制者；抑制器」
由该动词加表示起某作用之物的词尾构成，义为「抑制剂（尤指止咳药）」
由该动词加表示可能性的形容词尾构成，义为「可被压制的」
由该动词加表示性质的形容词尾构成，义为「压制的；抑制性的」

senses.title: Put down a revolt by force
senses.definition: to end an uprising, riot or disturbance using authority or armed force
senses.definitionCN: 用权威或武力结束暴动、骚乱或动乱
senses.example: Troops were sent to suppress the revolt.
senses.exampleCN: 军队被派去镇压叛乱。
senses.why: The Latin compound means to press from below, and a force that presses a crowd down is the oldest sense of the word.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁复合词意为「从下面压」，而把人群压下去的力量，正是这个词最古老的义项。

senses.title: Hold back an expression of feeling
senses.definition: to stop a smile, laugh, tear or cry from showing or escaping
senses.definitionCN: 阻止笑、哭或眼泪表现出来或发出
senses.example: She could not suppress a smile at the joke.
senses.exampleCN: 听到那个笑话，她忍不住笑了。
senses.why: A feeling pushes upward like a spring, and suppressing it is the hand that keeps the spring compressed.
senses.whyCN: 情绪像弹簧一样向上顶，而「抑制」就是那只把弹簧压住的手。

senses.title: Hold back a bodily reflex
senses.definition: to prevent a cough, sneeze or yawn from happening or being heard
senses.definitionCN: 阻止咳嗽、打喷嚏或打哈欠发生或被听见
senses.example: He tried to suppress a cough during the lecture.
senses.exampleCN: 讲座期间他努力忍住咳嗽。
senses.why: Here the body itself is the spring, and the will is the hand pressing it down for a while.
senses.whyCN: 这里身体本身就是那根弹簧，而意志是暂时把它压住的手。

senses.title: Keep information from the public
senses.definition: to prevent a report, fact or image from being published or circulated
senses.definitionCN: 阻止报道、事实或图像被发表或传播
senses.example: The government tried to suppress the report.
senses.exampleCN: 政府试图压下那份报告。
senses.why: What is pressed down cannot rise into view, so the word moved from crowds to facts that someone wants buried.
senses.whyCN: 被压住的东西无法升到眼前，于是这个词从人群转到有人想埋掉的事实。

senses.title: Hold back growth
senses.definition: to stop plants, cells or organisms from growing or spreading
senses.definitionCN: 阻止植物、细胞或生物生长或蔓延
senses.example: Chemical sprays suppress the weeds along the fence.
senses.exampleCN: 化学喷剂抑制了篱笆边的杂草。
senses.why: Growth is an upward push too, and agriculture uses the same pressing image as politics.
senses.whyCN: 生长同样是一种向上的推力，农业用的也是政治里那同一个「压」的意象。

senses.title: Reduce a biological response
senses.definition: in medicine and biology, to weaken an immune, inflammatory or nervous response
senses.definitionCN: 医学与生物学中指减弱免疫、炎症或神经反应
senses.example: The drug suppresses the immune response.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药抑制免疫反应。
senses.why: A response that has been damped down is literally held back, which is exactly what the Latin verb says.
senses.whyCN: 被压低的反应字面上就是被按住，这正是那个拉丁动词所说的。

senses.title: Reduce sound or vibration
senses.definition: to lessen noise, echo or shaking produced by a machine or a room
senses.definitionCN: 减弱机器或房间产生的噪音、回声或震动
senses.example: New panels were fitted to suppress the engine noise.
senses.exampleCN: 安装了新面板以压制发动机噪音。
senses.why: Sound is a wave that pushes outward, and damping it is another version of pressing down.
senses.whyCN: 声音是向外推的波，把它减弱又是「压下去」的另一种版本。

senses.title: Keep evidence from being seen
senses.definition: to hide a document, witness or fact that would otherwise come before a court
senses.definitionCN: 藏起本会呈上法庭的文件、证人或事实
senses.example: The company was accused of suppressing evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 该公司被指控隐瞒证据。
senses.why: The legal sense sharpens the secrecy sense: what is suppressed is not destroyed but kept from surfacing.
senses.whyCN: 法律义把「隐瞒」义磨得更锋利：被压下的东西不是被销毁，而是被阻止浮出水面。

senses.title: Put out a fire
senses.definition: to stop a fire or flame from spreading by smothering or cooling it
senses.definitionCN: 用窒息或降温的方式阻止火或火焰蔓延
senses.example: Firefighters worked fast to suppress the blaze.
senses.exampleCN: 消防员迅速行动扑灭大火。
senses.why: Fire is the most visible thing that spreads upward, and putting it out is the word at its most physical.
senses.whyCN: 火是最显眼的向上蔓延之物，把火扑灭正是这个词最物理的一面。

intro.en: Suppress comes from Latin suppressus, the past participle of supprimere, to press down, built from sub-, under, and premere, to press.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语 suppressus，即 supprimere「向下压」的过去分词，由 sub-「在下」与 premere「压」构成。

items.en: Premere meant to press, squeeze or stamp, and its family includes press and imprint.
items.cn: premere 意为压、挤或印，其同族包括「压」与「印痕」等词。

items.en: The compound added the idea of downward pressure, and it could describe both a foot on a thing and a force on a people.
items.cn: 这个复合词加上向下的压力，既能描述脚踩在某物上，也能描述力量压在人群上。

items.en: The participle meant pressed down or held back, and English took it as an adjective before it took it as a verb.
items.cn: 这个分词意为被压下、被按住的，英语先把它作形容词用，再作动词用。

items.en: The verb entered English in the late Middle Ages with the political sense first; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个动词在中世纪末进入英语，最先带的正是政治义；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Medicine extended the word to coughs, immune responses and hormones that the body itself holds back.
items.cn: 医学把词扩展到咳嗽、免疫反应与身体自身会抑制的激素。

items.en: Journalism gave the word its common modern sense of keeping a story out of sight.
items.cn: 新闻业赋予它常见的现代义：把一则报道挡在视线之外。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like suppress; the second group names neighbouring ways of holding something down.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与 suppress 相近；第二组是与「压住、止住」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: The act of putting something down or keeping it from showing.
entries.definitionCN: 指压制、抑制或隐瞒的行为。

entries.definition: A person or device that holds something back.
entries.definitionCN: 指进行压制的人或装置。

entries.definition: A substance that reduces a bodily function, especially a cough.
entries.definitionCN: 指减弱身体功能的物质，尤指止咳药。

entries.definition: Acting to hold something down or reduce it.
entries.definitionCN: 指起压制或减弱作用的。

entries.definition: To think something is likely; it shares the prefix but rests on a verb meaning to place.
entries.definitionCN: 指认为某事很可能；共享前缀，但底层是意为「放置」的动词。

entries.definition: To push a feeling or memory back so that it does not enter awareness; it stresses the inward push.
entries.definitionCN: 指把情绪或记忆压回去使其不进入意识；强调向内的推压。

entries.definition: To keep people under harsh control over a long time; it stresses the weight on the group.
entries.definitionCN: 指长期以严酷方式统治人群；强调压在群体身上的重量。

entries.definition: To hold someone or something back from acting; it stresses the leash rather than the weight.
entries.definitionCN: 指阻止某人或某物行动；强调缰绳而非重量。

entries.definition: To put down a disturbance or a strong feeling; close to the first sense but more literary.
entries.definitionCN: 指平息骚动或强烈情绪；接近第一个义项，但更书面。

entries.definition: To cut off the air or the expression of something; it stresses suffocation more than pressure.
entries.definitionCN: 指切断空气或某种表达；强调窒息感而非压力。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the pressing root, the downward prefix and the many objects the word has been applied to.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想利用「压」的词根、向下的前缀，以及这个词曾被用到的众多对象。

normal.en: The prefix means under and the verb means press, so the word says press under.
normal.cn: 前缀意为「在下」，词根意为「压」，所以这个词说的就是「往下压」。

normal.en: A hand on a spring is the picture: hold it down and it cannot jump.
normal.cn: 手压弹簧就是那幅图：按住它，它就弹不起来。

normal.en: A cough suppressant does to a cough what a lid does to a flame.
normal.cn: 止咳药对咳嗽做的事，就像盖子对火焰做的事。

normal.en: A suppressed report is a report someone is sitting on.
normal.cn: 被压下的报道，就是有人坐在上面的报道。

normal.en: The word covers crowds, smiles, coughs, weeds, immune cells, noise, evidence and fire, all by the same downward gesture.
normal.cn: 这个词覆盖人群、笑容、咳嗽、杂草、免疫细胞、噪音、证据与火焰，靠的都是同一个向下压的手势。

abstract.en: Suppression works by making something invisible rather than by making it cease to exist.
abstract.cn: 压制靠的是让某物看不见，而不是让它不再存在。

abstract.en: What is held down keeps its energy; release it and the spring jumps.
abstract.cn: 被压住的东西保留着能量；一松手，弹簧就会跳起来。

abstract.en: A society that suppresses a fact usually pays for it later in a larger disturbance.
abstract.cn: 压制事实的社会，通常要在之后以更大的动荡付出代价。

examples.en: The regime suppressed every paper that criticised it.
examples.cn: 该政权压制了每一份批评它的报纸。

examples.en: She suppressed a yawn and kept writing.
examples.cn: 她忍住哈欠，继续写下去。

examples.en: Doctors gave him a drug to suppress the inflammation.
examples.cn: 医生给他一种药以抑制炎症。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「瑟普雷斯」——「瑟」抖的弹簧被「普雷」一下压平，还「斯」的一声贴住桌面：压制

root: 拉丁语 premere「压」→ sub-「在下」+ premere 构成 supprimere「向下压」→ 过去分词 suppressus「被压住的」→ 英语 suppress「压制；抑制；隐瞒」；核心动作始终是「从上方把东西按下去」。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses share one downward gesture: a revolt, a smile, a cough, a report, weeds, an immune response, noise, evidence and a fire.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项共享同一个向下压的手势：叛乱、笑容、咳嗽、报道、杂草、免疫反应、噪音、证据与火焰。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a palm pressing a standing spring flat against the table.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手掌把立着的弹簧压平在桌面上。

branches.en: THE FORCE BRANCH: troops end a revolt, and firefighters end a blaze.
branches.cn: 武力分支：军队平息叛乱，消防员扑灭大火。

branches.en: THE HELD-BACK BRANCH: a smile is kept in and a cough is kept down.
branches.cn: 忍住分支：笑容被收住，咳嗽被压下。

branches.en: THE SECRECY BRANCH: a report is buried and evidence is kept from court.
branches.cn: 隐瞒分支：报道被埋掉，证据被挡在法庭之外。

branches.en: THE BIOLOGY BRANCH: sprays hold weeds back and drugs damp an immune response.
branches.cn: 生物分支：喷剂抑制杂草，药物压低免疫反应。

branches.en: THE NOISE BRANCH: panels take the push out of engine sound.
branches.cn: 噪音分支：面板卸掉发动机声音里的推力。

intro.en: Suppress is a Latin compound of under and press, and English added a full set of noun and adjective endings to it.
intro.cn: 这是一个由「在下」与「压」构成的拉丁复合词，英语又给它配上一整套名词与形容词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies the prefix sub-, the verb premere and its compound supprimere, whose participle English borrowed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供前缀 sub-、动词 premere 及其复合词 supprimere，英语借用的正是它的分词。

items.example: It gives the pressure its downward direction.
items.exampleCN: 它给这份压力一个向下的方向。

items.example: The verb is the physical core of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是整族词的物理核心。

items.example: The compound already carries both the physical and the political sense.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词已经同时带有物理义与政治义。

items.example: English took this participle as the base of the verb.
items.exampleCN: 英语把这个分词作为动词的基础。

items.example: It forms the noun for the act of putting down.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示「压下」这一动作的名词。

items.example: It names the person or device that suppresses.
items.exampleCN: 它命名进行压制的个人或装置。

items.example: It forms the name of a cough-reducing drug.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示止咳药物的名称。

items.example: It marks what can be held down.
items.exampleCN: 它标出可以被压住的东西。

items.example: It forms the adjective for a damping action.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示「起压制作用」的形容词。

derivatives.zh: 由该动词加表示动作结果的名词尾构成，义为「压制；抑制；隐瞒」
由该动词加表示施动者或装置的名词尾构成，义为「压制者；抑制器」
由该动词加表示起某作用之物的词尾构成，义为「抑制剂（尤指止咳药）」
由该动词加表示可能性的形容词尾构成，义为「可被压制的」
由该动词加表示性质的形容词尾构成，义为「压制的；抑制性的」

definition_zh: 鸟类的；鸟纲的；禽源的（疾病）；某一地区鸟类区系的；似鸟的
definition_en: relating to birds, whether as a class of animals, as the source of a disease, as a regional fauna, or as a model for birdlike form
core_image: 清晨湿地的芦苇丛里，鸟的骨架、羽毛与鸣声被同一位记录者收进同一本册子
scene: 养殖场的鸡舍外拉起警戒线，防疫人员穿着白色防护服逐笼取样。 The outbreak was confirmed as avian influenza after samples from three sheds tested positive.
sceneCN: 这里 avian 是「禽源的」（第 3 个义项：指病原源自鸟类、在禽类之间传播的疾病）；句意为三个鸡舍的样本检测呈阳性后，这次暴发被确认为禽流感。

pos.zh: 鸟类的；鸟纲的；禽源的
（罕用名词）鸟；可数

senses.title: Of or Relating to Birds
senses.definition: of, relating to, or characteristic of birds as a class of animals
senses.definitionCN: 属于、关于鸟类这一动物类群的，或为其特征的
senses.example: The aviary sign explained the avian traits shared by all the birds inside.
senses.exampleCN: 鸟舍的标牌说明了里面所有鸟共有的鸟类特征。
senses.why: Latin avis simply means 'bird', and -an makes an adjective, so the widest sense is the plainest one: anything that has to do with birds.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 avis 就是「鸟」，-an 使其成为形容词，所以最宽的义项也是最直白的：与鸟有关的一切。

senses.title: Resembling a Bird in Form
senses.titleCN: 形似鸟的；有鸟的形态的
senses.definition: having a shape, outline, or movement that suggests a bird without actually being one
senses.definitionCN: 形状、轮廓或动作像鸟，但本身并不是鸟
senses.example: The glider's avian profile let it ride thermals with very little engine noise.
senses.exampleCN: 滑翔机形似鸟的轮廓使它几乎不需要引擎声就能乘着热气流飞行。
senses.why: once the adjective means 'of birds', it can be lent to anything that borrows a bird's silhouette or motion, with no claim that the thing is alive.
senses.whyCN: 形容词一旦表示「鸟的」，就可以借给任何借用鸟的轮廓或动作的事物，并不声称那东西是活物。

senses.title: Of Diseases Carried by Birds
senses.definition: used of infections whose pathogen circulates in birds and can pass from them to other animals
senses.definitionCN: 用于描述病原在鸟类中循环、并可由鸟传给其他动物的感染
senses.example: Avian influenza reached the farm through wild waterfowl using the pond.
senses.exampleCN: 禽流感经由使用池塘的野生水禽传入这家养殖场。
senses.why: public health naming puts the source animal in front of the disease, so avian marks where the pathogen normally lives, not who is sick now.
senses.whyCN: 公共卫生命名把来源动物放在疾病名前，因此 avian 标明病原通常寄居何处，而不是眼下谁在生病。

senses.title: Of a Region's Bird Fauna
senses.definition: used of the whole assemblage of bird species found in a given area
senses.definitionCN: 用于描述某一地区所见的全部鸟类物种组合
senses.example: Avian diversity falls sharply above the treeline on this mountain.
senses.exampleCN: 在这座山上，鸟类多样性在树线以上急剧下降。
senses.why: because avis is a kind of animal, the adjective can label a fauna by its kind, the way one says mammalian fauna for the mammals of a place.
senses.whyCN: 因为 avis 是一类动物，形容词可以按类别给一个动物区系贴标签，就像用哺乳动物区系指某地的哺乳类。

senses.title: Of Bird Anatomy and Air Flow
senses.titleCN: 鸟类解剖结构的（如肺与气囊）
senses.definition: used of anatomical structures unique to birds, especially the fixed lung and the air sacs
senses.definitionCN: 用于描述鸟类特有的解剖结构，尤其是固定的肺与气囊
senses.example: The avian lung does not expand like a mammal's; air moves through it in one direction.
senses.exampleCN: 鸟类的肺不像哺乳动物的肺那样扩张，空气单向穿过它。
senses.why: comparative anatomy needs a short label for 'the bird version of an organ', and avian supplies it without naming a species.
senses.whyCN: 比较解剖学需要一个短标签来表示「器官的鸟类版本」，avian 不必点名物种就能提供它。

senses.title: Of Research That Takes Birds as Its Subject
senses.titleCN: 以鸟为研究对象的（方法与课题）
senses.definition: used of field methods and study designs whose subject is birds rather than of the birds themselves
senses.definitionCN: 用于描述以鸟为研究对象而非描述鸟本身的野外方法与研究设计
senses.example: Avian point counts were repeated at each plot for three mornings.
senses.exampleCN: 每个样地连续三个早晨重复进行了鸟类定点计数。
senses.why: the adjective shifts from the animal to the practice: a count, a survey, or a model can be called avian because birds are what it measures.
senses.whyCN: 形容词从动物转向做法：计数、调查或模型可以被称为 avian，因为它测量的对象是鸟。

senses.title: Of Flight Modelled on Birds
senses.definition: used of wings, aircraft, or robots whose motion is copied from bird flight
senses.definitionCN: 用于描述动作模仿鸟类飞行的翼、飞行器或机器人
senses.example: The team tested an avian-inspired wing that folds on the downstroke.
senses.exampleCN: 团队测试了一种在下扑时折拢的仿鸟机翼。
senses.why: engineering borrows the bird as a working model, so avian labels the source of a design rather than a biological fact.
senses.whyCN: 工程学把鸟当作可用的模型来借用，因此 avian 标注的是设计来源，而非生物学事实。

senses.title: A Bird, in Technical Prose
senses.definition: rare countable noun: a bird, used mostly in survey writing and museum catalogues
senses.definitionCN: 罕用的可数名词：一只鸟，多见于调查记录与博物馆目录
senses.example: A single avian was recorded on the transect, a female warbler.
senses.exampleCN: 样线上只记录到一只鸟，是雌性柳莺。
senses.why: the adjective was long ago turned into a noun by writers who wanted a neutral count word, and the usage survives in clipped field notes.
senses.whyCN: 想用中性计数词的写作者早已把这个形容词名词化，这一用法在简省的野外记录里留存下来。

intro.en: Avian is Latin avis 'bird' plus the adjective suffix -an (Latin -anus). English took the word from scientific Latin in the nineteenth century; the deeper origin of avis is not settled.
