intro.cn: avian 是拉丁 avis「鸟」加形容词后缀 -an（拉丁 -anus）。英语在 19 世纪从科学拉丁语引入这个词；avis 更早的来源尚无定论。

items.en: Avis, genitive avis, is a feminine noun of the third declension meaning 'bird'; it names any bird rather than a species, and its pre-Latin origin is uncertain.
items.cn: avis 是阴性第三变格名词，属格同为 avis，意为「鸟」；它泛指任何鸟而非某一物种，其在拉丁语之前的来源不确定。

items.en: The suffix -anus meant 'belonging to, pertaining to', and it regularly became -an in English adjectives such as mammalian and avian.
items.cn: 后缀 -anus 意为「属于……的、与……有关的」，在英语形容词中通常写作 -an，如 mammalian 与 avian。

items.en: Avian is recorded in English from the nineteenth century, first in zoological description; the exact first citation is not firmly established.
items.cn: avian 在英语中自 19 世纪有记录，最早见于动物学描述；确切的首次书证尚未定论。

items.en: The phrase avian influenza became standard in veterinary virology once fowl plague was shown to be caused by a virus, and the adjective then named the reservoir rather than the patient.
items.cn: 当鸡瘟被证明由病毒引起后，avian influenza 这一说法在兽医病毒学中成为标准，形容词由此指病原宿主而非患病者。

items.en: Avis also underlies aviary and aviculture, and, through French, aviation; the link to aviation is generally accepted, though the French intermediate steps are thinly documented.
items.cn: avis 也衍生出 aviary 与 aviculture，并经法语进入 aviation；与 aviation 的联系一般认为是正确的，但法语中介环节的书证较单薄。

items.en: Source uncertain: no agreed pre-Latin reconstruction for avis exists, and the first English date is only approximate; both the root's earlier history and the word's arrival date remain open.
items.cn: 来源不确定：avis 没有公认的前拉丁语重构形式，英语首见年代也只是约数；词根更早的历史与词进入英语的时间都仍无定论。

note.en: Group one separates the look-alike words: two share the Latin root avis, two merely resemble it in spelling. Group two holds the words that overlap with avian in meaning but differ in scope.
note.cn: 第一组区分形近词：两个与 avian 共享拉丁词根 avis，两个只是拼写相像。第二组是含义重叠但范围不同的词。

entries.definition: From Latin aviarium 'bird house', built on avis; it shares the root with avian but names a building rather than a quality.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 aviarium「鸟舍」，由 avis 构成；与 avian 同根，但指的是建筑而非性质。

entries.definition: From French aviation, from Latin avis 'bird'; the root is shared, but the word means a person who flies aircraft.
entries.definitionCN: 来自法语 aviation，再上溯拉丁 avis「鸟」；词根相同，但词义指驾驶飞行器的人。

entries.definition: From Latin avarus 'greedy', from avere 'to crave'; the opening letters match, but there is no link to avis.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 avarus「贪财的」，再上溯 avere「渴求」；开头字母相同，但与 avis 无关。

entries.definition: From Latin avunculus 'maternal uncle'; the resemblance to avian is accidental and the roots are unrelated.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 avunculus「舅父」；与 avian 的相像是偶然的，词根无关。

entries.definition: Resembling a bird; it covers the same ground as the figurative avian but carries no technical tone.
entries.definitionCN: 像鸟的；与比喻义的 avian 覆盖相近范围，但不带技术语体。

entries.definition: Relating to the scientific study of birds; it describes the research, while avian describes the animal.
entries.definitionCN: 与鸟类科学研究有关的；描述的是研究，而 avian 描述的是动物。

entries.definition: Flying or able to fly; it is a functional term about locomotion, not about membership in the bird class.
entries.definitionCN: 飞行的或能飞的；是描述运动方式的功能术语，不涉及是否属于鸟纲。

entries.definition: Of the order Passeriformes, the perching birds; far narrower than avian, which covers every bird.
entries.definitionCN: 属于雀形目的；范围远比 avian 窄，后者覆盖所有鸟。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real zoological phrases and real relatives of the word.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的动物学搭配与真实的同族词。

normal.en: avi- 'bird' + -an: the suffix turns the Latin noun into 'of birds'.
normal.cn: avi-「鸟」+ -an：后缀把拉丁名词变成「鸟的」。

normal.en: Latin avis is the anchor: avi- appears again in avifauna, aviary and aviculture.
normal.cn: 锚点是拉丁 avis：avi- 又出现在 avifauna、aviary 与 aviculture 中。

normal.en: Avian influenza fixes the public-health sense: the pathogen's reservoir is birds.
normal.cn: 禽流感这一固定搭配确立了公共卫生义：病原的宿主是鸟。

normal.en: Mammalian is the same pattern for mammals, which shows how -ian attaches a class name.
normal.cn: 表示哺乳类的形容词用的是同一模式，可见 -ian 如何接在类群名后。

normal.en: The family runs avian, avifauna, aviary, aviculture, aviculturist.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 avian、avifauna、aviary、aviculture、aviculturist。

abstract.en: Picture a museum drawer of study skins, every tag written with one local place name.
abstract.cn: 想象博物馆抽屉里一排鸟皮标本，每张标签都写着一个本地地名。

abstract.en: Picture a poultry shed with a taped line at the gate and white suits beyond it.
abstract.cn: 想象鸡舍门口拉起一道胶带，胶带那侧站着穿白衣的人。

abstract.en: Picture a paper wing folding at the top of a stroke above an empty field.
abstract.cn: 想象一只纸翼在空野上空扑到最高点时折拢。

examples.en: Avian bones are hollow and braced by fine internal struts.
examples.cn: 鸟类的骨骼中空，并有细小的内部支柱加固。

examples.en: The reserve publishes an avian species list every spring.
examples.cn: 保护区每年春天发布一份鸟类物种名录。

examples.en: Avian flu led to a temporary ban on live-bird markets.
examples.cn: 禽流感导致活禽市场被暂时关闭。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「诶维恩」——把开头的「诶维」记成「鸟」，后面的「恩」记成「的」→ 鸟的、鸟类的

root: 拉丁 avis「鸟」（阴性第三变格，属格 avis）+ -an（拉丁 -anus「属于……的」）。avis 更深来源不确定，无公认的前拉丁语重构形式；英语 avian 自 19 世纪科学文献起有记录，确切首见年代存疑。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses start from one plain move: attach the adjective 'of birds' to a noun. That noun may be a disease, a regional list, an organ, a research method, a machine or, rarely, the bird itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都从同一个简单动作出发：把「鸟的」这个形容词接到一个名词上。那个名词可以是疾病、地区名录、器官、研究方法、机器，偶尔也可以是一只鸟本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one notebook that holds a bird's bones, feathers and song at once.
core.cn: 核心意象：一本同时收着鸟的骨骼、羽毛与鸣声的册子。

branches.en: THE CLASS: the adjective of the animal itself, and of the studies that count it.
branches.cn: 类群本身：既是这种动物的形容词，也修饰以它为对象的调查。

branches.en: BORROWED FORM: a silhouette and a wing stroke copied from birds.
branches.cn: 借来的形态：从鸟那里借走的轮廓与一次扑翼。

branches.en: RESERVOIR: the bird is where the pathogen lives, not who falls ill.
branches.cn: 宿主：鸟是病原寄居之处，而不是发病者。

branches.en: LIST AND ORGAN: a regional inventory, and the parts that make flight possible.
branches.cn: 名录与器官：一份地区清单，以及使飞行成为可能的部件。

branches.en: ONE BIRD: the adjective worn down into a count noun in field notes.
branches.cn: 一只鸟：形容词在野外记录里被磨成了一个计数名词。

intro.en: Avian is a two-piece word: a Latin noun for bird and a Latin adjective suffix. Every longer relative repeats that same stem.
intro.cn: avian 是两段式单词：一个表「鸟」的拉丁名词，加一个拉丁形容词后缀。所有更长的同族词都重复这同一词干。

latinIntro.en: Latin avis 'bird' yields aviarius 'of birds' and aviarium 'bird house'; English builds aviary, aviculture and avifauna on the same stem.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 avis「鸟」衍生 aviarius「鸟的」与 aviarium「鸟舍」；英语用同一词干构成 aviary、aviculture 与 avifauna。

items.structure: avis (Latin noun, third declension, genitive avis)
items.example: The stem avi- carries the meaning 'bird' in every relative.
items.exampleCN: 词干 avi- 在所有同族词里都带「鸟」的意思。

items.example: Avian means pertaining to a bird.
items.exampleCN: avian 意为与鸟有关的。

items.example: The avian skeleton is built for lightness.
items.exampleCN: 鸟类的骨骼为轻盈而构造。

items.structure: avi- + fauna (Latin Fauna, a goddess name used for animal life)
items.meaning: the bird fauna of a region
items.example: The island's avifauna includes three endemic warblers.
items.exampleCN: 该岛的鸟类区系包括三种特有柳莺。

items.meaning: relating to a regional bird fauna
items.example: An avifaunal survey was run before the dam was built.
items.exampleCN: 大坝修建前进行了一次鸟类区系调查。

items.meaning: a place where birds are kept
items.example: The aviary holds rescued hawks and owls.
items.exampleCN: 鸟舍里收容着获救的鹰与猫头鹰。

items.meaning: the keeping and breeding of birds
items.example: Aviculture of songbirds has a long history in this region.
items.exampleCN: 这一地区饲养鸣禽的历史悠久。

items.meaning: a person who keeps and breeds birds
items.example: The aviculturist raised the chicks by hand.
items.exampleCN: 养禽者亲手养大了这些雏鸟。

items.meaning: influenza whose pathogen circulates in birds
items.example: Avian influenza is monitored in both poultry and wild birds.
items.exampleCN: 禽流感在家禽与野生鸟中都被监测。

latinEntries.meaning: a place where birds are kept

definition_zh: 引力场；重力场；由质量产生的、对其他质量施加吸引力的空间区域
definition_en: the region of space around a mass in which another mass experiences an attractive force
core_image: 一张网格状的时空示意图，中间压着一颗小球，网格向下凹陷
scene: 天文台里，研究员盯着屏幕上绕月探测器轨迹的弯曲弧线，那弧度正是看不见的力造成的。 The probe's path bent as it crossed the moon's gravitational field.
sceneCN: 这里指卫星周围的引力场（第 4 个义项：行星或卫星质量所产生的引力作用区域）；句意为探测器穿过月球引力场时轨迹发生了弯曲。图中可辨识物件：轨迹屏、弯曲弧线、月球轮廓、控制台。

pos.zh: 名词短语：可数，指某质量周围的引力作用区域；常带表示来源的介词短语

collocations.phrase: the gravitational field of a planet

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁动词加表示「作用、过程」的词尾构成，义为「引力作用」
由本词组的第一成分构成，义为「引力的；重力的」
同一词根的动词，义为「受引力作用；被吸引」
同一词根的名词，义为「重力；严重性」
由本词根加表示「粒子」的词尾构成，指假设中的引力子
由本词根加表示「测量仪器」的成分构成，义为「重力仪」

senses.title: A region of gravitational influence
senses.definition: the region around a mass in which its attraction can be detected by another body
senses.definitionCN: 质量周围能被另一物体检测到其吸引作用的区域
senses.example: A gravitational field is the region around a mass where another mass feels a pull.
senses.exampleCN: 引力场是质量周围另一质量能感到吸引的区域。
senses.why: Physics needed a way to speak about action at a distance without naming a messenger, so it described the space itself.
senses.whyCN: 物理学需要一种不必指明传递者也能谈论超距作用的说法，于是转而描述空间本身。

senses.title: Field strength
senses.definition: the force per unit mass at a point, equal to the local acceleration of a freely falling body
senses.definitionCN: 某点单位质量所受的力，等于自由落体在该处的加速度
senses.example: The gravitational field strength at the surface is about ten newtons per kilogram.
senses.exampleCN: 地表的引力场强度约为每千克十牛顿。
senses.why: Once the field is a quantity, it can be measured, graphed and compared between planets.
senses.whyCN: 一旦场成为可量化的量，就能测量、绘图并在行星之间比较。

senses.title: Earth's field
senses.definition: the field produced by the earth, which defines local vertical and the weight of objects
senses.definitionCN: 地球产生的场，定义当地的竖直方向与物体的重量
senses.example: Satellites stay in orbit because they move through the earth's gravitational field.
senses.exampleCN: 卫星之所以留在轨道上，是因为它们在穿过地球引力场。
senses.why: Everyday weight is the most familiar reading of the field, which is why the concept feels intuitive.
senses.whyCN: 日常的重量就是对这个场最熟悉的读数，因此这一概念显得直观。

senses.title: A planet's or moon's field
senses.definition: the field around a particular body, whose shape reveals how mass is distributed inside it
senses.definitionCN: 围绕某一天体的场，其形状能揭示其内部质量分布
senses.example: The probe mapped the gravitational field of the moon in fine detail.
senses.exampleCN: 探测器精细地测绘了月球的引力场。
senses.why: A field is not a perfect sphere when the body is lumpy, and those bumps become a map of what lies beneath.
senses.whyCN: 当天体质量分布不均时，场并非完美球形，这些起伏便成了地下结构的图。

senses.title: A uniform field
senses.definition: an idealised field whose strength and direction are the same at every point in a region
senses.definitionCN: 在某一区域内各点强度与方向都相同的理想化场
senses.example: Near the floor of the laboratory, the gravitational field is almost uniform.
senses.exampleCN: 在实验室地板附近，引力场几乎是匀强的。
senses.why: Textbooks flatten the field on purpose, because constant acceleration makes the arithmetic simple.
senses.whyCN: 教科书有意把场压平，因为恒定加速度让运算变得简单。

senses.title: Field lines
senses.definition: imaginary curves drawn to show the direction a small test mass would be pulled
senses.definitionCN: 用来表示小试验质量受力方向的假想曲线
senses.example: Field lines of the gravitational field always point toward the mass that creates them.
senses.exampleCN: 引力场线总是指向产生它们的质量。
senses.why: Drawing lines turns an invisible influence into a picture that can be checked by eye.
senses.whyCN: 画出线条，就把看不见的作用变成了可以用眼睛核对的图像。

senses.title: Gravitational potential
senses.definition: the work needed per unit mass to move a body from a reference point to a given point in the field
senses.definitionCN: 在场中把单位质量从参考点移到某点所需的功
senses.example: The gravitational field can also be described by a potential, one number at each point.
senses.exampleCN: 引力场也可以用势来描述，每个点对应一个数值。
senses.why: A single number per point is easier to compute with than a direction and a magnitude, so the field gets a scalar twin.
senses.whyCN: 每点一个数比方向加大小更易计算，于是场有了一个标量孪生描述。

senses.title: Curvature in general relativity
senses.titleCN: 广义相对论中的时空弯曲
senses.definition: the description of gravity as the bending of spacetime by mass and energy rather than as a force in flat space
senses.definitionCN: 把引力描述为质量与能量使时空弯曲，而非平直空间中的一种力
senses.example: In general relativity the gravitational field is the curvature of spacetime itself.
senses.exampleCN: 在广义相对论中，引力场就是时空本身的弯曲。
senses.why: The old field became geometry, which removed the need for a force acting across empty space.
senses.whyCN: 旧的场概念变成了几何，于是不再需要一种跨越真空的力。

senses.title: A sphere of attraction
senses.definition: a figurative area in which a person or organisation draws others toward itself
senses.definitionCN: 比喻意义上，个人或组织把他人吸引过来的范围
senses.example: The young firm had a gravitational field that pulled suppliers into its orbit.
senses.exampleCN: 这家年轻公司拥有引力场般的吸引力，把供应商拉入自己的轨道。
senses.why: Because the concept describes invisible pulling, it transfers easily to markets and reputations.
senses.whyCN: 由于这一概念描述的是看不见的牵引，它很容易被挪用到市场与声誉上。

intro.en: The phrase joins an adjective from Latin gravis, heavy, to an English word for open ground that later became a technical term for a region of influence. The direct sources are clear; the date of the phrase's first technical use is approximate.
intro.cn: 这个短语把一个来自拉丁语「重的」的形容词，与一个原指开阔地的英语词连在一起，后者后来成为指「作用区域」的术语。直接来源清楚，短语首次技术性使用的年代为约数。

items.en: Gravis meant heavy, weighty and, figuratively, serious.
items.cn: 这个词表示「重的、有分量的」，引申为「严重的」。

items.en: The noun named weight and also the dignity of a person who carries weight.
items.cn: 这个名词既指重量，也指有分量者的威严。

items.en: The verb meant to weigh down or to be heavy, and English made it gravitate.
items.cn: 这个动词意为「压重、变重」，英语据其造出表示「被吸引」的动词。

items.en: Newton's physics gave English the noun for the attraction between masses.
items.cn: 牛顿的物理学为英语提供了表示质量间吸引的名词。

items.en: Feld meant open land or a stretch of ground, a word for a bounded expanse.
items.cn: 这个词指开阔地或一片土地，本是一个表示有界延展的词。

items.en: Nineteenth-century physics turned field into a region of force, and the two words combined into one term.
items.cn: 十九世纪的物理学把「场」变成力的作用区域，两个词于是合成一个术语。

note.en: The first group shares the adjective gravitational or the noun field; the second group names other ways of describing attraction.
note.cn: 第一组共享形容词「引力的」或名词「场」；第二组表示描述吸引的其他说法。

entries.definition: The force exerted between two masses.
entries.definitionCN: 两个质量之间施加的力。

entries.definition: A ripple in spacetime produced by accelerating masses.
entries.definitionCN: 加速的质量在时空中产生的涟漪。

entries.definition: A mass that bends light from a distant source.
entries.definitionCN: 使远处光源光线弯曲的质量。

entries.definition: The potential energy per unit mass in a field.
entries.definitionCN: 场中单位质量的势能。

entries.definition: A region in which a force acts on a body.
entries.definitionCN: 力对物体起作用的区域。

entries.definition: A plainer name for the same region of attraction.
entries.definitionCN: 对同一引力区域的更朴素说法。

entries.definition: Any region where a force is defined at every point.
entries.definitionCN: 在任何一点都定义有某种力的区域。

entries.definition: The tendency of bodies to draw toward one another.
entries.definitionCN: 物体相互靠拢的趋势。

entries.definition: A steady force drawing something toward a source.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物拉向来源的持续力。

entries.definition: An area in which one power or person can affect events.
entries.definitionCN: 某一力量或个人能影响事件的区域。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations start from the bent grid and move to strength, maps and relativity; abstract ones treat the field as an invisible shape in space.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想从被压弯的网格出发，走向场强、测绘与相对论；抽象联想把场看作空间中看不见的形状。

normal.en: Put a ball on a stretched sheet and the dip is a gravitational field.
normal.cn: 把球放在绷紧的布上，凹陷就是引力场。

normal.en: A scale reading is your body sensing the local field strength.
normal.cn: 体重秤的读数，就是你的身体在感知当地的场强。

normal.en: Probes map bumps in the field to find mass hidden underground.
normal.cn: 探测器测绘场的起伏，从而找出地下的质量。

normal.en: Field lines always point at the mass that made them.
normal.cn: 场线总是指向产生它们的质量。

normal.en: Einstein replaced the field with the shape of spacetime.
normal.cn: 爱因斯坦用时空的形状取代了场。

abstract.en: A field is a way of saying that space itself remembers where the mass is.
abstract.cn: 场是一种说法：空间本身记得质量在哪里。

abstract.en: Invisible influence becomes real once you can draw its lines.
abstract.cn: 看不见的作用一旦能画出线条，就变得真实。

abstract.en: Anything that pulls has a field, even a reputation.
abstract.cn: 凡能牵引者皆有场，声誉也不例外。

examples.en: The gravitational field near the surface is almost constant.
examples.cn: 地表附近的引力场几乎是恒定的。

examples.en: Instruments measured a weak gravitational field around the small asteroid.
examples.cn: 仪器测得这颗小行星周围有微弱的引力场。

examples.en: Students plotted the gravitational field on a grid of arrows.
examples.cn: 学生们用箭头网格画出了这个引力场。

dict_mnemonic.text: gravitational（引力的）+ field（场）——引力作用的场，就是引力场

root: 由 gravitational 与 field 组合而成。前者源自拉丁语 gravis「重的」，经 gravitas「重量」与 gravitare「使变重」进入英语；后者源自古英语 feld「开阔地、一片土地」。十九世纪物理学把 field 变为「力的作用区域」，两词遂合成术语，确切首见年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses move from the bare definition to strength, the earth, other bodies, idealised cases, lines, potential, curvature and metaphor.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从基本定义出发，依次走向场强、地球、其他天体、理想情形、场线、势、时空弯曲与比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a taut grid with a heavy ball sinking into it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张绷紧的网格，被重球压出凹陷。

branches.en: THE CORE PAIR: the region where a pull exists and the number that measures it.
branches.cn: 核心一对：存在吸引的区域，以及测量它的数值。

branches.en: THE REAL BODIES: the earth's field and the mapped field of another world.
branches.cn: 真实天体：地球的场，以及另一个世界被测绘出的场。

branches.en: THE SIMPLIFIED PICTURE: a uniform field and the lines drawn to show it.
branches.cn: 简化图景：匀强场，以及为显示它而画的场线。

branches.en: THE DEEPER DESCRIPTIONS: a potential at each point, then curvature of spacetime.
branches.cn: 更深描述：每点一个势，随后是时空弯曲。

branches.en: THE TRANSFER: an invisible pull used for markets and reputations.
branches.cn: 迁移用法：把看不见的牵引用到市场与声誉上。

intro.en: The phrase is built from a Latin adjective of weight and an Old English noun of ground, each with its own family.
intro.cn: 这个短语由一个表示重量的拉丁形容词和一个表示土地的英语名词构成，各自都有一族同根词。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies gravis and its noun and verb; Old English supplies feld, which survives as field.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了表示重的形容词及其名词与动词；古英语提供了后来变为 field 的土地名词。

items.example: It is the root of gravity and of grave in the sense of serious.
items.exampleCN: 它是「重力」以及表示「严重的」那个词的根。

items.example: The noun names both physical weight and personal seriousness.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词既指物理重量，也指人的庄重。

items.example: English formed gravitate from this verb.
items.exampleCN: 英语据这个动词造出了表示「受吸引」的动词。

items.example: It turns the verb into the name of the attraction itself.
items.exampleCN: 它把动词变成表示吸引作用本身的名词。

items.example: It turns gravitation into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它把「引力」变成形容词。

items.meaning: open land, a stretch of ground
items.example: The word named a bounded expanse before it named a region of force.
items.exampleCN: 这个词先指有界的延展，后才指力的区域。

items.example: Physics gave the old land word its modern technical sense.
items.exampleCN: 物理学给了这个古老的土地词现代技术含义。

items.example: The suffix marks a particle rather than a region.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾标记粒子而非区域。

definition_zh: 视觉艺术；造型艺术（绘画、雕塑、摄影、设计等）
definition_en: art forms that are primarily seen, such as painting, drawing, sculpture, photography and design
core_image: 一排作品挂在墙上，观众只能靠眼睛进入它们
scene: 展厅把架上绘画与声音装置放进同一空间，逼观众思考界线在哪里。 The exhibition sets visual art beside a sound installation to test where the boundary lies.
sceneCN: 这里 visual art 指「以视觉为媒介的整个艺术类别」（第 1 个义项：统称绘画、雕塑、摄影等门类）；句意为展览把视觉艺术与声音装置并置，测试两者界线。

pos.zh: 视觉艺术（总称，通常不可数；可数时指一件作品或一个门类）

collocations.zh: 视觉艺术（总称，常用复数）

derivatives.zh: visual art + -ist（人）→ 视觉艺术家；从「类别」转到「从业者」
visual art + -s（复数类别）→ 视觉艺术总称；从「一门」转到「多门类集合」
visual artist + -s（复数）→ 视觉艺术家们；仅数量变化

senses.title: The umbrella category
senses.definition: the category of art forms addressed primarily to the eye
senses.definitionCN: 主要以眼睛为对象的艺术门类总称
senses.example: The exhibition sets visual art beside a sound installation.
senses.exampleCN: 展览把视觉艺术与声音装置并置。
senses.why: The phrase names a category by its channel: art that reaches the viewer through sight rather than sound, text or performance.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语按接收通道命名类别：通过视觉而非声音、文字或表演抵达观众的艺术。

senses.title: A particular work in these forms
senses.definition: one work belonging to the visual arts
senses.definitionCN: 属于视觉艺术门类的一件作品
senses.example: The museum acquired a major visual art from the estate.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆从遗产中购得一件重要的视觉艺术作品。
senses.why: A category name can be used countably for its members, so one painting or photograph can be called a visual art.
senses.whyCN: 类别名称可以可数地用于其成员，因此一幅画或一张照片可以被称为 a visual art。

senses.title: The practice of making it
senses.definition: the activity or practice of making visual art
senses.definitionCN: 创作视觉艺术的活动或实践
senses.example: She works in visual art rather than in theatre.
senses.exampleCN: 她从事视觉艺术，而不是戏剧。
senses.why: The name of a product category also names the labour that produces it, as with 'painting' and 'sculpture'.
senses.whyCN: 产品类别的名称也命名生产它的劳动，正如 painting 与 sculpture 那样。

senses.title: The field as a profession
senses.titleCN: 作为职业领域的视觉艺术
senses.definition: the professional world of galleries, commissions and funding for visual art
senses.definitionCN: 由画廊、委托与资助构成的视觉艺术职业世界
senses.example: She has worked in visual art for twenty years.
senses.exampleCN: 她在视觉艺术行业工作了二十年。
senses.why: An art world is a set of institutions, so the phrase can name the field as a career rather than a medium.
senses.whyCN: 艺术世界是一组机构，因此这个短语能指作为职业的领域，而非媒介。

senses.title: A school subject
senses.titleCN: 学校课程中的视觉艺术
senses.definition: the subject taught in schools under this name
senses.definitionCN: 学校以该名称教授的科目
senses.example: Visual art is timetabled twice a week.
senses.exampleCN: 视觉艺术每周排两次课。
senses.why: Curricula turn fields into subjects, so the phrase can mean the classroom slot rather than the whole art world.
senses.whyCN: 课程表把领域变成科目，因此这个短语能指课堂位置，而非整个艺术界。

senses.title: The contrast with performing arts
senses.titleCN: 与表演艺术相对的门类
senses.definition: the category defined by contrast with music, dance and theatre
senses.definitionCN: 通过与音乐、舞蹈、戏剧对照而界定的类别
senses.example: Funding divides visual art from performing art.
senses.exampleCN: 资助体系把视觉艺术与表演艺术分开。
senses.why: Categories are often made by contrast: what is not performed live for an audience is grouped as visual.
senses.whyCN: 类别常通过对照建立：不在现场为观众表演的，就被归为视觉艺术。

senses.title: A market category
senses.definition: the grouping used by dealers, auctions and collectors
senses.definitionCN: 画商、拍卖与收藏界使用的分类
senses.example: Visual art sales rose while print sales fell.
senses.exampleCN: 视觉艺术销售额上升，版画销售额下降。
senses.why: Markets need sortable labels, so the phrase becomes a sales category covering objects that can be owned and hung.
senses.whyCN: 市场需要可分类的标签，因此这个短语成为销售类别，涵盖可以拥有与悬挂的物件。

senses.title: An academic field
senses.definition: the field of study and degree programmes devoted to visual art
senses.definitionCN: 以视觉艺术为对象的研究领域与学位项目
senses.example: The university offers a degree in visual art.
senses.exampleCN: 这所大学提供视觉艺术学位。
senses.why: When a practice enters universities, its name also names the department and the degree, a familiar institutional shift.
senses.whyCN: 当一种实践进入大学，其名称也命名院系与学位，这是常见的机构化转移。

intro.en: Visual art joins a Late Latin adjective of sight to a Latin noun for skill; the compound is modern, though both parts are old. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: visual art 把晚期拉丁的「视觉」形容词与拉丁的「技艺」名词结合；两部分都古老，复合词却是现代产物。年代均为约数。

items.en: Videre 'to see' gives the participle visus and the Late Latin adjective visualis 'of sight'.
items.cn: videre「看见」给出分词 visus 与晚期拉丁形容词 visualis「视觉的」。

items.en: Ars, artis meant practical skill or craft; the modern category of the fine arts grew from this word in the Renaissance and after.
items.cn: ars、artis 意为实用技艺或手艺；现代「美术」类别在文艺复兴及以后从这个词生长出来。

items.en: English art is recorded from the thirteenth century and visual from the fifteenth; the two words long led separate lives.
items.cn: 英语 art 自 13 世纪有记录，visual 自 15 世纪有记录；两词长期各自发展。

items.en: In the nineteenth and twentieth centuries museums, schools and funding agencies grouped painting, sculpture, printmaking, photography and design as the visual arts.
items.cn: 到 19 与 20 世纪，博物馆、学校与资助机构把绘画、雕塑、版画、摄影与设计归为视觉艺术。

items.en: The plural visual arts became standard in arts education and public funding, and the singular visual art followed as a subject name.
items.cn: 复数 visual arts 在艺术教育与公共资助中成为标准说法，单数 visual art 随后成为科目名称。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the compound has no agreed first citation, and its boundary with fine art or design is still argued.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：这个复合词没有公认的最早书证，它与美术或设计的界线至今仍有争论。

note.en: Group one separates the singular, plural and personal forms that are often mixed up; group two separates visual art from categories that overlap but answer a different question.
note.cn: 第一组把常被混用的单数、复数与指人形式分开；第二组把视觉艺术与有重叠但回答不同问题的类别分开。

entries.definition: The standard collective name for the group of disciplines; the singular often names a subject or one work.
entries.definitionCN: 该组门类的标准总称；单数常指一个科目或一件作品。

entries.definition: A practitioner in the visual arts; the phrase names a person, not a category.
entries.definitionCN: 视觉艺术的从业者；这个短语指人，而非类别。

entries.definition: The study of all visual media, including advertising and scientific images; visual art keeps the art category.
entries.definitionCN: 研究一切视觉媒介，包括广告与科学图像；visual art 保留艺术类别。

entries.definition: The arrangement of graphics for communication; it may be taught beside visual art but serves a client's purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 为传达而安排图形；可能与视觉艺术同教，但服务客户目的。

entries.definition: Art valued for beauty and expression, especially painting and sculpture; visual art is the wider, medium-based category.
entries.definitionCN: 因美与表达而被珍视的艺术，尤指绘画与雕塑；visual art 是更广的、按媒介划分的类别。

entries.definition: Arts that shape material into three-dimensional form, such as sculpture and ceramics; visual art also covers flat images.
entries.definitionCN: 把材料塑成立体形式的艺术，如雕塑与陶艺；visual art 也包含平面图像。

entries.definition: Art made for a practical function, such as furniture or typography; visual art does not decide by function.
entries.definitionCN: 为实用功能而作的艺术，如家具或字体设计；visual art 不以功能来划分。

entries.definition: Art presented live before an audience, such as dance or theatre; it is the usual contrast term.
entries.definitionCN: 在观众面前现场呈现的艺术，如舞蹈或戏剧；是常用的对照词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real compounds and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: visual + art: art that reaches you through the eye.
normal.cn: visual + art：通过眼睛抵达你的艺术。

normal.en: The plural visual arts is the standard collective name in schools and funding.
normal.cn: 复数 visual arts 是学校与资助体系中的标准总称。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: visual art practice, visual art education, a degree in visual art.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：视觉艺术实践、视觉艺术教育、视觉艺术学位。

normal.en: The family runs visual, visual arts, visual artist and visual culture.
normal.cn: 同族说法包括 visual、visual arts、visual artist 与 visual culture。

normal.en: The category is defined by contrast with performing art, not by one medium.
normal.cn: 这个类别靠与表演艺术对照来界定，而不是靠单一媒介。

abstract.en: Picture a wall that lets only eyes through.
abstract.cn: 想象一面只放眼睛通过的墙。

abstract.en: Picture a room where sound is the exception and sight the rule.
abstract.cn: 想象一个以视觉为常规、声音为例外的房间。

abstract.en: Picture a label broad enough to hold a drawing, a photograph and a building.
abstract.cn: 想象一个宽到能装下素描、照片与建筑的标签。

examples.en: Visual art and music share a gallery but not a budget line.
examples.cn: 视觉艺术与音乐共用展厅，却不在同一预算科目下。

examples.en: The course treats visual art as a way of thinking, not only of making.
examples.cn: 这门课把视觉艺术当作一种思考方式，而不只是制作方式。

examples.en: Photography's place in visual art was settled only in the twentieth century.
examples.cn: 摄影在视觉艺术中的位置到 20 世纪才被确定。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「visual（视觉的）+ art（艺术）」——给眼睛看的艺术 → 视觉艺术

root: visual 来自拉丁 videre「看见」的分词 visus 与晚期拉丁 visualis；art 来自拉丁 ars（属格 artis）「技艺」。二者合成现代英语复合词 visual art，19 至 20 世纪成为机构类别。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses distinguish the category from one work, the practice, the profession, the school subject, the contrast with performance, the market and the academic field.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把类别与单件作品、创作实践、职业、学校科目、与表演的对照、市场及学术领域区分开。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of works hangs on a wall, and viewers can enter them only through the eye.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排作品挂在墙上，观众只能靠眼睛进入它们。

branches.en: THE CATEGORY AND ITS EDGE: the umbrella term, then the contrast that defines it.
branches.cn: 类别及其边界：总称，然后是界定它的对照。

branches.en: ONE WORK: the category used countably for a single piece.
branches.cn: 单件作品：类别被可数地用于一件作品。

branches.en: THE PRACTICE: the labour behind the category.
branches.cn: 实践：类别背后的劳动。

branches.en: PROFESSION AND MARKET: the field as a career, then as a sales category.
branches.cn: 职业与市场：领域作为职业，再作为销售类别。

branches.en: SCHOOL AND UNIVERSITY: the subject in a timetable, then the degree and department.
branches.cn: 中小学与大学：课表上的科目，再是学位与院系。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Latin-derived adjective of sight to a Latin-derived noun of skill, and each half keeps its own family.
intro.cn: 这个短语把拉丁来源的「视觉」形容词与拉丁来源的「技艺」名词结合，两半各保留自己的词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin videre supplies visual through visus and visualis; Latin ars supplies art. The compound itself is modern English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 videre 经 visus 与 visualis 提供 visual；拉丁 ars 提供 art。复合词本身是现代英语的产物。

items.example: Visual marks the channel.
items.exampleCN: visual 标记接收通道。

items.example: Art marks the category.
items.exampleCN: art 标记类别。

items.example: The museum collects visual art of the last century.
items.exampleCN: 博物馆收藏上一个世纪的视觉艺术。

items.meaningCN: 各视觉艺术门类的总称
items.example: The faculty of visual arts has four departments.
items.exampleCN: 视觉艺术学院有四个系。

items.meaning: a maker in the visual arts
items.example: The visual artist works in video and clay.
items.exampleCN: 这位视觉艺术家用录像与黏土创作。

items.example: The artist signed the print.
items.exampleCN: 艺术家在版画上签了名。

items.example: The suffix turns a field into a person.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把领域变成人。

items.example: The software visualizes the plan.
items.exampleCN: 这款软件把方案可视化。

definition_zh: 林地；树木覆盖的土地；（英）成片小树林；疏林
definition_en: land covered with trees, usually smaller or more open than a full forest
core_image: 一片不过几百步宽的榛树林，林下有风信子，林外就是麦田，树冠把两种土地分开
scene: 五月初，这片矮林刚被砍过一茬，林下开满风信子，是庄园里物种最丰富的生境之一。 In early May the hazel coppice and bluebells make this woodland one of the richest habitats on the estate.
sceneCN: 这里 woodland 指「树木覆盖的成片土地」（第 1 个义项：以树木为主的陆地区域）；句意为五月初这茬矮林与风信子使这片林地成为庄园里最丰富的生境之一。图中可辨识物件：榛树萌条、风信子花丛、林缘麦田、林下落叶层。

pos.zh: 林地；小树林；疏林（可数或不可数）
林地的；林栖的（多作定语）

collocations.zh: 古老林地（长期连续有林）

derivatives.zh: 林居者；林地居民（较少用）

senses.title: Land covered with trees
senses.definition: an area of land whose main cover is trees, generally smaller than a forest and often bounded by fields
senses.definitionCN: 以树木为主要覆盖的陆地区域，通常比森林小，常与农田相接
senses.example: A narrow woodland separates the village from the highway.
senses.exampleCN: 一片狭长林地把村庄与公路隔开。
senses.why: woodland is literally 'wood-land', a compound that names land by what grows on it rather than by ownership or size.
senses.whyCN: woodland 字面就是「长树的土地」，这个复合词按地表长什么来命名，而不按所有权或面积。

senses.title: A managed wood in Britain
senses.definition: a small wood that is actively managed, often by coppicing or thinning, as a land-use category
senses.definitionCN: 经积极经营的小片树林，常行矮林作业或疏伐，作为土地用途类别
senses.example: The trust owns forty hectares of woodland under a coppice rotation.
senses.exampleCN: 该信托拥有四十公顷按矮林轮伐经营的林地。
senses.why: British land-use vocabulary separates woodland from forest, because a forest there is often a large open hunting area rather than a closed wood.
senses.whyCN: 英国土地用途术语把 woodland 与 forest 分开，因为那里的 forest 常指大片开阔猎场，而非密闭树林。

senses.title: Open woodland with scattered canopy
senses.definition: a tree community whose crowns do not close, so that grass or heath grows between the trunks
senses.definitionCN: 树冠不闭合的树木群落，树干之间长着草或灌丛
senses.example: Open woodland lets light reach the grass layer all summer.
senses.exampleCN: 疏林让阳光整个夏天都能照到草层。
senses.why: ecology uses woodland as a structural term, and the open type sits between grassland and closed forest.
senses.whyCN: 生态学把 woodland 当作结构术语，疏林型正好位于草地与密闭森林之间。

senses.title: Habitat with layered vegetation
senses.titleCN: 具有垂直层次的林地生境
senses.definition: a habitat whose canopy, shrub layer and litter support distinct groups of animals and plants
senses.definitionCN: 由树冠层、灌木层与落叶层构成、供养不同动植物类群的生境
senses.example: The woodland shelters warblers in the canopy and beetles in the litter.
senses.exampleCN: 这片林地为树冠层的莺与落叶层的甲虫提供庇护。
senses.why: once woodland is seen as a place rather than a crop, it becomes a habitat whose value lies in its layers.
senses.whyCN: 当 woodland 被视为一个地方而非作物，它就成了生境，其价值在于层次。

senses.title: Ancient woodland with long continuity
senses.titleCN: 长期连续有林的古老林地
senses.definition: woodland that has been continuously wooded since at least 1600, and so preserves old soil and plant communities
senses.definitionCN: 至少自 1600 年起持续有林、因而保存古老土壤与植物群落的林地
senses.example: Ancient woodland indicators such as wild garlic cover the slope.
senses.exampleCN: 野蒜等古老林地指示植物覆盖着这片坡地。
senses.why: continuity, not age of individual trees, defines the type: a wood can be cut many times and still be ancient.
senses.whyCN: 定义这个类型的是连续性而非单株树龄：一片林子可被反复采伐，仍算古老林地。

senses.title: Woodland edge as a transition
senses.definition: the boundary zone where woodland meets field or clearing, richer in light and in species than either side
senses.definitionCN: 林地与田野或空地相接的边界带，光照与物种都比两侧更丰富
senses.example: Butterflies concentrate along the sunny woodland edge.
senses.exampleCN: 蝴蝶聚集在向阳的林缘。
senses.why: the compound's 'land' part becomes visible here: woodland is a patch with a boundary, and the boundary is itself a habitat.
senses.whyCN: 这里显出复合词中 land 的一面：林地是有边界的地块，而边界本身也是生境。

senses.title: Newly created woodland
senses.definition: trees planted on former farmland or bare ground with the declared aim of forming woodland
senses.definitionCN: 在退耕地或裸地上植树，目标明确为形成林地
senses.example: Woodland creation on the upper fields has doubled tree cover in ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 在上部农田新造林地，使树木覆盖在十年内翻倍。
senses.why: the word can look forward as well as backward: land becomes woodland at the moment the planting scheme is registered.
senses.whyCN: 这个词也能朝前看：当造林方案登记之时，那块地就被算作林地。

senses.title: Woodland as a source of woodfuel
senses.definition: woodland valued for the regular supply of logs, poles and charcoal it yields under a cutting cycle
senses.definitionCN: 因按采伐周期稳定产出原木、杆材与木炭而受重视的林地
senses.example: The woodland heats three cottages from a single winter cut.
senses.exampleCN: 这片林地一次冬季采伐就能供三座农舍取暖。
senses.why: the oldest use of a wood was to be cut on rotation, and this productive reading still attaches to woodland in rural economies.
senses.whyCN: 树林最古老的用途就是轮期采伐，这一生产性含义在乡村经济中仍附着于 woodland。

intro.en: Woodland is a native English compound of wood and land, both Old English words of Germanic origin, so it has no Latin ancestor.
intro.cn: woodland 是 wood 与 land 构成的英语本族复合词，两者都是日耳曼来源的古英语词，因此没有拉丁语祖先。

items.en: Wudu meant 'wood, tree, forest'. Its Germanic source is usually reconstructed as *widuz, but the further Indo-European connections are not settled.
items.cn: wudu 意为「木材、树、森林」。其日耳曼来源通常重构为 *widuz，更远的印欧语联系尚无定论。

items.en: Land meant 'ground, soil, territory'. Germanic *landam is reconstructed, but its pre-Germanic origin is uncertain.
items.cn: land 意为「地面、土壤、领土」。日耳曼语 *landam 属重构形式，其在日耳曼语之前的来源不确定。

items.en: The compound is recorded in Middle English, naming ground grown with trees rather than the trees themselves.
items.cn: 这个复合词见于中古英语，指长着树木的地面，而非树木本身。

items.en: Modern forestry fixed woodland as a category distinct from forest, especially in Britain, where forest often names an old royal hunting area.
items.cn: 现代林业把 woodland 固定为与 forest 不同的类别，在英国尤其如此，因为那里的 forest 常指旧日王室猎场。

items.en: Source uncertain: the first date of the compound is not precisely recorded, and the deeper roots of both wudu and land are reconstructions rather than attested forms.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这个复合词的最早年代没有精确书证；wudu 与 land 的更深词根均属重构，并非有文献的形式。

note.en: Group one separates the wood-words by size and management; group two gives true synonyms for a stand of trees.
note.cn: 第一组按面积与经营方式区分几个 wood 系词；第二组是「一片树林」的真正近义词。

entries.definition: A small area of trees, or the material cut from them; in British English a wood is typically smaller than a woodland.
entries.definitionCN: 小片树林，或由其砍出的木材；英式英语中 wood 通常比 woodland 更小。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning 'covered with trees', used of hills or land, not a noun for the place itself.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，意为「树木覆盖的」，用于山丘或土地，不是地点名词。

entries.definition: A North American term for a small privately owned stand of trees managed for fuel and fence posts.
entries.definitionCN: 北美用语，指私有小片树林，经营薪材与篱柱。

entries.definition: A larger, denser or legally designated wooded area; historically a royal hunting ground, which is why British usage differs.
entries.definitionCN: 更大、更密或依法划定的林区；历史上指王室猎场，这正是英式用法差异的由来。

entries.definition: A small group of trees, often of one kind and often in open ground; it stresses cluster, not area.
entries.definitionCN: 一小群树，常为同一树种，多生于开阔地；强调成簇，不强调面积。

entries.definition: A small wood grown for periodic cutting, from Old French copeiz; it names a working wood rather than any tree-covered land.
entries.definitionCN: 为定期采伐而育的小树林，来自古法语 copeiz；指作业林，而非任意林地。

entries.definition: Australian land dominated by shrubs and scattered trees; the cover is lower and drier than woodland.
entries.definitionCN: 澳洲以灌木与散生树为主的土地；覆盖比林地更低更干。

entries.definition: Forest land valued for the timber it can yield; it is an economic label, not an ecological one.
entries.definitionCN: 以可产木材为价值的林地；是经济标签，不是生态分类。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: wood + land: land whose crop is trees.
normal.cn: wood + land：以树为作物的土地。

normal.en: The family runs wood, wooded, woody, woodlot, woodland.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 wood、wooded、woody、woodlot、woodland。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: ancient woodland, open woodland, woodland edge, woodland creation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：古老林地、疏林、林缘、新造林地。

normal.en: British usage keeps woodland smaller than forest; American usage often treats them alike.
normal.cn: 英式用法中 woodland 比 forest 小；美式用法常不加区分。

normal.en: The image is a narrow wood with a field on one side and a road on the other.
normal.cn: 意象是一片窄林，一边是麦田，一边是公路。

abstract.en: Think of a green room whose walls are trunks and whose ceiling is leaves.
abstract.cn: 想象一间绿色的屋子，墙是树干，顶是叶子。

abstract.en: Think of a shadow that stays in one place while the fields around it are cut and sown.
abstract.cn: 想象一片停在原处的阴影，周围的田地不断被收割与播种。

abstract.en: Think of a bookshelf with three shelves: canopy, shrub, litter.
abstract.cn: 想象一个三层书架：树冠层、灌木层、落叶层。

examples.en: The path runs through a hazel woodland that is cut every seventh winter.
examples.cn: 小路穿过一片每七个冬季采伐一次的榛树林。

examples.en: Ancient woodland soils store carbon that a new plantation cannot quickly replace.
examples.cn: 古老林地的土壤储存着新人工林无法迅速替代的碳。

examples.en: Woodland birds declined after the hedges were removed.
examples.cn: 树篱被清除后，林栖鸟类减少了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「wood（木头/树林）+ land（土地）」——长满树的土地 → 林地

root: 古英语 wudu「木材、树、森林」+ land「土地、地面」。二者均属日耳曼语来源（*widuz、*landam 为重构形式），更深词源不确定；无拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the plain fact of trees on land to the many ways such land is managed, measured, inhabited and cut.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从「土地上有树」这一朴素事实，走向这类土地被经营、计量、栖息与采伐的各种方式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bounded patch of trees with fields pressing against its edge.
core.cn: 核心意象：一片有边界的树地，田地紧贴着它的边缘。

branches.en: THE PATCH: first a piece of land with trees, then a piece someone actually works.
branches.cn: 地块：先是有树的一片地，再是有人实际经营的一片地。

branches.en: LIGHT: when crowns fail to close, grass enters and the type becomes open woodland.
branches.cn: 光：树冠不闭合时草层进入，类型就成了疏林。

branches.en: LAYERS AND BORDER: habitat value sits in canopy, shrub and litter, and peaks at the sunny edge.
branches.cn: 层次与边界：生境价值在树冠、灌木与落叶层中，并在向阳林缘达到高峰。

branches.en: TIME: a wood can be cut again and again and still be ancient if the ground never cleared.
branches.cn: 时间：只要地面未被彻底清除，林子可反复采伐，仍属古老林地。

branches.en: FUTURE AND YIELD: land can be made woodland, and woodland can be made fuel.
branches.cn: 未来与产出：土地可被造成林地，林地也可被变成燃料。

intro.en: Woodland is a native compound, so its parts are two free English words rather than a prefix and a root.
intro.cn: woodland 是本族复合词，其组成部分是两个独立的英语单词，而不是前缀加词根。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin element in woodland; both halves are Germanic, so the Latin entry list is left empty rather than filled with invented relatives.
latinIntro.cn: woodland 中没有拉丁成分；两半都属日耳曼语，因此拉丁词条留空，而不编造同族词。

items.example: The old wood was cut for charcoal.
items.exampleCN: 那片老树林被砍去烧炭。

items.example: The land east of the stream is wet all year.
items.exampleCN: 溪流以东的土地终年潮湿。

items.example: The woodland stops at the fence.
items.exampleCN: 林地在栅栏处止住。

items.example: A wooded ridge hides the quarry.
items.exampleCN: 一道长满树的岭遮住了采石场。

items.example: Woody stems survive the winter above ground.
items.exampleCN: 木质茎能在地面上越冬。

items.meaning: a small private stand of trees
items.example: He cuts one row of his woodlot each year.
items.exampleCN: 他每年在自己那片小树林里砍一行。

items.meaning: one who lives in or works a wood
items.example: The woodlander knows which oaks are ready.
items.exampleCN: 林居者知道哪些栎树可以采了。

items.meaning: of or belonging to a wood
items.example: Woodland birds need the shrub layer.
items.exampleCN: 林栖鸟类需要灌木层。

definition_zh: 生物圈；生命层；全球生命支持系统
definition_en: the zone of Earth, including land, water and air, in which living things exist
core_image: 一颗裹着薄薄绿色生命膜的蓝色星球，那层膜比苹果皮还薄
scene: 地球表面那层薄薄的活体，决定了我们呼吸的空气。 The biosphere is a thin skin on the planet, yet it controls the air we breathe.
sceneCN: 这里 biosphere 指「生物圈」（第 1 个义项：地球上生命存在的整体区域）；句意：生物圈只是这颗行星上薄薄的一层，却控制着我们呼吸的空气。图中可辨识物件：地球剖面、绿色生命层、大气薄层标注。

pos.zh: 生物圈；生命层；全球生命支持系统（通常作单数，带定冠词 the biosphere；也可指其他行星的生命圈）

derivatives.zh: 生物区系；一个地区的全部生物

senses.title: The Living Zone of Earth
senses.titleCN: 生物圈：地球上生命存在的整体区域
senses.definition: the zone of Earth where living things exist, including land, water and air
senses.definitionCN: 地球上生命存在的区域，包括陆地、水与空气
senses.example: The biosphere is a thin skin on the planet, yet it controls the air we breathe.
senses.exampleCN: 生物圈只是这颗行星上薄薄的一层，却控制着我们呼吸的空气。
senses.why: Greek bios 'life' plus sphaira 'ball' gives 'the life-ball'. The word treats all living things together as one layer of the planet, not as a list of species.
senses.whyCN: 希腊 bios「生命」加 sphaira「球」构成「生命之球」。这个词把所有生物合起来当作行星的一层，而不是一张物种清单。

senses.title: Life on Another World
senses.definition: the living layer of any planet, real or imagined
senses.definitionCN: 任何行星上真实或想象的生命层
senses.example: A Mars biosphere, if it ever existed, may survive only underground.
senses.exampleCN: 火星生物圈若曾存在，可能只幸存于地下。
senses.why: Once the word means a layer rather than a place, it can be detached from Earth. Planetary science uses it for the total living system of any world.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词指「一层」而不是「一个地方」，它就能与地球脱离；行星科学用它指任何世界的整体生命系统。

senses.title: The Ecological Layer
senses.definition: the living layer studied as part of the Earth system
senses.definitionCN: 作为地球系统一部分来研究的生命层
senses.example: Ecologists model the biosphere as one component of the Earth system.
senses.exampleCN: 生态学家把生物圈建模为地球系统的一个组分。
senses.why: Earth-system science splits the planet into spheres: atmosphere, hydrosphere, lithosphere and biosphere. The word then names one box in a diagram of interacting boxes.
senses.whyCN: 地球系统科学把行星分成若干圈：大气圈、水圈、岩石圈与生物圈；此时这个词命名的是相互作用框图里的一个方框。

senses.title: A Sealed Living System
senses.titleCN: 封闭生物圈：人工封闭生态系统
senses.definition: a closed experimental system that contains living things and recycles its materials
senses.definitionCN: 包含生物并循环其物质的人工封闭系统
senses.example: The sealed biosphere lasted only two years.
senses.exampleCN: 那个封闭生物圈只维持了两年。
senses.why: Experiments such as Biosphere 2 borrowed the name for a sealed miniature world. The test is whether life can keep its own conditions without outside help.
senses.whyCN: 生物圈二号一类实验借用了这个名字，指封闭的微型世界；它检验的是生命能否在没有外界帮助的情况下维持自身条件。

senses.title: Life as a Planetary Component
senses.titleCN: 作为行星组分的生命总体
senses.definition: the total living component of a planet, considered as one system
senses.definitionCN: 一颗行星的全部生命组分，被视为一个系统
senses.example: The biosphere and the atmosphere exchange carbon every second.
senses.exampleCN: 生物圈与大气每时每刻都在交换碳。
senses.why: Here the emphasis is on exchange: life is not only inside the environment but helps make it. This sense underlies the idea that life regulates the planet's chemistry.
senses.whyCN: 这里强调交换：生命不只在环境之中，还参与制造环境。这一义项支撑了「生命调节行星化学」的观点。

senses.title: Total Living Support
senses.definition: the whole system that keeps conditions suitable for life
senses.definitionCN: 维持适宜生命条件的整个系统
senses.example: Protecting the biosphere is not the same as protecting a few species.
senses.exampleCN: 保护生物圈并不等于保护少数几个物种。
senses.why: Policy language uses the word for the life-support system as a whole. The shift is from a place to a function: the biosphere is what keeps conditions livable.
senses.whyCN: 政策语言用这个词指整个生命支持系统；重心从「地点」转向「功能」：生物圈是维持条件宜居的那套东西。

senses.title: A Reserve for Life
senses.titleCN: 生物圈保护区：受保护的样板区
senses.definition: an area designated to protect ecosystems and to study them
senses.definitionCN: 为保护并研究生态系统而划定的区域
senses.example: The valley was named a biosphere reserve in 1998.
senses.exampleCN: 该山谷于 1998 年被列为生物圈保护区。
senses.why: International programmes turned the abstract noun into a label on a map. A biosphere reserve is not the whole biosphere but a local sample of it, managed for both use and study.
senses.whyCN: 国际计划把这个抽象名词变成地图上的标记；生物圈保护区不是整个生物圈，而是它的一个地方样本，兼顾利用与研究。

senses.title: The Object of a Science
senses.titleCN: 作为研究对象的全球生态系
senses.definition: the global ecosystem taken as the object of a scientific field
senses.definitionCN: 作为某一科学领域研究对象的全球生态系统
senses.example: Biosphere science connects biology with climate and chemistry.
senses.exampleCN: 生物圈科学把生物学与气候、化学联系起来。
senses.why: A name for a layer can become the name of a field. The word then appears in course titles and journal names, where it marks a scale rather than a single object.
senses.whyCN: 一个圈层的名称可以变成一个领域的名称；此时该词出现在课程名与期刊名里，标出的是一个尺度，而不是单一对象。

intro.en: Biosphere joins Greek bios 'life' and sphaira 'ball, sphere'. It was coined by the geologist Eduard Suess in 1875 and later popularized by Vladimir Vernadsky.
intro.cn: biosphere 由希腊 bios「生命」与 sphaira「球、球体」组成。该词由地质学家 Eduard Suess 于 1875 年造出，后由 Vladimir Vernadsky 推广。

items.en: Bios meant 'life, mode of life'. It appears in biology, biography, biota and antibiotic, though the compound meanings differ in each.
items.cn: bios 意为「生命、生活方式」，出现在 biology、biography、biota、antibiotic 中，但各复合词的含义并不相同。

items.en: Sphaira meant 'ball, globe'. Latin took it as sphaera, and English gets sphere, spherical and the -sphere of atmosphere and hydrosphere.
items.cn: sphaira 意为「球、球体」。拉丁语借作 sphaera，英语由此得到 sphere、spherical，以及 atmosphere、hydrosphere 中的 -sphere。

items.en: Eduard Suess coined Biosphere in 1875 to name the layer of Earth in which life occurs. His word treated life as a stratum comparable to rock or water, a geological rather than a poetic idea.
items.cn: Eduard Suess 于 1875 年造出 Biosphere，用来指地球上生命出现的那一层。他的词把生命视为可与岩石或水相提并论的层，这是一个地质学观念，而非诗意比喻。

items.en: Vladimir Vernadsky developed the concept in the early twentieth century, arguing that life actively shapes the planet's chemistry. His work made the word common in ecology.
items.cn: Vladimir Vernadsky 在二十世纪初发展了这一概念，主张生命主动塑造行星的化学；他的工作使该词在生态学中通行。

items.en: UNESCO's biosphere reserve programme and Earth-system science gave the word a policy and a modelling life. It now names a layer, a global system and a protected area at once.
items.cn: 联合国教科文组织的生物圈保护区计划与地球系统科学赋予该词政策与建模上的生命；如今它同时指一个圈层、一个全球系统与一片保护区。

note.en: The first group separates the neighboring sphere terms and the smaller ecological units. The second holds near-synonyms that name life at global scale.
note.cn: 第一组区分相邻的圈层术语与更小的生态单位；第二组是命名全球尺度生命的近义词。

entries.definition: A large ecological region defined by climate and vegetation, such as a rainforest. The biosphere is the sum of all biomes.
entries.definitionCN: 由气候与植被界定的大尺度生态区域，如雨林；生物圈是所有生物群系的总和。

entries.definition: A community of organisms together with its physical environment. It can be as small as a pond and need not be global.
entries.definitionCN: 生物群落与其物理环境的整体；可以小到一个池塘，不必是全球尺度。

entries.definition: The place where a particular species lives. It is species-specific, while the biosphere is the total living zone.
entries.definitionCN: 某一特定物种生活的地方；它针对物种，而生物圈是全部生命所在的区域。

entries.definition: The gaseous envelope of a planet. It is one of the spheres that exchange matter with the biosphere.
entries.definitionCN: 行星的气体包层；它是与生物圈交换物质的圈层之一。

entries.definition: The global system of life together with its environment. It overlaps with biosphere but stresses the system rather than the layer.
entries.definitionCN: 全球生命与其环境的整体系统；与 biosphere 重叠，但强调系统而非圈层。

entries.definition: All the living things of a region or of Earth. It names the organisms, not the zone they occupy.
entries.definitionCN: 一个地区或地球上的全部生物；它命名生物本身，而不是它们占据的区域。

entries.definition: The Earth or a realm of activity. It is far vaguer than biosphere, which is a defined layer of the planet.
entries.definitionCN: 地球或某个活动领域；比 biosphere 模糊得多，后者是行星上一个被界定的圈层。

entries.definition: The conditions surrounding an organism. It can exclude the organisms themselves, unlike biosphere.
entries.definitionCN: 围绕生物的条件；与 biosphere 不同，它可以把生物本身排除在外。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: bio- 'life' + sphere 'ball': the layer of life on the ball of Earth.
normal.cn: bio-「生命」+ sphere「球」：地球这个球上的生命之层。

normal.en: The family runs biology, biota, biome, biosphere, biospheric, antibiotic, biography.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 biology、biota、biome、biosphere、biospheric、antibiotic、biography。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the use: biosphere reserve, biosphere integrity, terrestrial biosphere, marine biosphere.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：生物圈保护区、生物圈完整性、陆地生物圈、海洋生物圈。

normal.en: The spheres run atmosphere, hydrosphere, lithosphere and biosphere.
normal.cn: 各圈层为：大气圈、水圈、岩石圈、生物圈。

normal.en: The biosphere is the whole; a biome is one large region inside it.
normal.cn: 生物圈是整体，生物群系是其中一个大的区域。

abstract.en: Picture a blue marble with a green film so thin that a fingernail could scrape it off.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗蓝色弹珠，上面覆着一层薄到指甲就能刮掉的绿膜。

abstract.en: Picture a sealed glass ball where the plants must remake the air for the animals.
abstract.cn: 想象一只密封玻璃球，里面的植物必须为动物重新制造空气。

abstract.en: Picture a planet where the rocks breathe because the living layer taught them to.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗岩石也会呼吸的行星，因为生命层教会了它。

examples.en: Carbon moves between the biosphere and the atmosphere constantly.
examples.cn: 碳在生物圈与大气之间不断移动。

examples.en: The biosphere reserve protects both the forest and the village inside it.
examples.cn: 生物圈保护区既保护森林，也保护其中的村庄。

examples.en: No sealed biosphere has yet supported people for many years.
examples.cn: 至今还没有封闭生物圈能多年维持人的生活。

dict_mnemonic.text: bio（生命）+ sphere（球、圈）→ 生命之球 → 生物圈

root: 希腊 bios「生命」+ sphaira「球、球体」→ 1875 年 Eduard Suess 造 Biosphere → 英语 biosphere。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all treat life as a layer or a system: Earth's living zone, another planet's life, an ecological component, a sealed experiment, a planetary actor, a support system, a protected area and a field of study.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都把生命视为一个圈层或一个系统：地球的生命区、其他行星的生命、生态组分、封闭实验、行星行动者、支持系统、保护区与研究领域。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a blue planet wrapped in a green film thinner than an apple's skin.
core.cn: 核心意象：一颗蓝色行星裹着比苹果皮还薄的绿色膜。

chain: ONE BOX IN THE EARTH SYSTEM

branches.en: THE LAYER: a thin zone of life, treated as one component of the planet.
branches.cn: 圈层：薄薄的生命带，被当作行星的一个组分。

branches.en: OTHER WORLDS: the word detaches from Earth and names any planet's living layer.
branches.cn: 其他世界：该词脱离地球，指任何行星的生命层。

branches.en: THE SEALED MODEL: a miniature biosphere tests whether life can recycle its own conditions.
branches.cn: 封闭模型：微型生物圈检验生命能否循环维持自身条件。

branches.en: LIFE AS ACTOR: the biosphere exchanges matter with air and water and keeps conditions livable.
branches.cn: 生命作为行动者：生物圈与空气、水交换物质，并维持条件宜居。

branches.en: NAMES ON MAPS AND IN JOURNALS: the same word became a protected area and a scientific field.
branches.cn: 地图与期刊上的名字：同一个词变成了保护区与科学领域。

intro.en: Biosphere is a scientific compound of two Greek roots: life and ball. It was made in the nineteenth century and needs no further affix to name its object.
intro.cn: biosphere 是由两个希腊词根构成的科学复合词：生命与球。它于十九世纪造成，命名其对象时不再需要别的词缀。

latinIntro.en: Greek bios gives biology, biota, biosphere and antibiotic; Greek sphaira, through Latin sphaera, gives sphere, spherical, atmosphere and hydrosphere. Biosphere sits where the two families meet.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 bios 给出 biology、biota、biosphere、antibiotic；希腊 sphaira 经拉丁 sphaera 给出 sphere、spherical、atmosphere、hydrosphere。biosphere 正处在两个词族的交会处。

items.meaning: the living layer of a planet
items.example: The biosphere absorbs a large share of our carbon emissions.
items.exampleCN: 生物圈吸收了我们排放的很大一部分碳。

items.example: Biospheric models link life to climate.
items.exampleCN: 生物圈模型把生命与气候联系起来。

items.example: Biology split into many subfields in the twentieth century.
items.exampleCN: 生物学在二十世纪分成许多子领域。

items.meaning: all living things of a region
items.example: The island's biota includes no large mammals.
items.exampleCN: 该岛的生物区系中没有大型哺乳动物。

items.example: The tundra biome has a short growing season.
items.exampleCN: 苔原生物群系的生长季很短。

items.example: The antibiotic blocks cell wall growth.
items.exampleCN: 该抗生素阻断细胞壁的生成。

items.meaning: a ball; a field of activity
items.example: The earth is not a perfect sphere.
items.exampleCN: 地球并不是完美的球体。

items.meaning: the gas envelope of a planet
items.example: The atmosphere filters ultraviolet light.
items.exampleCN: 大气过滤紫外线。

definition_zh: 能力；潜力；功能；性能
definition_en: the power or ability to do something, or the range of things a person or system can do
core_image: 一双手伸进箱子，够到最里面的东西并把它拿出来
scene: 这里指「能力」。 The new telescope has the capability to detect light from the earliest galaxies.
sceneCN: 这里 capability 是「功能／性能」（第 3 个义项：设备能做到的事）；句意：这台新望远镜具备探测最早星系光线的能力。场景要点：镜头深入夜空，把极暗的光收进来，强调“能做到”而非“能装多少”。

pos.zh: 能力；潜力；功能；性能

senses.title: The power to do something
senses.titleCN: 一般能力：手够得到，也拿得动
senses.definition: the power or ability to do something
senses.definitionCN: 做某事的力量或能力
senses.example: She has the capability to lead a large team.
senses.exampleCN: 她有能力领导一支大团队。
senses.why: Capabilis meant 'able to grasp or hold'. The -ity suffix turns that adjective into the quality, so the holding hand becomes the power to carry a task through.
senses.whyCN: capabilis 意为“能抓住、能容纳的”。-ity 后缀把这个形容词变成性质，于是“握住的手”变成“把任务做到底的力量”。

senses.title: Undeveloped ability
senses.definition: an undeveloped ability that may be realized later
senses.definitionCN: 尚未发展、但以后可能实现的能力
senses.example: The program helps students discover capabilities they did not know they had.
senses.exampleCN: 这个项目帮助学生发现他们不知道自己拥有的能力。
senses.why: A hand can hold more than it is currently holding. The noun therefore names capacity not yet used, which is why the plural often means latent powers.
senses.whyCN: 一只手能拿的东西比它现在拿着的更多。因此这个名词指尚未被使用的能力，这也是复数常表示“潜在才能”的原因。

senses.title: What a device can do
senses.titleCN: 功能／性能：机器能做的事
senses.definition: the range of things a device or system is able to do
senses.definitionCN: 设备或系统能够做到的事情的范围
senses.example: The telescope has the capability to detect very faint light.
senses.exampleCN: 这台望远镜有能力探测非常微弱的光。
senses.why: Tools are treated as hands: what they can reach and hold defines them. The noun moves from a person's power to a machine's functions.
senses.whyCN: 工具被当作手：它们能伸到、能拿住什么，就定义了它们。名词于是从人的力量转到机器的功能。

senses.title: Developed professional skill
senses.titleCN: 专业本领：训练出来的够取范围
senses.definition: a person's developed skill or competence in a field
senses.definitionCN: 某人在某一领域已发展的技能或胜任力
senses.example: Her capabilities as a translator are well known.
senses.exampleCN: 她作为译者的本领广为人知。
senses.why: Training turns a general power into a specific reach. The plural names the set of things a person can actually do well.
senses.whyCN: 训练把一般的力量变成具体的够取范围。复数命名的是一个人真正能做好的那一组事情。

senses.title: Military power to act
senses.titleCN: 军事能力：国家的手能伸多远
senses.definition: the military power to carry out an operation
senses.definitionCN: 执行军事行动的能力
senses.example: The country announced a new long-range strike capability.
senses.exampleCN: 该国宣布具备新的远程打击能力。
senses.why: States are treated as agents with hands. What they can reach across distance is their capability, so the word becomes a measure of strategic reach.
senses.whyCN: 国家被当作有手的行动者。它们能跨越距离够到什么，就是它们的 capability，因此这个词成为战略触达的度量。

senses.title: The power to produce at all
senses.titleCN: 生产能力：能不能做，而非能做多少
senses.definition: the power to produce goods or results, as distinct from the maximum amount
senses.definitionCN: 生产商品或成果的能力，区别于最大产量
senses.example: The factory has the capability to switch to electric parts.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂有能力转产电动部件。
senses.why: Here capability answers 'can it do this at all', not 'how many can it hold'. That is the line between capability and capacity.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 capability 回答的是“它到底能不能做”，而不是“它能装多少”。这正是 capability 与 capacity 的分界线。

senses.title: The range of operations a system offers
senses.titleCN: 技术能力：可执行操作的清单
senses.definition: the set of operations a technique or instrument can perform
senses.definitionCN: 某项技术或仪器能够执行的一组操作
senses.example: The software's capabilities include voice search and offline maps.
senses.exampleCN: 这款软件的功能包括语音搜索和离线地图。
senses.why: Each operation is something the system can reach. The plural lists the reachable actions, turning an abstract power into a checklist.
senses.whyCN: 每一项操作都是系统能够够到的东西。复数把这些可达动作列成清单，把抽象的能力变成可勾选的条目。

senses.title: An organization's power to carry out its mandate
senses.titleCN: 机构执行力：能不能真正办到
senses.definition: an organization's power to respond and carry out its mandate
senses.definitionCN: 组织作出反应并完成其职责的能力
senses.example: The agency lacks the capability to inspect every site.
senses.exampleCN: 该机构没有能力检查每一个场地。
senses.why: An institution is also an agent. Its reach is measured by what it can actually carry out, so the word names operational power rather than intention.
senses.whyCN: 机构也是行动者。它的触达由它实际能办成的事来衡量，因此这个词命名的是执行力量，而不是意图。

senses.title: A right held by a computing process
senses.titleCN: 计算机能力／权限：把“能力”做成可传递的令牌
senses.definition: in computing, a right or token that allows a process to perform an action
senses.definitionCN: 计算机中允许某个进程执行某项操作的权利或令牌
senses.example: The sandbox grants only the capabilities the program needs.
senses.exampleCN: 沙盒只授予程序所需的能力权限。
senses.why: In capability-based security, an abstract ability is made into a concrete object that can be held and passed. The old 'hold' image becomes literal again.
senses.whyCN: 在基于能力的安全模型中，抽象的能力被做成一个可以持有、可以传递的具体对象。古老的“握住”意象又变回了字面意义。

intro.en: Capability is an English derivative of capable, which came from Late Latin capabilis. Its Latin base differs from the base of capacity, and that difference explains the modern division of work between the two words.
intro.cn: capability 是 capable 的英语派生词，而 capable 来自晚期拉丁语 capabilis。它的拉丁词基与 capacity 的词基不同，这个差异解释了现代英语中两个词的分工。

items.en: capere meant 'to grasp, lay hold of, take, catch; take in, hold; be large enough for; comprehend'. The root is PIE *kap- 'to grasp'.
items.cn: capere 意为“抓住、握住、拿取、接住；收进、容纳；大到足以装下；理解”。词根是原始印欧语 *kap-“抓”。

items.en: capax (genitive capacis) meant 'able to hold much, broad, roomy', also 'receptive, fit for'. Its noun capacitas produced English capacity in the early 15th century.
items.cn: capax（属格 capacis）意为“能装很多的、宽的、宽敞的”，也表示“能接受的、适合的”。其名词 capacitas 在 15 世纪初产生英语 capacity。

items.en: Late Latin capabilis meant 'receptive; able to grasp or hold' and was used especially by theologians. It passed through French capable into English capable in the 1590s.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 capabilis 意为“能接受的；能抓住或容纳的”，尤其为神学家使用。它经法语 capable 于 16 世纪 90 年代进入英语。

items.en: English added -ity, from Latin -itatem, to capable, producing capability in the 1580s with the sense 'quality of being capable, power to do'. The suffix names a state or quality.
items.cn: 英语给 capable 加上来自拉丁 -itatem 的 -ity，于 16 世纪 80 年代构成 capability，意为“有能力的状态、做事的力量”。这个后缀命名状态或性质。

items.en: Capax and capacitas answer 'how much fits'; capabilis and capability answer 'what one can do'. Because the Latin bases differ, English capacity specializes in volume and containment, while capability specializes in performance.
items.cn: capax 和 capacitas 回答“能装多少”；capabilis 和 capability 回答“能做什么”。由于拉丁词基不同，英语 capacity 专管容量与容纳，而 capability 专管做事与表现。

items.en: Capabilities in the sense 'undeveloped faculty or property' is recorded from 1778. Modern English extends the word to devices, organizations, the military, and computing permissions, while keeping the 'can do' core.
items.cn: capabilities 表示“尚未发展的能力或属性”的记录可追溯到 1778 年。现代英语把这个词扩展到设备、组织、军事和计算机权限，同时保留“能做到”的核心。

note.en: The look-alikes all descend from capere but split between the capax and capabilis bases; the near-meaning group contains words for ability, skill, and unused power.
note.cn: 形近词都源自 capere，但分成 capax 与 capabilis 两个词基；近义词组则包含能力、技能和未使用的力量。

entries.definition: how much a container, system, or factory can hold or produce. It comes from capax and capacitas, so it answers 'how much', while capability answers 'can it do this'.
entries.definitionCN: 容器、系统或工厂能装下或产出多少。它来自 capax 和 capacitas，回答“多少”，而 capability 回答“能不能做”。

entries.definition: able to do something well. It is the adjective behind capability; the noun adds -ity and names the quality.
entries.definitionCN: 有能力的；能干的。它是 capability 背后的形容词；名词加 -ity，命名这种性质。

entries.definition: large and roomy; able to hold much. It belongs to the containment branch and describes physical space, not performance.
entries.definitionCN: 容量大的；宽敞的；能装很多的。它属于“容纳”分支，描述物理空间，而非做事表现。

entries.definition: in an able or competent manner. It is the adverb of capable, not another noun like capability.
entries.definitionCN: 能干地；有能力地。它是 capable 的副词，不是像 capability 那样的名词。

entries.definition: the general power to do something, often innate or learned. It is the plain everyday word, while capability is more formal and often technical.
entries.definitionCN: 做某事的一般力量，常指天生或习得的能力。它是平实的日常词，而 capability 更正式，常带技术色彩。

entries.definition: the skill needed to do a job to an acceptable standard. It is judged by performance, while capability may exist before it is shown.
entries.definitionCN: 把工作做到可接受标准所需的技能。它由表现来评判，而 capability 可能在表现出来之前就已存在。

entries.definition: ability that has not yet been realized. It matches the latent sense of capability but says nothing about current performance.
entries.definitionCN: 尚未实现的能力。它与 capability 的潜在义相符，但不涉及当前表现。

entries.definition: a particular mental or physical power, such as sight or reason; also a teaching body. It is more specific and less organizational than capability.
entries.definitionCN: 某一具体的心智或身体能力，如视力、理性；也指教师团体。它比 capability 更具体，组织性更弱。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin verb, the real suffix contrast, and the real technical collocations of capability.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁动词、真实的后缀对比，以及 capability 真实的技术搭配。

normal.en: capere = to grasp and hold. Capability is the hand's reach made into a noun.
normal.cn: capere 就是抓住并容纳。capability 就是把手的够取范围变成名词。

normal.en: capable + -ity: the adjective says 'able', the noun says 'the ability'.
normal.cn: capable + -ity：形容词说“有能力的”，名词说“这种能力”。

normal.en: Capability vs capacity is a clean pair: capability = can do; capacity = can hold or produce how much.
normal.cn: capability 与 capacity 是一组清楚的对比：capability 是“能不能做”，capacity 是“能装或能产多少”。

normal.en: The pattern capability to do something keeps the active sense visible.
normal.cn: capability to do something 这个句式让“主动能做”的意义保持可见。

normal.en: Technical capability and capabilities and limitations are standard in specifications, where a checklist of actions is meant.
normal.cn: technical capability 和 capabilities and limitations 是规格书里的标准说法，指的是一份可执行动作清单。

abstract.en: Picture a hand reaching into a deep box and closing around an object at the bottom.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手伸进深箱，在底部合拢抓住一个东西。

abstract.en: Picture a toolbox: each tool is a thing the box can do, and the set of tools is its capabilities.
abstract.cn: 想象一个工具箱：每件工具都是这个箱子能做的一件事，整套工具就是它的 capabilities。

abstract.en: Picture a ring of keys: each key is a permission, and the set of keys is exactly what the holder is capable of opening.
abstract.cn: 想象一串钥匙：每把钥匙是一项权限，整串钥匙正好就是持有者能打开的范围。

examples.en: The team has the capability to finish the project ahead of schedule.
examples.cn: 团队有能力提前完成项目。

examples.en: Engineers tested the material's capability to withstand extreme heat.
examples.cn: 工程师测试了这种材料耐受极端高温的性能。

examples.en: The new radar extends the aircraft's detection capability by fifty kilometres.
examples.cn: 新雷达把飞机的探测能力扩展了五十公里。

dict_mnemonic.text: “开怕必利提”——开（ca）怕（pa）必（bi）利（li）提（ty），箱子开得够深，手才够得着 → capability 能力

root: 拉丁 capere“拿、抓住、容纳”（原始印欧语 *kap-“抓”）；capable < 晚期拉丁 capabilis“能抓住／容纳的”+ -ity（拉丁 -itatem）。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses share one image: a hand that can reach, grasp, and hold. The question is always 'what can this agent do', not 'how much room does it have'.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项共享一个意象：一只能伸到、抓住并握住的手。问题始终是“这个行动者能做什么”，而不是“它有多大空间”。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand reaching into a space, closing on an object, and holding it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手伸进空间，合拢抓住物体并握住。

branches.en: POWER AND LATENT POWER: what an agent can do now, and what it could do once developed.
branches.cn: 现有力量与潜在力量：行动者现在能做什么，以及发展后可能做什么。

branches.en: DEVICE FUNCTIONS: a machine's power and the list of operations it offers are the same reach described at two scales.
branches.cn: 设备功能：机器的能力与它提供的操作清单，是同一够取范围在两种尺度上的描述。

branches.en: PEOPLE AND INSTITUTIONS: a trained person's skill and an organization's operational power are both developed reach.
branches.cn: 人与机构：受过训练者的技能和组织的执行力量，都是发展后的够取范围。

branches.en: COLLECTIVE REACH: military reach and the power to produce answer 'can we act', not 'how much can we hold'.
branches.cn: 集体触达：军事触达与生产的力量，回答的是“我们能不能行动”，而不是“我们能装多少”。

branches.en: COMPUTING: an abstract ability becomes a token that can be held and passed, making the old image literal.
branches.cn: 计算机：抽象能力变成一个可持有、可传递的令牌，使古老意象重新字面化。

intro.en: Capability is formed inside English from the adjective capable plus -ity. The suffix is productive; the base capabil- is a Late Latin stem, and its relatives split into two branches.
intro.cn: capability 是在英语内部由形容词 capable 加 -ity 构成的。后缀有能产性；词基 capabil- 是晚期拉丁词干，其亲属分成两个分支。

latinIntro.en: Latin capere 'to grasp, hold' is the common source of two English families: capax/capacitas gives capacity, capacious and capacitance; capabilis gives capable and capability. English borrowed the stems separately, so the spellings and senses diverge.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 capere“抓、容纳”是两个英语词族的共同源头：capax/capacitas 产生 capacity、capacious、capacitance；capabilis 产生 capable、capability。英语分别借入这些词干，因此拼写和词义都发生分化。

items.structure: capabil- (stem of capabilis) + -ity (state or quality noun)
items.meaning: the quality of being capable; power to do
items.meaningCN: 能力；做事的力量（-ity 构成状态或性质名词）
items.example: The lab has the capability to run the test.
items.exampleCN: 实验室有能力运行这项测试。

items.meaning: able, competent; able to hold or receive
items.meaningCN: 有能力的；能干的；能容纳或接受的
items.example: She is capable of handling the pressure.
items.exampleCN: 她有能力承受这种压力。

items.meaningCN: 能干地；有能力地（-ly 构成方式副词）
items.example: He capably managed the negotiations.
items.exampleCN: 他干练地主持了谈判。

items.meaningCN: 无能力的；不能的（in- 表示否定）
items.example: The old system is incapable of handling the load.
items.exampleCN: 旧系统无法承受这种负载。

items.meaningCN: 无能力；不能胜任（in- 表示否定）
items.example: The report noted the incapability of the current process.
items.exampleCN: 报告指出了当前流程的无力之处。

items.meaningCN: 容量；最大容纳或产出量（词基与 capability 不同）
items.example: The tank has a capacity of 500 litres.
items.exampleCN: 这个罐子的容量是 500 升。

items.meaningCN: 容量大的；宽敞的（-ious 表示“具有……性质的”）
items.example: The bag is capacious enough for a week's clothes.
items.exampleCN: 这个包容量够装一周的衣服。

items.meaning: to make capable; to qualify legally
items.meaningCN: 使有能力；授予法律资格（-ate 构成动词）
items.example: The training capacitates staff to use the equipment.
items.exampleCN: 这项培训使员工具备使用设备的能力。

items.meaning: the ability to store electric charge
items.meaningCN: 电容（储存电荷的能力；-ance 构成状态名词）
items.example: The circuit's capacitance is measured in farads.
items.exampleCN: 电路的电容用法拉计量。

items.meaning: a device that stores electric charge
items.meaningCN: 电容器（储存电荷的装置；-or 表示装置）
items.example: The capacitor discharges through the resistor.
items.exampleCN: 电容器通过电阻放电。
