latinEntries.meaning: to grasp, take, hold; to contain; to comprehend
able to hold much; roomy, receptive
latinEntries.meaningCN: 能装很多的；宽敞的、能接受的

latinEntries.meaning: receptive; able to grasp or hold
latinEntries.meaningCN: 能接受的；能抓住或容纳的

latinEntries.meaning: breadth, capacity, ability to hold much
latinEntries.meaningCN: 宽度；容量；容纳多的能力

definition_zh: 更宽的；更广阔的；更概括的；更广泛的（broad 的比较级）
definition_en: the comparative of broad: wider in physical extent, or larger in range, generality, or inclusiveness
core_image: 两只手把同一块布向两边再拉开一截，比原来更宽
scene: 这里指「更宽的」。 At the review, the editor asked for a broader view that placed the single case inside the whole industry.
sceneCN: 这里 broader 是「更广阔的、更概括的」（第 3 个义项：更概括而非局限于一点）；句意：评审会上，编辑要求作者给出更广阔的视角，不只盯一个案例，而要放进整个行业的背景。场景要点：评审桌、论文稿、行业图表、放大的取景框。

pos.zh: 更宽的；更广阔的；更概括的（broad 的比较级）

senses.title: Wider in physical extent
senses.definition: comparative of broad: having a greater distance from side to side than something else
senses.definitionCN: broad 的比较级：从一侧到另一侧的距离比另一物更大
senses.example: The new bridge is broader than the old one by two lanes.
senses.exampleCN: 新桥比旧桥宽出两条车道。
senses.why: Broader is not a separate word with its own meaning; it is broad plus the comparative suffix -er. The first sense simply compares two physical widths, so the base adjective supplies all the content and -er supplies the comparison.
senses.whyCN: broader 不是有独立词义的词，而是 broad 加比较级后缀 -er。第一个义项只是比较两个物理宽度，因此基础形容词提供全部内容，-er 提供比较。

senses.title: Larger in range or scope
senses.definition: covering a larger range of things, cases, or activities than another range
senses.definitionCN: 比另一范围覆盖更多事物、案例或活动
senses.example: The second study uses a broader range of sources.
senses.exampleCN: 第二项研究使用了范围更广的资料。
senses.why: The comparison moves from space to scope: one range extends farther at both ends than another. The comparative suffix does the comparing, and broad supplies the range image, so no new root is created.
senses.whyCN: 比较从空间转到范围：一个范围的两端都比另一个伸得更远。比较级后缀负责比较，broad 提供范围的意象，因此没有产生新词根。

senses.title: More general, less specific
senses.definition: belonging to a higher or more general category, as in the broader sense of a word
senses.definitionCN: 属于更高或更概括的类别，如某词的 broader sense
senses.example: In the broader sense, 'tool' includes software as well as hammers.
senses.exampleCN: 在更宽泛的意义上，tool 既包括锤子，也包括软件。
senses.why: A category is imagined as an area: the broader category covers the narrower one. Saying 'in the broader sense' moves up one level of generality, losing detail as it gains coverage; the comparative is doing the movement.
senses.whyCN: 类别被想象成一块面积：更宽的类别覆盖更窄的类别。说 in the broader sense 就是上升一层概括，覆盖变多而细节变少；这个移动由比较级完成。

senses.title: More inclusive: audience and participation
senses.titleCN: 更具包容性：受众与参与
senses.definition: reaching or including more people than a previous audience, group, or arrangement
senses.definitionCN: 比先前的受众、群体或安排触及或包含更多人
senses.example: The podcast found a broader audience than the original radio show.
senses.exampleCN: 这档播客找到了比原广播节目更广泛的受众。
senses.why: The circle of people is treated as an area. A broader audience means the circle's edge has moved outward, so more people are inside it; the same spatial comparison now measures social reach.
senses.whyCN: 人群的圈子被当作一块面积。更广泛的受众意味着圈的边缘向外移，因此更多人在圈内；同一个空间比较现在量的是社会触达。

senses.title: More open or tolerant in outlook
senses.definition: of a person or view, more willing to accept differences and less limited by one narrow standpoint
senses.definitionCN: 指人或观点更愿意接受差异，较少受单一狭隘立场限制
senses.example: She came back with a broader view of what counts as success.
senses.exampleCN: 她回来时对什么算成功有了更开阔的看法。
senses.why: This is the mind-as-space metaphor again, now comparative: an outlook with wider walls admits more kinds of life and opinion without rejecting them first. The comparison turns width into tolerance.
senses.whyCN: 这仍是“心智即空间”的比喻，只是变成比较级：墙更宽的眼界能容纳更多生活方式与意见，而不先排斥它们。比较把宽度变成了宽容。

senses.title: Discourse: the broader picture and context
senses.titleCN: 篇章用法：更大的图景与背景
senses.definition: used in writing and speech to call for the larger setting around a case, as in the broader context
senses.definitionCN: 用于书面与口语，要求把个案放回更大的背景中，如 the broader context
senses.example: Before judging the decision, consider the broader context of the shortage.
senses.exampleCN: 在评判这一决定前，先考虑短缺这一更大的背景。
senses.why: The comparative asks the reader to step back until more of the scene is visible. It is a framing move, not a new sense of broad: the same adjective is simply placed in a comparison of visible scope.
senses.whyCN: 这个比较级要求读者后退，直到看见更多场景。它是一种取景动作，而不是 broad 的新义项：同一个形容词只是被放进可见范围的比较。

senses.title: Usage boundary: broader versus wider
senses.definition: both compare width; wider is usual for physical gaps, while broader is usual for scope, meaning, and outlook
senses.definitionCN: 两者都比较宽度；wider 常用于物理缺口，broader 常用于范围、意义与眼界
senses.example: The river is wider here, but the argument is broader there.
senses.exampleCN: 河在这里更宽，而论点在那里更广。
senses.why: Broad and wide overlap physically, but broad developed a strong abstract life. Broader therefore follows broad into abstract comparisons, and wider stays closer to measured space; the difference is in the base adjective, not the comparative ending.
senses.whyCN: broad 与 wide 在物理上有重叠，但 broad 发展出很强的抽象用法。因此 broader 跟随 broad 进入抽象比较，而 wider 更贴近可测量的空间；差别在基础形容词，不在比较级词尾。

senses.title: Usage boundary: broader versus larger and greater
senses.definition: larger compares size or number; greater compares amount or importance; broader compares the width of a range
senses.definitionCN: larger 比较尺寸或数量；greater 比较数量或重要性；broader 比较范围的宽度
senses.example: A larger sample may still not give a broader picture.
senses.exampleCN: 更大的样本未必能给出更广的图景。
senses.why: The three comparatives measure different things: size, amount, and breadth. A sample can grow in number without covering more kinds of cases, which is why the adjectives cannot be swapped.
senses.whyCN: 这三个比较级量的是不同东西：尺寸、数量与广度。样本数量可以变大，却未必覆盖更多种类的案例，因此这些形容词不能互换。

senses.title: Grammar boundary: comparison without an independent meaning
senses.titleCN: 语法边界：没有独立词义的比较级
senses.definition: broader exists only as the comparative of broad; it cannot be used as a base adjective or paired with 'more'
senses.definitionCN: broader 只作为 broad 的比较级存在；不能当原级形容词用，也不能与 more 搭配
senses.example: Say 'broader', not 'more broader'; the comparison is already inside the word.
senses.exampleCN: 说 broader，不说 more broader；比较意义已经在词内。
senses.why: The suffix -er is the comparative marker, so the word has no lexical entry of its own. Every sense it shows is simply one sense of broad placed in a comparison, which is why no new etymology is needed.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -er 就是比较级标记，因此这个词没有自己的词条。它显示的每个义项，都只是 broad 的某个义项被放进比较，因此不需要新的词源。

intro.en: Broader is not a borrowed word and has no independent history. It is broad plus the native comparative suffix -er, formed by rule whenever two things are compared; its meaning is entirely the meaning of broad under comparison. Etymonline has no separate broader entry.
intro.cn: broader 不是借词，也没有独立的历史。它是 broad 加本土比较级后缀 -er，凡比较两物时按规则构成；它的意义完全是 broad 的意义被放进比较。etymonline 没有单独的 broader 词条。

items.en: The base is Old English brād 'wide, not narrow', also 'flat, open, extended'. It already covered physical width and open space; the abstract senses of daylight and of speech developed later.
items.cn: 基础词是古英语 brād“宽的、不窄的”，也表示“平坦的、敞开的、延展的”。它已覆盖物理宽度与开阔空间；白昼与言语的抽象义后来才发展出来。

items.en: Brād goes back to Proto-Germanic *braidi-, also the source of German breit and Dutch breed. Etymonline says the origin is unknown and the word is not found outside Germanic; the deeper PIE source should not be invented.
items.cn: brād 上溯原始日耳曼语 *braidi-，也是德语 breit、荷兰语 breed 的来源。etymonline 称其来源不明，且不见于日耳曼语族之外；更深的原始印欧语来源不应硬造。

items.en: The suffix -er is the native comparative ending, from Old English -ra and Germanic *-izô. It is the regular marker for short adjectives, as in wider, deeper, and broader. It adds comparison, not a new lexical root.
items.cn: 后缀 -er 是本土比较级词尾，来自古英语 -ra 与日耳曼语 *-izô。它是短形容词的规则标记，如 wider、deeper、broader。它添加的是比较，不是新的词根。

items.en: Broader is produced by rule, not recorded as a separate coinage. It has no dictionary history of its own; the same form would appear whenever broad is compared. This is why its etymology is the etymology of broad plus the comparative ending.
items.cn: broader 按规则生成，不是单独铸造的词。它没有自己的词典史；只要 broad 参与比较，就会出现这个形式。因此它的词源就是 broad 的词源加比较级词尾。

items.en: As broad grew common in abstract phrases such as broad view and broad sense, the comparative followed: broader view, broader sense, broader context. The exact first dates of these phrases are not recorded, so the century is only an approximate frame.
items.cn: 随着 broad 在 broad view、broad sense 等抽象短语中普及，比较级也随之跟进：broader view、broader sense、broader context。这些短语的确切最早年代未见记录，因此该世纪只是大致框架。

items.en: Modern academic and journalistic English uses broader before nouns to frame a discussion: broader implications, broader picture, broader debate. The comparative still carries every sense of broad, and it is still an inflected form rather than a new word.
items.cn: 现代学术与新闻英语把 broader 放在名词前，用来给讨论取景：broader implications、broader picture、broader debate。这个比较级仍承载 broad 的所有义项，也仍是屈折形式，而不是一个新词。

note.en: The first group is broad in its positive, superlative, adverbial, and verb forms; the second separates comparisons of width, size, amount, and coverage.
note.cn: 第一组是 broad 的原级、最高级、副词与动词形式；第二组区分宽度、尺寸、数量与覆盖范围这几种比较。

entries.definition: Wide or large in range. It is the base form; broader is only this adjective under comparison.
entries.definitionCN: 宽的，或范围广的。它是原级；broader 只是这个形容词被放进比较。

entries.definition: The most broad of a group. It uses the superlative -est, where broader uses the comparative -er.
entries.definitionCN: 一群中最宽的。它用最高级 -est，而 broader 用比较级 -er。

entries.definition: In general terms or widely. It modifies a verb or sentence, while broader modifies a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 大体上或广泛地。它修饰动词或句子，而 broader 修饰名词。

entries.definition: To make or become broad. It names the action, while broader only compares two degrees of the quality.
entries.definitionCN: 使变宽或变宽。它命名动作，而 broader 只比较同一性质的两个程度。

entries.definition: Comparative of wide: measuring more from side to side. It is the usual choice for physical gaps, roads, and openings.
entries.definitionCN: wide 的比较级：两侧之间量得更多。它是物理缺口、道路与开口的常用选择。

entries.definition: Comparative of large: greater in size or number. It measures overall magnitude, not the width of a range.
entries.definitionCN: large 的比较级：尺寸或数量更大。它量的是总体规模，而不是范围的宽度。

entries.definition: Comparative of great: larger in amount, degree, or importance. It often compares abstract value rather than extent.
entries.definitionCN: great 的比较级：数量、程度或重要性更大。它常比较抽象价值，而不是范围。

entries.definition: Covering much or nearly everything. It stresses completeness of coverage, while broader only compares two degrees of width.
entries.definitionCN: 覆盖很多或几乎全部的。它强调覆盖的完整性，而 broader 只比较宽度的两个程度。

normalIntro.en: Real associations: broad + the comparative -er, the same adjective-and-suffix pattern as wider and deeper; broader has no separate root to memorise.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联想：broad + 比较级 -er，与 wider、deeper 同一“形容词加后缀”模式；broader 没有可单独记的词根。

normal.en: broad + -er = broader, exactly like wide + -er = wider and deep + -er = deeper. The suffix means 'more', and it needs no new root.
normal.cn: broad + -er = broader，正如 wide + -er = wider、deep + -er = deeper。后缀表示“更”，不需要新词根。

normal.en: broader is not a base adjective: you say broader, never more broader. The comparison is already inside the word.
normal.cn: broader 不是原级形容词：说 broader，绝不说 more broader。比较意义已经在词内。

normal.en: In the broader sense, you climb one step up the category ladder: more coverage, less detail.
normal.cn: in the broader sense 就是沿类别阶梯上升一级：覆盖更多，细节更少。

normal.en: A broader audience is a circle with its edge pushed outward, so more people are inside.
normal.cn: 更广泛的受众就是一个边缘被向外推的圈，因此更多人在圈内。

normal.en: The broader picture is a wider camera angle: the same scene, but more of it is visible.
normal.cn: the broader picture 就是一个更广的镜头：场景不变，但看见的部分更多。

abstract.en: Two roads side by side: broader is the one whose two edges stand farther apart, though both lead to the same destination.
abstract.cn: 两条并排的路：broader 是两边距离更远的那条，尽管两者通向同一目的地。

abstract.en: A lens zooming out: nothing in the scene changes, but the frame now holds more of the world, and that is broader.
abstract.cn: 镜头拉远：场景里没有任何东西改变，但取景框现在装下更多世界，这就是 broader。

abstract.en: A hand opening from a fist to a flat palm: the same hand, a wider span, more things it can hold.
abstract.cn: 一只手从拳头张开成掌心：同一只手，跨度更大，能握住的东西更多。

examples.en: The new report takes a broader view of the problem than the earlier one.
examples.cn: 这份新报告比早先那份对问题采取了更广阔的视角。

examples.en: A broader range of countries took part in the second survey.
examples.cn: 第二次调查有更广泛的国家参与。

examples.en: We need to consider the broader context before making a decision.
examples.cn: 在做决定之前，我们需要考虑更大的背景。

dict_mnemonic.text: “布若德”——把布（broad）再往两边拉一点，比原来更宽 → broader 更宽的

root: broad（古英语 brād“宽的”，原始日耳曼语 *braidi-，来源不明）+ -er（本土比较级词尾，古英语 -ra，日耳曼语 *-izô）；broader 是 broad 的比较级屈折形式，不是独立词根或新派生词。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of broader are nine senses of broad under comparison: physical width, range, generality, inclusion, outlook, framing, and two boundaries. The comparative ending never adds a new meaning of its own.
sensesIntro.cn: broader 的九个义项就是 broad 的九个义项被放进比较：物理宽度、范围、概括度、包容性、眼界、取景，以及两个边界。比较级词尾本身从不添加新意义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one width is set beside another, and this one reaches farther at both edges.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个宽度与另一个并置，而这一个在两条边上都伸得更远。

branches.en: PHYSICAL: two objects are compared, and one measures more from side to side.
branches.cn: 物理：两个物体被比较，其中一个从一侧到另一侧量得更多。

branches.en: SCOPE: the compared thing covers more cases, sources, or activities at both ends.
branches.cn: 范围：被比较者覆盖更多案例、资料或活动，两端都伸得更远。

branches.en: GENERALITY: the broader category sits one level above the narrower one.
branches.cn: 概括度：较宽的类别位于较窄类别之上的一层。

branches.en: PEOPLE AND MIND: a wider circle admits more people, and a wider outlook admits more views.
branches.cn: 人群与心智：更宽的圈容纳更多人，更宽的眼界容纳更多观点。

branches.en: FRAME AND BOUNDARIES: the comparative frames a scene, then meets wider, larger, greater, and the grammar of comparison.
branches.cn: 取景与边界：这个比较级为场景取景，再与 wider、larger、greater 以及比较语法划界。

intro.en: Broader has one live suffix, the comparative -er, attached to the adjective broad. There is no prefix and no derivational suffix; the ending marks a grammatical degree, not a new word.
intro.cn: broader 在形容词 broad 上只有一个活后缀，即比较级 -er。它没有前缀，也没有派生后缀；这个词尾标记语法程度，而不是构成新词。

latinIntro.en: Broader has no Latin ancestry. Latin latus 'wide' and amplus 'large' are separate roots, and extendere is a separate verb; the entries below are counterparts that English also uses, not ancestors of broader.
latinIntro.cn: broader 没有拉丁语血统。拉丁语 latus“宽的”与 amplus“大的”是另外的词根，extendere 是另一个动词；下面的条目是英语同时使用的对应词，不是 broader 的祖先。

items.meaning: more broad; the adjective placed in a comparison, with no change of lexical meaning
items.meaningCN: 更宽的；形容词被放进比较，词汇意义不变
items.example: The river is broader at its mouth.
items.exampleCN: 这条河在入海口更宽。

items.meaning: wide in space or large in range; the base that supplies all the content of broader
items.meaningCN: 空间上宽的，或范围广的；为 broader 提供全部内容的基础词
items.example: A broad plain lies beyond the hills.
items.exampleCN: 山丘之外是一片广阔的平原。

items.meaning: most broad of a group; the superlative counterpart of broader
items.meaningCN: 一群中最宽的；broader 的最高级对应形式
items.example: This is the broadest part of the valley.
items.exampleCN: 这是山谷最宽的部分。

items.meaning: in general terms or widely; the adjective becomes an adverb
items.meaningCN: 大体上或广泛地；形容词变成副词
items.example: Broadly, the two plans agree.
items.exampleCN: 大体而言，两个方案是一致的。

items.structure: broad + -th (noun of a quality), with a vowel change
items.meaning: width or range; the noun of the quality that broader compares
items.meaningCN: 宽度或广度；broader 所比较的性质的名词形式
items.example: The breadth of the shelf is two metres.
items.exampleCN: 这个架子的宽度是两米。

items.meaning: to make or become broad; the action that produces a broader state
items.meaningCN: 使变宽或变宽；产生更宽状态的动作
items.example: They broadened the road last year.
items.exampleCN: 他们去年把路加宽了。

items.meaning: the quality of being broad; a regular alternative to breadth
items.meaningCN: 宽的性质；breadth 的规则替代形式
items.example: The broadness of the proposal worried the board.
items.exampleCN: 提案的宽泛让董事会担忧。

items.meaning: measuring much from side to side; a separate adjective whose comparative is wider
items.meaningCN: 两侧之间量得多的；另一个形容词，其比较级是 wider
items.example: The gap is too wide to jump.
items.exampleCN: 缺口太宽，跳不过去。

items.meaning: to make or become wide; the physical-width counterpart of broaden
items.meaningCN: 使变宽或变宽；broaden 在物理宽度上的对应动词
items.example: They widened the doorway for the wheelchair.
items.exampleCN: 他们为轮椅把门洞加宽了。

latinEntries.meaning: wide, broad; a separate Latin root, not the source of broad
latinEntries.meaningCN: 宽的；另一个拉丁词根，并非 broad 的来源

latinEntries.meaning: large, spacious, abundant; the source of amplify and ampler, not of broader
latinEntries.meaningCN: 大的、宽敞的、丰富的；amplify 与 ampler 的来源，不是 broader 的来源

latinEntries.meaning: to stretch out or lengthen; a Latin counterpart stressing length
latinEntries.meaningCN: 向外伸展或延长；强调长度的拉丁对应词

definition_zh: 刚性；僵直；死板；严格不变的性质
definition_en: the quality of being stiff, unbending or unable to change; resistance to deformation or adaptation
core_image: 一根钢梁在重压下弯了不到一毫米，卸去载荷后仍然笔直如初
scene: 桥梁检测时，工程师在钢梁上逐级加载，仪表指针几乎不动。 The rigidity of the steel beam kept the bridge deck from sagging under the load.
sceneCN: 这里取第 1 个义项：材料抵抗弯曲与变形的能力；句意为钢梁的刚性使桥面在载荷下没有下沉。图中可辨识物件：钢梁、千分表、加载砝码、桥面。

pos.zh: 刚性；僵直；死板；不可变性（不可数）

senses.title: A material that will not bend
senses.definition: the property of a solid that resists bending or deformation under force
senses.definitionCN: 固体在外力下抵抗弯曲与变形的性质
senses.example: The rigidity of the alloy kept the blade from warping.
senses.exampleCN: 这种合金的刚性使叶片不会变形。
senses.why: A material that holds its shape under load is the oldest sense, because rigidity was first seen in beams and bones.
senses.whyCN: 受载仍保持形状是这个词最古老的一层，因为刚性最早见于梁木与骨骼。

senses.title: A frame that will not sag
senses.definition: the stiffness of a structure or frame that keeps it from sagging or twisting
senses.definitionCN: 结构或框架的刚度，使其不致下沉或扭转
senses.example: The rigidity of the frame comes from triangular bracing.
senses.exampleCN: 框架的刚性来自三角形支撑。
senses.why: A frame is rigid when its parts cannot slide past one another, and bracing is how builders remove that freedom.
senses.whyCN: 构件的各部分不能相互滑动时，框架才算刚，而支撑正是建造者拿走那种自由的手段。

senses.title: A body that will not loosen
senses.definition: stiffness of the limbs or muscles that makes movement slow and awkward
senses.definitionCN: 四肢或肌肉发僵，使动作迟缓笨拙的状态
senses.example: Rigidity in his shoulders made the swimmer slow to turn.
senses.exampleCN: 肩部的僵直让这名游泳者转身很慢。
senses.why: Warm muscle bends and lengthens; cold or tense muscle holds its length, and that held length is rigidity.
senses.whyCN: 温暖的肌肉能弯能伸，寒冷或紧张的肌肉则保持原长，这种被固定住的长度就是僵直。

senses.title: A sign in medicine
senses.definition: in medicine, a fixed resistance of muscles to passive movement, often a sign of nerve disease
senses.definitionCN: 在医学中，肌肉对被动活动呈现固定阻力，常为神经疾病的体征
senses.example: Muscle rigidity is common in Parkinson's disease.
senses.exampleCN: 肌肉僵直在帕金森病中很常见。
senses.why: When the nervous system keeps a muscle switched on, the limb feels like a locked hinge, and clinicians call it rigidity.
senses.whyCN: 当神经系统让肌肉持续紧张，肢体就像被锁住的铰链，临床医生称这种状态为僵直。

senses.title: A mind that will not move
senses.definition: an unwillingness or inability to change habits of thought or accept another view
senses.definitionCN: 不愿或不能改变思维习惯、接受另一种看法的状态
senses.example: Her rigidity about routines made any change distressing.
senses.exampleCN: 她对固定流程的执着让任何改变都令人难受。
senses.why: Thinking that will not bend repeats the same answer, and the physical word for unbending serves the mental case.
senses.whyCN: 不会弯的思维重复同一个答案，那个表示「不弯」的物理词就用到了心理情形上。

senses.title: A rule applied without slack
senses.definition: the quality of a rule or official practice that allows no discretion or exception
senses.definitionCN: 规则或官方做法不留裁量空间、不容例外的性质
senses.example: The rigidity of the rule left the clerk no discretion.
senses.exampleCN: 规则的僵硬让那名职员毫无裁量权。
senses.why: A rule written so tightly that no case can bend it turns a guard against exceptions, and that is what the word criticises.
senses.whyCN: 写得紧到任何个案都弯不动的规则，会把守则变成拒绝例外的关卡，这正是这个词所批评的。

senses.title: Wages that will not fall
senses.definition: in economics, the failure of prices or wages to adjust when supply and demand change
senses.definitionCN: 在经济学中，价格或工资在供求变化时无法调整的现象
senses.example: Wage rigidity keeps unemployment high after a shock.
senses.exampleCN: 工资刚性使冲击之后的失业率居高不下。
senses.why: A wage that cannot move down is a price stuck at one level, and economists describe that stuckness as rigidity.
senses.whyCN: 降不下去的工资是卡在一个水平上的价格，经济学家把这种卡住的状态称为刚性。

senses.title: A shape that cannot deform
senses.definition: in geometry and mechanics, the property of a body whose distances and angles do not change under movement
senses.definitionCN: 在几何与力学中，物体在运动时距离与角度都不改变的性质
senses.example: The rigidity of a body in geometry means its distances never change under rotation.
senses.exampleCN: 几何中物体的刚性意味着旋转时距离永不改变。
senses.why: If every pair of points keeps its distance, the body can only turn and slide, never distort, and that is the strict mathematical sense.
senses.whyCN: 若每一对点的距离都保持不变，物体就只能转动和平移，绝不会扭曲，这是严格的数学含义。

senses.title: A hierarchy that blocks movement
senses.definition: the inflexibility of an institution or social order that prevents people or ideas from moving
senses.definitionCN: 机构或社会秩序不容人或观念流动的僵化状态
senses.example: The rigidity of the old hierarchy blocked promotion.
senses.exampleCN: 旧有层级的僵化堵住了晋升之路。
senses.why: A ladder whose rungs cannot be reached is rigid in the social sense, and the word carries the same image of a fixed frame.
senses.whyCN: 一架横档够不着的梯子在社会的意义上就是僵硬的，这个词仍带着固定框架的同一意象。

intro.en: Rigidity comes from Latin rigiditas, built on rigidus 'stiff' and rigere 'to be stiff or numb'. Beyond Latin the reconstruction is source uncertain, so the deeper root is usually left open.
intro.cn: rigidity 来自拉丁语 rigiditas，由 rigidus「僵硬的」与 rigere「发僵、变硬」构成。越过拉丁语之后属于重构，来源不确定，因此更深的词根通常不作定论。

items.en: Rigere meant to be stiff, numb or fixed, said of a limb that will not move and of a body stiffened by cold.
items.cn: rigere 意为发僵、麻木、固定不动，用于不会活动的肢体，也用于被寒冷冻僵的身体。

items.en: The adjective rigidus described anything stiff, hard or unbending, from a beam to a person's manner.
items.cn: 形容词 rigidus 描述一切僵硬、坚硬、不肯弯的东西，从梁木到人的态度。

items.en: Rigor named the stiffness itself, and in English it kept the senses of strictness and of a chill running through the body.
items.cn: rigor 指僵硬本身，进入英语后保留了「严格」与「寒战穿身」两种意思。

items.en: Rigiditas turned the adjective into a noun of quality, the form that passed through French into English.
items.cn: rigiditas 把形容词变成表示性质的名词，这一形式经法语进入英语。

items.en: English rigidity appears in the seventeenth century, first in descriptions of bodies and mechanical parts.
items.cn: 英语中的 rigidity 出现于十七世纪，最初用于描述物体与机械部件。

items.en: In the nineteenth and twentieth centuries the word was applied to muscle signs, to rigid prices and wages, and to institutional inflexibility.
items.cn: 十九与二十世纪，这个词被用到肌肉体征、价格与工资刚性，以及制度的僵化上。

note.en: The first group shares the stiff root or merely looks like it; the second group names related qualities.
note.cn: 第一组与本词同根或只是形近；第二组是意思相关的其他性质。

entries.definition: The adjective: stiff, unbending, strictly fixed.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词：僵硬的、不肯弯的、严格固定的。

entries.definition: The adverb: in a stiff or unyielding manner.
entries.definitionCN: 副词：以僵硬或不妥协的方式。

entries.definition: To make or become stiff, literally or in habit.
entries.definitionCN: 使变硬、变僵，可用于实物，也可用于习惯。

entries.definition: Strictness, or a sudden chill; the noun behind the adjective rigorous.
entries.definitionCN: 严格，或突然的寒战；形容词「严谨的」背后的名词。

entries.definition: Strict and thorough, from the same stiffness but turned into method.
entries.definitionCN: 严格而周密的，同出「僵」这一层，但转成了方法上的严谨。

entries.definition: Cold in temperature or in manner; it only looks close, since its root means cold.
entries.definitionCN: 温度低或态度冷淡；只是形近，其词根意为寒冷。

entries.definition: The everyday word for the bodily or material quality.
entries.definitionCN: 口语中最常用的说法，指身体或材料的僵、硬。

entries.definition: Unwillingness to bend, closer to the mental and institutional senses.
entries.definitionCN: 不愿弯曲，更贴近心理与制度层面的意思。

entries.definition: Resistance to scratching or pressing, a material property that is not the same as stiffness.
entries.definitionCN: 抗刮擦或抗压的能力，与刚性并非同一性质。

entries.definition: Steadiness under pressure, often a virtue rather than a fault.
entries.definitionCN: 受压时的稳定，常是优点而非缺陷。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the Latin verb, the real family and the fixed phrases of engineering and economics.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁动词、同族词，以及工程与经济学里的固定说法。

normal.en: Latin rigere meant to be stiff or numb, and rigidity is that state turned into a noun.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 rigere 意为发僵、麻木，rigidity 就是把这种状态变成名词。

normal.en: The family runs rigid, rigidly, rigidify, rigidity and rigor.
normal.cn: 同族词有 rigid、rigidly、rigidify、rigidity 与 rigor。

normal.en: Engineers test structural rigidity; doctors note muscle rigidity; economists warn of wage rigidity.
normal.cn: 工程师测结构刚性，医生记肌肉僵直，经济学家警告工资刚性。

normal.en: A rigid body in geometry keeps every distance fixed while it turns.
normal.cn: 几何中的刚体在转动时保持所有距离不变。

normal.en: Rigidity is measured against flexibility: the same scale, two ends.
normal.cn: 刚性是相对柔性来度量的：同一根标尺，两个端点。

abstract.en: A beam that will not bend carries more, but it also breaks instead of yielding.
abstract.cn: 不肯弯的梁能承更多重量，但宁可断裂也不让步。

abstract.en: A rule with no slack protects nobody in the end, because every real case needs an exception.
abstract.cn: 不留余地的规则最终保护不了谁，因为每个真实个案都需要例外。

abstract.en: The stiffest mind is not the strongest; it is the one with the fewest ways out.
abstract.cn: 最僵硬的头脑不是最强的，而是出口最少的。

examples.en: The rigidity of the ceramic keeps the cutting edge sharp.
examples.cn: 陶瓷的刚性使刀刃保持锋利。

examples.en: Rigidity in the labour market can prolong a recession.
examples.cn: 劳动力市场的刚性会拖长衰退。

examples.en: The instructor noticed rigidity in the beginner's hips.
examples.cn: 教练注意到初学者髋部的僵紧。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「瑞吉迪提」——像冻住的铁棍，怎么掰也掰不弯：刚性

root: 拉丁语 rigere「发僵、变硬」→ rigidus「僵硬的」→ rigiditas「僵硬的性质」；经法语进入英语。更深词根属重构，来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one unbending beam: the stiffness of a material, of a frame, of a limb, the medical sign, the closed mind, the rule without slack, the wage that will not fall, the shape that cannot deform and the hierarchy that blocks movement.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项跟着一根不肯弯的梁：材料的刚性、构架的刚性、肢体的僵直、医学体征、封闭的头脑、不留余地的规则、降不下来的工资、不能变形的形体，以及卡住流动的层级。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a steel beam bends less than a millimetre under load and returns to dead straight.
core.cn: 核心意象：钢梁在载荷下弯不到一毫米，卸力后笔直如初。

branches.en: THE MATERIAL AND THE FRAME: a solid that will not bend and a structure that will not sag.
branches.cn: 材料与构架：不肯弯的固体，不会下沉的结构。

branches.en: THE BODY: stiff shoulders, and the clinical sign of a muscle that stays switched on.
branches.cn: 身体：僵住的肩，以及肌肉持续紧张这一临床体征。

branches.en: THE CLOSED MIND: thought that repeats its first answer and cannot turn.
branches.cn: 封闭的头脑：重复第一个答案、转不过弯的思维。

branches.en: THE FROZEN ORDER: a rule without discretion and a ladder with unreachable rungs.
branches.cn: 冻结的秩序：不留裁量权的规则，与横档够不着的阶梯。

branches.en: THE FIXED NUMBER: a wage that will not fall and a body whose distances never change.
branches.cn: 固定不变的数量：降不下来的工资，与距离永不改变的形体。

intro.en: Rigidity is a Latin adjective and noun ending over the verb rigere; unlike elastic, it has a genuine Latin root chain.
intro.cn: rigidity 是拉丁形容词与名词词尾叠加在动词 rigere 上；与 elastic 不同，它有一条真实的拉丁词根链。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer runs rigere, rigidus, -idus, rigor and -itas.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语成分包括 rigere、rigidus、-idus、rigor 与 -itas。

items.example: The noun is the abstract quality behind every concrete use.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是各具体用法背后的抽象性质。

items.example: The verb describes the state, not the act of making.
items.exampleCN: 动词描述状态，而非使之变硬的动作。

items.example: The adjective covers beams and manners alike.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词同时覆盖梁木与态度。

items.example: It builds adjectives of condition.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示状态形容词。

items.example: The noun kept a medical chill as well as a moral strictness.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词既保留医学上的寒战，也保留道德上的严格。

items.example: The suffix makes the adjective into an abstract noun.
items.exampleCN: 词尾把形容词变成抽象名词。

items.example: English took the adjective first.
items.exampleCN: 英语先取形容词。

items.example: The verb names a change of state.
items.exampleCN: 动词命名状态的变化。

items.example: The same root turns into method rather than matter.
items.exampleCN: 同一词根转向方法，而非物质。

latinEntries.structure: Latin verb rigere (rig-; to be stiff)
latinEntries.example: Latin rigere means to be stiff, and its stem gives rigidus.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 rigere 意为发僵，其词干给出 rigidus。

latinEntries.example: Latin rigidus means stiff or hard.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 rigidus 意为僵硬的、硬的。

latinEntries.example: Latin -idus builds adjectives such as fluidus, flowing.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 -idus 构成 fluidus（流动的）这类形容词。

latinEntries.example: It builds rigiditas, the Latin noun behind rigidity.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 它构成 rigiditas，即 rigidity 背后的拉丁名词。

definition_zh: 市场；集市；某种商品的交易领域；销路、需求；股市；行销、推销
definition_en: a place or system in which goods and services are bought and sold, or the willingness of buyers to purchase them
core_image: 清晨的集市街：木棚下摆着成筐的果子，一杆秤搁在摊边，买主与卖主在摊前讨价
scene: 天刚亮，街边木棚下摆满果筐，买卖双方在摊前讨价。 Growers bring their produce to a market where buyers bargain over each crate.
sceneCN: 前半情境：天刚亮，街边木棚下摆满果筐，买卖双方在摊前讨价；句中的 market 指「买卖双方定期相聚的集市场地」（第 1 个义项：作为交易场所的集市）。图中可辨识物件：木棚、果筐、杆秤、写价的木牌。

pos.zh: 市场；集市；交易领域；销路；股市；买方群体
行销；推销；把产品推向市场

senses.title: A place where buyers and sellers meet
senses.titleCN: 买卖双方相聚的集市场地
senses.definition: an open place, often with stalls, where people regularly come together to buy and sell goods
senses.definitionCN: 常设有摊位的露天场所，人们定期在此相聚买卖货物
senses.example: Farmers set up stalls at the weekly market.
senses.exampleCN: 农民每周在集市上摆摊。
senses.why: the Latin noun mercatus named the place and the trading done there, so the word began as a location for exchange.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁名词 mercatus 既指场所也指在那里进行的交易，因此这个词最初就是交换的地点。

senses.title: Trade in one particular commodity
senses.titleCN: 某一种商品的交易领域
senses.definition: the whole body of buying and selling in one commodity or one sector, wherever it happens
senses.definitionCN: 某一种商品或某一部门中全部买卖活动的总和，不论发生在何处
senses.example: The world market for copper tightened last year.
senses.exampleCN: 去年世界铜的交易领域收紧了。
senses.why: the place sense was transferred from a square to a field of trade, so that copper can have a market with no square at all.
senses.whyCN: 场所义从一方广场转移到一片交易领域，于是铜可以有市场，而完全不需要广场。

senses.title: Demand for a product
senses.definition: the number of buyers willing to purchase something, or the absence of such buyers
senses.definitionCN: 愿意购买某物的买者数量，或这类买者的缺乏
senses.example: There is little market for hand-written ledgers now.
senses.exampleCN: 如今手写账簿已没什么销路。
senses.why: without buyers a place of exchange is empty, so the word came to mean the willingness to buy rather than the ground it stands on.
senses.whyCN: 没有买主，交换的场所就是空的，于是这个词转而指购买的意愿，而不是它所在的那块地。

senses.title: The market for shares and securities
senses.definition: the organized exchange on which shares, bonds and currencies are traded, or trading there as a whole
senses.definitionCN: 买卖股票、债券与货币的有组织的交易所，或该处的交易整体
senses.example: Share prices fell across the market before noon.
senses.exampleCN: 午前整个股市的股价都下跌了。
senses.why: a stock exchange is a marketplace in the original sense, only with paper claims instead of crates, so the old word was kept.
senses.whyCN: 证券交易所就是原义上的集市，只是货物换成了纸面权益，旧词因此被沿用。

senses.title: Offered for sale
senses.titleCN: 在售；待售（置于售卖状态）
senses.definition: the state of being available to buy, as in a house that has come onto the market
senses.definitionCN: 处于可供购买的状态，如已挂牌出售的房子
senses.example: The building came onto the market in spring.
senses.exampleCN: 这栋楼在春天挂牌出售。
senses.why: being placed before buyers is the modern equivalent of being carried to the stalls, and the phrase on the market keeps that image.
senses.whyCN: 被摆到买主面前，相当于旧时把货物挑到摊位上，这一短语保留了那个画面。

senses.title: To sell and promote a product
senses.definition: to promote and sell a product by choosing its buyers, its price and the way it is presented
senses.definitionCN: 通过选择买主、定价与呈现方式来推销并卖出产品
senses.example: The firm markets its software to schools.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司把软件行销给学校。
senses.why: if a market is where goods find buyers, then to market is to do the work of bringing goods and buyers together.
senses.whyCN: 如果市场是货物找到买主的地方，那么行销就是把货物与买主带到一起的工作。

senses.title: The mechanism that sets prices
senses.definition: the system in which prices and quantities are settled by the competing decisions of many buyers and sellers
senses.definitionCN: 价格与数量由众多买卖双方的竞争性决定来敲定的系统
senses.example: The market, not the ministry, decides which suppliers survive.
senses.exampleCN: 决定哪些供应商存活的是市场，而不是部委。
senses.why: abstracting the place away leaves only its function: bringing competing offers together until a price emerges.
senses.whyCN: 把场所抽掉，只剩它的功能：把互相竞争的报价汇集起来，直到价格出现。

senses.title: The body of intended buyers
senses.definition: the group of people or institutions a seller intends to reach, considered as a whole
senses.definitionCN: 卖方打算触及的那一群人或机构，被作为一个整体来看
senses.example: The brand's market is young urban readers.
senses.exampleCN: 这个品牌的目标买方群体是年轻的城市读者。
senses.why: a seller who studies the crowd at the stalls ends by treating that crowd as an object to be served, which is the marketing sense.
senses.whyCN: 研究摊位前人群的卖方，最终把那群人当作服务对象，这就是营销义。

intro.en: Market is Latin in origin, not a native English word: it goes back to Latin mercatus 'market, trading', a noun from the verb mercari 'to trade', which in turn rests on merx (genitive mercis) 'goods'. It reached Old English through Old Northern French and Germanic channels. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: market 是拉丁来源，而非英语本族词：它上溯至拉丁名词 mercatus「市场、集市、交易」，该名词出自动词 mercari「做买卖」，而动词又基于 merx（属格 mercis）「货物」。它经古北法语与日耳曼中介进入古英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Merx, genitive mercis, meant 'goods, merchandise'. Its own deeper origin is uncertain, and no pre-Latin source can be demonstrated.
items.cn: merx（属格 mercis）意为「货物、商品」。它自身更深的来源不确定，无法证明任何拉丁语之前的源头。

items.en: From the noun came the deponent verb mercari 'to buy and sell, to trade', which names the activity rather than the goods.
items.cn: 由这个名词产生异态动词 mercari「买卖、做交易」，命名的是活动而非货物。

items.en: The noun mercatus 'market, marketplace, trading' was formed on the same stem, so place and activity were one word from the start.
items.cn: 名词 mercatus「市场、集市、交易」由同一词干构成，因此场所与活动从一开始就是一个词。

items.en: The form market is generally thought to have come to England through Old Northern French, with Germanic channels also involved in its spread.
items.cn: 一般认为 market 这一形式经古北法语传入英格兰，其传播也涉及日耳曼中介。

items.en: Old English already had market as a loanword, which is why the word counts as Latin in origin rather than as an inherited native term.
items.cn: 古英语已经以借词形式拥有 market，因此这个词算作拉丁来源，而非承继的本族词。

items.en: From the physical fair the word widened to trade in one commodity, to demand, to the share market and finally to the verb for promoting goods.
items.cn: 从有形的集市出发，这个词扩展到单一商品的交易、需求、股票市场，最后扩展到推销货物的动词义。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same Latin root, so their kinship is real and can be traced; group two holds near neighbours that all name places or gatherings for trade.
note.cn: 第一组的词同出拉丁词根，亲缘关系真实可溯；第二组是同样指交易场所或聚会的近邻词。

entries.definition: Through Old French from Latin mercari: a person who trades, so it shares the root for 'goods' with market and adds an agent suffix.
entries.definitionCN: 经古法语来自拉丁 mercari：做买卖的人，与本词同出「货物」这一词根，只多了一个施事后缀。

entries.definition: From merx 'goods' through Old French: the goods themselves, which is the root meaning in concrete form.
entries.definitionCN: 经古法语来自 merx「货物」：货物本身，正是该词根的具体形态。

entries.definition: From Italian mercante, from Latin mercari: relating to trade, a later borrowing of the same root rather than a new coinage.
entries.definitionCN: 经意大利语来自拉丁 mercari：关于贸易的，是同一词根的后期借入，而非新造词。

entries.definition: Com- 'together' plus merx: trade viewed as an organized exchange between parties, another descendant of the same root.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语中表示「共同」的前缀加 merx：把贸易看作各方之间有组织的交换，是同一词根的另一支后裔。

entries.definition: Market plus place: the square or platform where trading happens, narrower than market because it has no demand or share-price senses.
entries.definitionCN: 由 market 与表示「地方」的成分复合而成：发生交易的广场或平台，比本词窄，因为不含需求与股价等义。

entries.definition: From Latin feria 'holiday': a periodic, often seasonal gathering for trade, with none of the abstract economic senses of market.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 feria「节日」：定期、常为季节性的交易聚会，不含本词那些抽象经济义。

entries.definition: From Persian through Turkish: a covered street of shops, a place word only and never a verb.
entries.definitionCN: 经土耳其语来自波斯语：有顶棚的店铺街，只作场所词，从不用作动词。

entries.definition: A shortened form of market kept for names and poetry; it retains only the place sense.
entries.definitionCN: market 的缩略形式，多用于名称与诗歌，只保留场所义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives rather than invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The chain runs goods, then trade, then place: merx, mercari, mercatus.
normal.cn: 链条是货物、交易、场所：merx、mercari、mercatus。

normal.en: The family runs market, marketing, marketplace, marketer, marketable, marketization.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 market、marketing、marketplace、marketer、marketable、marketization。

normal.en: Fixed phrases separate the senses: on the market, market share, market forces, stock market.
normal.cn: 固定搭配分开各个义项：在售、市场份额、市场力量、股票市场。

normal.en: The same root shows in merchant, merchandise, mercantile and commerce.
normal.cn: 同一词根出现在 merchant、merchandise、mercantile 与 commerce 中。

normal.en: The verb takes an object: to market a product, and the -ing form is the noun marketing.
normal.cn: 动词要带宾语：把产品行销出去，其动名词形式就是名词「营销」。

abstract.en: Picture a square that is crowded at dawn and swept clean by noon.
abstract.cn: 想象一方广场，黎明时挤满人，到正午已被扫空。

abstract.en: Picture two columns on a page: what buyers want, and what they will pay.
abstract.cn: 想象纸页上两栏：买主想要什么，愿意付多少。

abstract.en: Picture a board of share prices where one company's fate becomes a single flashing number.
abstract.cn: 想象一块股价牌，一家公司的命运变成一个闪动的数字。

examples.en: The fishing market opens before sunrise and is empty by noon.
examples.cn: 鱼市在日出前开张，到正午便空了。

examples.en: A product with no market cannot survive, however carefully it is made.
examples.cn: 无论做得多用心，没有销路的产品都活不下去。

examples.en: The cooperative markets its coffee directly to roasters abroad.
examples.cn: 这家合作社把咖啡直接行销给国外的烘焙商。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马克」的谐音——集市上每件货物都用马克笔标上价钱 → 市场

root: 拉丁 merx（属格 mercis）「货物」→ 动词 mercari「做买卖」→ 名词 mercatus「市场、集市、交易」→ 经古北法语与日耳曼中介借入古英语 market；merx 更深来源不确定，故为拉丁来源而非英语本族词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one building: goods (merx) are traded (mercari) in a place (mercatus). From the dawn square the line moves to trade in a single commodity, to the demand that fills or empties the square, to the share market that inherited the name, to the state of being offered for sale, to the verb that brings goods and buyers together, to the price-setting mechanism abstracted from the square, and finally to the crowd of buyers a seller sets out to serve.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一座建筑展开：货物在某个场所里被交易。从黎明时的广场出发，这条线依次走向单一商品的交易、决定广场空与满的需求、继承了这个名称的股票市场、被摆出来售卖的状态、把货物与买主带到一起的动词、从广场抽象出来的定价机制，最后走向卖方打算服务的那群买主。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dawn market square where crates change hands and the crowd thins by noon.
core.cn: 核心意象：黎明的集市广场，成筐货物易手，到正午人群渐散。

branches.en: PLACE AND COMMODITY: a square for exchange becomes a field of trade in one good.
branches.cn: 场所与商品：用于交换的广场变成某一种商品的交易领域。

branches.en: DEMAND AND SHARES: buyers make the square alive, and paper claims inherit its name.
branches.cn: 需求与证券：买主让广场有生气，纸面权益则继承了它的名称。

branches.en: OFFER AND PROMOTE: goods are placed before buyers, and someone must bring them there.
branches.cn: 摆出与推销：货物被摆到买主面前，而总得有人把它们带到那里。

branches.en: ALLOCATION: strip away the square and what remains is a mechanism that settles prices.
branches.cn: 配置：把广场抽走，剩下的就是一个敲定价格的机制。

branches.en: BUYER GROUP: the crowd at the stalls becomes the audience a seller intends to reach.
branches.cn: 买方群体：摊位前的人群变成卖方打算触及的对象。

intro.en: The word is a Latin root for 'goods' dressed in noun and verb endings, with English suffixes building the modern family on top.
intro.cn: 这个词是「货物」这一拉丁词根加上名词与动词词尾，再由英语后缀在其上搭起现代词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin merx and its verb mercari supply the stem; mercatus, the noun of place and activity, is the direct ancestor of the English word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 merx 及其动词 mercari 提供词干；指场所与活动的名词 mercatus 则是英语这个词的直接祖先。

items.example: The root supplies the idea of goods in every member of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根为词族中每个成员提供「货物」这一观念。

items.example: Merx names what is carried to the stalls.
items.exampleCN: merx 指被挑到摊位上的东西。

items.structure: mercari, mercatus sum (Latin deponent verb, first conjugation)
items.meaning: to trade, to buy and sell
items.example: The verb turns goods into an activity.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把货物变成一种活动。

items.example: The noun carries both the place and the dealing.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词同时承载场所与交易。

items.meaning: a place or system of exchange
items.example: Old English already used the borrowed noun.
items.exampleCN: 古英语已经使用这个借入的名词。

items.example: The compound keeps only the place sense.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词只保留场所义。

items.example: Marketing grew out of the verb to market.
items.exampleCN: 营销由动词「行销」发展而来。

items.meaning: the process or activity of doing
items.example: The suffix turns the verb into a trade activity.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词变成一种行业活动。

items.example: Only marketable varieties reached the stalls.
items.exampleCN: 只有可销售的品种被送上摊位。

items.example: The suffix marks what can be sold.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀标出能够被卖出之物。

latinEntries.structure: mercari, mercatus sum (deponent verb, first conjugation)
latinEntries.meaning: to trade, to buy and sell

definition_zh: 理论模型；理论模式；概念框架；（物理、经济等领域的）数学化理论构造
definition_en: a simplified formal representation of a system, built from theory, that is used to explain or predict its behaviour
core_image: 一块透明板上画着几条相互连接的圆圈，真实世界的杂乱被简化成清晰的路径
scene: 工程师还没下钻，先在纸上画出含水层的层数与流向，用来估算压力会怎样变化。 The team built a theoretical model of the aquifer before drilling the first well.
sceneCN: 这里指用理论构造出的简化表示（第 1 个义项：理论模型、概念框架）；句意为团队在钻第一口井之前先建了一个含水层的理论模型。场景图取象：透明板上几条相互连接的圆圈，把杂乱简化成清晰路径。

pos.zh: 理论模型；理论模式
（物理、化学的）数学模型化构造
（经济学的）理论分析框架
概念框架；用以指导研究的简化图式

collocations.phrase: the limits of a theoretical model

derivatives.zh: 理论；学说（出自希腊语「观看、旁观」，从「看的方式」转为「解释体系」）
理论的；理论上的（加表示「与……有关」的形容词后缀）
理论家（加表示「从事者」的名词后缀）
模型；模式；模仿（出自拉丁语「小尺度」，从量具转为缩小的代表物）
建模；模型制作（加表示「行为、过程」的词尾，指构造模型的工作）
作理论推演；建立理论（加表示「使成为」的动词词尾）

senses.title: A simplified representation
senses.definition: a deliberately simplified representation of a system, built to make its behaviour easier to reason about
senses.definitionCN: 对一个系统有意作出的简化表示，使其行为更容易推理
senses.example: The team built a theoretical model of the aquifer before drilling the first well.
senses.exampleCN: 团队在钻第一口井之前先建了一个含水层的理论模型。
senses.why: A model is a small measure of a large thing, and theory supplies the shape that the measurement takes.
senses.whyCN: 模型是对大事物的小尺度代表，而理论提供这次量取所采取的形状。

senses.title: A mathematical construction
senses.definition: a set of equations or formal assumptions that generates predictions about a system
senses.definitionCN: 一组方程或形式化假设，能对某系统生成预测
senses.example: The theoretical model reduces the climate to three variables.
senses.exampleCN: 这个理论模型把气候简化成三个变量。
senses.why: Equations make a model precise enough to be wrong, which is what a theory needs.
senses.whyCN: 方程让模型精确到足以出错，而这正是理论所需要的。

senses.title: A physicist's working picture
senses.definition: a standard construct in physics that organizes known behaviour and guides new experiments
senses.definitionCN: 物理学中组织已知行为、指导新实验的标准构造
senses.example: The standard theoretical model of the atom treats electrons as waves.
senses.exampleCN: 原子的标准理论模型把电子当作波。
senses.why: Physics often cannot see its objects directly, so a model stands in and is tested by its predictions.
senses.whyCN: 物理学常常看不到对象本身，于是让模型代为站立，用预测来检验它。

senses.title: An economic framework
senses.definition: a formal framework of assumptions in economics used to analyse choices, markets or growth
senses.definitionCN: 经济学中一套形式化假设，用于分析选择、市场或增长
senses.example: The theoretical model assumes that buyers know all prices.
senses.exampleCN: 这个理论模型假设买方知道所有价格。
senses.why: Economics builds from stated assumptions, and the model is the place where they are made visible.
senses.whyCN: 经济学从明说的假设出发，模型正是这些假设显形的地方。

senses.title: Untested theory, not yet data
senses.titleCN: 尚未受数据检验的理论
senses.definition: a model that has been constructed but not yet checked against observation
senses.definitionCN: 已经建好、但尚未对照观测检验的模型
senses.example: The paper's contribution is still a theoretical model, not a result.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇论文的贡献仍是一个理论模型，而不是一个结果。
senses.why: The adjective marks the gap between a construction and a finding, a distinction reviewers guard.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词标出构造与发现之间的空隙，审稿人对此看得很紧。

senses.title: A simulation's basis
senses.definition: the theoretical core on which a computer simulation or forecast is built
senses.definitionCN: 计算机模拟或预报所依托的理论内核
senses.example: The forecast runs on a theoretical model of ocean currents.
senses.exampleCN: 这份预报运行在一个洋流的理论模型之上。
senses.why: Simulation adds computation to theory; the model is what the machine is told to obey.
senses.whyCN: 模拟是在理论上加计算，模型就是机器被要求服从的那套东西。

senses.title: A guide for experiment
senses.definition: a model used to decide which measurements matter and what result would count as support
senses.definitionCN: 用来决定哪些测量要紧、什么结果算支持模型的框架
senses.example: The theoretical model told them which two temperatures to test.
senses.exampleCN: 这个理论模型告诉他们该测哪两个温度。
senses.why: A model that predicts nothing specific cannot guide a bench, so usefulness is its own test.
senses.whyCN: 什么具体结果都预测不出的模型指导不了实验台，因此有用本身就是一种检验。

senses.title: A model known to be wrong
senses.titleCN: 明知不完美却仍有用的模型
senses.definition: a simplified model accepted despite known inaccuracies, because it explains enough
senses.definitionCN: 明知不准确却仍被接受的简化模型，因为它解释得够用
senses.example: Every theoretical model is wrong somewhere, but some are useful.
senses.exampleCN: 每个理论模型都在某处是错的，但有些仍然有用。
senses.why: The purpose is explanation, not mimicry; a map the size of the country would be useless.
senses.whyCN: 目的是解释而非复制；一张与国土等大的地图反而没有用。

intro.en: Theoretical model joins Greek theoria, 'a looking or viewing', with Latin modulus, 'a small measure'. Both halves are well documented; the compound is a modern scientific phrase.
intro.cn: theoretical model 把希腊语 theoria「观看」与拉丁语 modulus「小尺度」合在一起。两半来源都有充分记录，这个复合词是现代科学用语。

items.en: Theoria meant a viewing or a spectacle, and it named the act of looking at something for understanding rather than for use.
items.cn: theoria 意为观看、景象，指为理解而非为实用去看一件事。

items.en: The related word for a spectator or envoy shows the root idea of someone sent to watch, which gives theory its air of distance.
items.cn: 相关的「观看者、使者」一词显出「被派去看」的词根意象，理论由此带上距离感。

items.en: Modulus meant a small measure, from modus, a measure or manner, and it survives in module and model.
items.cn: modulus 意为小尺度，出自 modus「尺度、方式」，在 module 与 model 中留存。

items.en: English took theory in the sixteenth century, first for a scheme of ideas and later for an explanation of observed facts.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入 theory，先指一套观念，后指对观测事实的解释。

items.en: By the eighteenth century model meant a small copy of a thing, and by the nineteenth a formal representation of a system.
items.cn: 到十八世纪，model 指事物的小型复制品；到十九世纪，指系统的形式化表示。

items.en: The phrase theoretical model became standard in twentieth-century physics and economics, where construction precedes measurement.
items.cn: 二十世纪，这一短语在物理与经济学中成为标准说法，那里构造先于测量。

note.en: The first group shares one of the two roots or looks close; the second group holds the neighbouring constructs that are often called models by mistake.
note.cn: 第一组或共享两个词根之一，或字形相近；第二组是常被误称为模型的邻近构造。

entries.definition: A system of explanation, the first half of the phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 一套解释体系，是词组的前一半。

entries.definition: Concerning theory rather than practice or measurement.
entries.definitionCN: 关涉理论而非实践或测量。

entries.definition: A simplified representation or a small copy.
entries.definitionCN: 简化的表示或小型复制品。

entries.definition: The activity of building models, now mostly computational.
entries.definitionCN: 构建模型的活动，如今多指计算建模。

entries.definition: Healing; it shares a Greek shape but comes from a verb meaning to attend or serve.
entries.definitionCN: 有疗愈作用的；希腊词形相近，词根却意为照料、服务。

entries.definition: An organised set of ideas that guides research, often less formal than a model.
entries.definitionCN: 指导研究的一套有组织的观念，通常不如模型形式化。

entries.definition: A running computation of a model over time, the model put to work.
entries.definitionCN: 让模型随时间运行的计算，是模型被投入使用。

entries.definition: A single testable proposal, smaller than a model and easier to kill.
entries.definitionCN: 单个可检验的提议，比模型小，也更容易被推翻。

entries.definition: A supporting structure of ideas, which may not generate predictions.
entries.definitionCN: 支撑性的观念结构，未必能生成预测。

entries.definition: A whole way of working within a field, larger than any single model.
entries.definitionCN: 一个领域内整套工作方式，比任何单个模型都大。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Greek viewing root, the real Latin measure word and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的希腊「观看」词根、真实的拉丁「尺度」词与真实固定搭配。

normal.en: Theoria is a viewing, modulus is a small measure, so a theoretical model is a small measured picture of something too large to see.
normal.cn: 前者是观看，后者是小尺度，合起来就是用缩小尺寸画出的图，去看太大的东西。

normal.en: The family runs theory, theoretical, theorist, model, modelling and module.
normal.cn: 同族词有 theory、theoretical、theorist、model、modelling 与 module。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: build a theoretical model, test a theoretical model, the limits of a model.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出用法：建立理论模型、检验理论模型、模型的限度。

normal.en: The plural is theoretical models, because the head noun is model.
normal.cn: 复数是 theoretical models，因为中心词是 model。

normal.en: A model that predicts nothing specific cannot guide an experiment.
normal.cn: 预测不出具体结果的模型，指导不了实验。

abstract.en: A theoretical model is a promise that the mess can be written down in fewer lines.
abstract.cn: 理论模型是一个承诺：这团杂乱能用更少的几行写下来。

abstract.en: Its usefulness and its falseness are often the same property seen from two sides.
abstract.cn: 它的有用与它的错误，常常是同一性质的两面。

abstract.en: Every model is a small lie told in order to tell a large truth.
abstract.cn: 每个模型都是一个为了说出大真相而撒的小谎。

examples.en: The theoretical model predicted a rise that the data later confirmed.
examples.cn: 理论模型预言了一次上升，数据后来证实了它。

examples.en: Without a theoretical model, the measurements were just numbers.
examples.cn: 没有理论模型，那些测量只是一堆数字。

examples.en: The theoretical model deliberately ignores friction to keep the equations simple.
examples.cn: 这个理论模型有意忽略摩擦，以保持方程简单。

dict_mnemonic.text: 记作「看的方式＋小尺度」——把大东西缩小画成图，再用理论去看：理论模型

root: theoretical（希腊语 theoria「观看」＋形容词词尾）＋ model（拉丁语 modulus「小尺度」← modus「尺度、方式」）。两词在二十世纪的物理与经济学中合成固定短语，指先构造、后测量的形式化表示。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one construction: a simplified picture, equations, a physicist's working image, an economic framework, untested theory, a simulation's core, a guide for experiment, and a model known to be wrong.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着同一种构造：简化的图景、方程、物理学家的作业图像、经济学框架、未经检验的理论、模拟的内核、实验的指南，以及明知有错的模型。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a transparent sheet with linked circles on it, standing in for a tangle it cannot copy.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块透明板上画着相连的圆圈，代替它复制不了的乱麻。

branches.en: THE PICTURE THAT STANDS IN: a simplified image of a system, including a physicist's working drawing of the atom.
branches.cn: 代为站立的图：系统的简化图像，包括物理学家关于原子的作业图。

branches.en: THE EQUATIONS AND THE RUN: formal assumptions that generate numbers, and the simulation built on them.
branches.cn: 方程与运行：生成数字的形式假设，以及建在其上的模拟。

branches.en: THE ECONOMIC FRAMEWORK: assumptions about buyers and prices made visible on one page.
branches.cn: 经济学框架：关于买方与价格的假设，在一页纸上显形。

branches.en: THE GAP FROM FACT: a construction not yet tested, and a model accepted although known to be wrong.
branches.cn: 与事实的间距：尚未受检的构造，以及明知有错仍被接受的模型。

branches.en: THE GUIDE: a model that decides which measurement matters.
branches.cn: 指南：决定哪一项测量要紧的模型。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Greek noun of viewing and a Latin noun of measuring, both of which have large English families.
intro.cn: 这个短语把希腊的「观看」名词与拉丁的「量度」名词合在一起，两者在英语中都有大词族。

latinIntro.en: Theoria and modulus are the two sources; the endings -ical and -el came through Latin and French forms.
latinIntro.cn: theoria 与 modulus 是两个来源，-ical 与 -el 词尾经由拉丁与法语形态而来。

items.example: The phrase names a construction, not a measurement.
items.exampleCN: 这个短语指一种构造，而非一次测量。

items.example: It gives theory its air of looking rather than doing.
items.exampleCN: 它给理论带上观看而非动手的意味。

items.meaning: a spectator, an envoy sent to watch
items.meaningCN: 观看者；被派去看的使者
items.example: The root image is someone watching from a distance.
items.exampleCN: 词根意象是从远处观看的人。

items.example: It builds theoretical, practical and medical.
items.exampleCN: 它构成理论的、实践的和医学的等词。

items.example: It also gives mode and moderate.
items.exampleCN: 它还给出 mode 与 moderate。

items.example: The diminutive makes the model a small version of a large thing.
items.exampleCN: 指小形式让模型成为大事物的小版本。

items.example: It survives in model, a small copy.
items.exampleCN: 它留存在 model 中，指小型复制品。

items.example: It builds modelling, the work of making models.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 modelling，即建模工作。

items.example: It builds theorist, a maker of theory.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 theorist，即理论制造者。

latinEntries.structure: Greek theoria (a viewing), borrowed into Latin
latinEntries.example: Greek theoria means a viewing or contemplation.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 希腊语 theoria 意为观看、沉思。

latinEntries.example: Latin modulus means a small measure.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 modulus 意为小尺度。

latinEntries.example: Latin modus means measure or manner, and gives English mode.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 modus 意为尺度、方式，并给出英语 mode。

definition_zh: 限制；约束；限制条件；约束力；强制
definition_en: a limit or restriction that reduces what a person, system or design may do, or the force that imposes such a limit
core_image: 四根拉索把箱体四角拴在台面夹具上，绳索绷紧，箱角留下勒痕
scene: 装配台上，四根拉索把箱体拴在夹具里，往任何一边推都会被绳子拽回原位。 A tight budget is the main constraint on the project.
sceneCN: 这里指资源上的限制（第 3 个义项：时间、资金或人力不足造成的限制）；句意为紧张的预算是这个项目最主要的限制。图中可辨识物件：箱体、四根拉索、夹具、台面、勒痕。

pos.zh: 限制；约束；限制条件；约束力；强制

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语 constringere 经法语而来，义为「限制；强迫」
由限制动词加已然词尾构成，义为「受限制的；勉强的」
由限制动词加现在分词词尾构成，义为「造成限制的」
由表示「向后」的前缀加同一拉丁词根构成，义为「抑制；约束」
由表示「共同」的前缀加同一拉丁词根构成，义为「压缩；收紧」

senses.title: A limit on what is possible
senses.definition: a condition that narrows the range of actions or outcomes available
senses.definitionCN: 缩小可选行动或结果范围的条件
senses.example: Funding is the constraint that decides the scope of the trial.
senses.exampleCN: 资金是决定试验规模的那个限制。
senses.why: The word begins with a rope pulled tight, and any limit draws the same boundary around action.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从一根绷紧的绳子开始，任何限制都在行动周围画出同样的边界。

senses.title: An imposed rule or condition
senses.definition: an external rule, permit condition or legal requirement that must be obeyed
senses.definitionCN: 必须遵守的外部规则、许可条件或法律要求
senses.example: The permit imposes a constraint on how much water may be drawn.
senses.exampleCN: 许可证对可取水量施加了一项限制。
senses.why: An authority binds behaviour by writing conditions, and the word names that binding.
senses.whyCN: 主管方用书面条件来绑定行为，这个词指的就是这种绑定。

senses.title: A shortage of time, money or staff
senses.definition: a practical scarcity that limits what a project can attempt within its resources
senses.definitionCN: 使项目在现有资源内只能做到某一步的现实短缺
senses.example: Time is the tightest constraint in the fieldwork season.
senses.exampleCN: 野外工作季里最紧的限制是时间。
senses.why: Resources are ropes of a different material: they pull the plan back whenever it tries to expand.
senses.whyCN: 资源是另一种材质的绳子：方案一想扩张，它就把方案拽回来。

senses.title: Physical restraint
senses.definition: a device or force that keeps a body or object from moving freely
senses.definitionCN: 使身体或物体无法自由移动的装置或力量
senses.example: A physical constraint kept the patient's arm from moving.
senses.exampleCN: 一项物理约束使病人的手臂无法移动。
senses.why: This is the literal sense: something is tied, and the tie is visible.
senses.whyCN: 这是字面义：某物被拴住，而拴住它的东西看得见。

senses.title: A condition in mathematics or optimization
senses.titleCN: 数学或优化中的约束条件
senses.definition: an equation or inequality that a solution must satisfy
senses.definitionCN: 求解结果必须满足的等式或不等式
senses.example: The model adds a constraint that total cost must stay below budget.
senses.exampleCN: 模型增加了一条约束：总成本必须低于预算。
senses.why: In optimization the search space is cut by conditions, and the solution exists only inside the cut.
senses.whyCN: 在优化中，条件把搜索空间切开，解只存在于切出的范围内。

senses.title: An engineering or design limit
senses.definition: a fixed limit on weight, size, temperature, cost or performance that a design must respect
senses.definitionCN: 设计在重量、尺寸、温度、成本或性能上必须遵守的固定界限
senses.example: Every design faces a constraint on weight and size.
senses.exampleCN: 每一项设计都面对重量与尺寸的限制。
senses.why: An engineer works between limits rather than in open space, and the limits are named as constraints.
senses.whyCN: 工程师是在界限之间而非空地上工作，这些界限就叫约束。

senses.title: Compulsion that forces action
senses.definition: pressure or obligation that leaves a person no acceptable alternative
senses.definitionCN: 使人别无合宜选择而只能照做的压力或义务
senses.example: A legal constraint compelled the firm to release the records.
senses.exampleCN: 一项法律强制力迫使该公司交出记录。
senses.why: A binding can also be applied to a person's will, not only to a body, and then it means compulsion.
senses.whyCN: 绳索也可以绑在人的意志上而不只是身体上，这时它指强制。

senses.title: A structural limit on freedom
senses.definition: a social, economic or institutional condition that restricts choices without any single visible rule
senses.definitionCN: 没有单一可见规则却限制选择的社会、经济或制度条件
senses.example: Social constraint can keep a group from questioning a familiar practice.
senses.exampleCN: 社会约束可以使一个群体不去质疑熟悉的做法。
senses.why: Some limits are not written anywhere yet still hold people in place, and the word covers those too.
senses.whyCN: 有些限制哪里都没写，却仍把人固定在原地，这个词也涵盖这些情况。

intro.en: Constraint comes from Latin constringere, to bind tightly, from con- together and stringere to draw tight. Old French passed the noun to English.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语 constringere「紧紧捆绑」，由 con-「一起」与 stringere「拉紧」构成，经古法语名词进入英语。

items.en: Stringere meant to draw tight, to bind or to touch lightly; the rope image is original.
items.cn: stringere 意为拉紧、捆绑或轻触，绳索意象就是它的本义。

items.en: Con- added the idea of binding together, so the verb meant to squeeze or confine from all sides.
items.cn: con- 加入「捆在一起」的意思，这个动词于是指从四面挤压或收束。

items.en: The noun named a drawing together, whether of a rope, a wound or a rule.
items.cn: 名词指收束、紧缩，无论对象是绳索、伤口还是规则。

items.en: Old French kept the verb for compulsion and restraint, and the noun constreinte followed.
items.cn: 古法语保留了这个动词的强迫与约束义，名词 constreinte 随之出现。

items.en: English borrowed the noun for a restriction or a forced condition; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语借入这个名词表示限制或被迫的条件；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Engineering, law and optimization each gave the word a precise local meaning without changing the rope image.
items.cn: 工程、法律与优化各自赋予这个词精确的局部含义，却没有改变绳索意象。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like constraint; the second group names neighbouring ideas of limiting and pressure.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与 constraint 相近；第二组是与「限制、压力」意思相邻的说法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations work through the real parts, word family and common phrases behind this term.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想依托这个术语背后真实的构词部件、同族词与常见搭配。

normal.en: The Latin verb means to tie tight, so every constraint begins as a rope around something.
normal.cn: 拉丁动词意为紧紧拴住，因此每一种约束最初都是绕在某物上的一根绳。

normal.en: Time, budget and staff are the three ropes that most often pull a project back.
normal.cn: 时间、预算与人手是最常把项目拽回的三根绳。

normal.en: A constraint in a model is an equation the answer must satisfy.
normal.cn: 模型中的约束是答案必须满足的一条等式。

normal.en: Constrained and restraint share the same root but different prefixes, one binding with, one holding back.
normal.cn: 「受限制的」与「抑制」共享词根但前缀不同，一个是捆在一起，一个是往回拉住。

normal.en: An engineering constraint is written into the specification before the first part is made.
normal.cn: 工程约束在第一个零件做出之前就写进规格书。

abstract.en: A constraint is a wall that does not need to be seen to be felt.
abstract.cn: 约束是一堵不必看见也能感觉到的墙。

abstract.en: Every free choice is drawn on a map whose edges were set by someone else.
abstract.cn: 每一次自由选择都画在一张由别人定好边界的地图上。

abstract.en: The tighter the rope, the clearer the shape; limits can make a design legible.
abstract.cn: 绳拉得越紧，形状越清楚；限制反而能让设计变得可读。

examples.en: The team treated cost as a constraint rather than a variable.
examples.cn: 团队把成本当作约束而非变量。

examples.en: A constraint on the sample size limited how many subgroups could be compared.
examples.cn: 样本量的限制决定了能比较多少个子组。

examples.en: The court's constraint required the company to change its disclosure practice.
examples.cn: 法院的强制要求迫使公司改变披露做法。

root: 拉丁 constringere「捆紧」← con-「一起」+ stringere「拉紧」；名词经古法语 constreinte 进入英语，本义为捆绑，后扩展到规则、资源、数学条件与强制。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the rope outward: a general limit, an imposed rule, resource scarcity, physical restraint, a mathematical condition, an engineering limit, compulsion, and a structural limit on freedom.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从绳子向外扩展：一般限制、外加规定、资源短缺、身体约束、数学条件、工程界限、强制力，以及对自由的结构性束缚。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: four ropes pull a box tight against a fixture, so that every push is answered by a pull back.
core.cn: 核心意象：四根绳把箱体紧紧拉在夹具上，任何一推都会被一拉回应。

branches.en: THE PRACTICAL BOUNDARY: a general limit and the scarcity of time or money.
branches.cn: 现实边界：一般限制与时间、资金的短缺。

branches.en: THE WRITTEN BINDING: a rule or permit condition that must be obeyed.
branches.cn: 书面绑定：必须遵守的规则或许可条件。

branches.en: THE LITERAL RESTRAINT: a body or object physically held.
branches.cn: 字面约束：身体或物体被物理地固定。

branches.en: THE TECHNICAL LIMIT: conditions inside a model and limits inside a design.
branches.cn: 技术界限：模型内的条件与设计内的界限。

branches.en: THE PRESSURE ON WILL AND SOCIAL POSITION: compulsion, and unwritten structural limits.
branches.cn: 对意志与处境的压力：强制，以及未写明的结构性限制。

definition_en: the activity or skill of writing computer programs, the programs so written, or the arranging of a schedule

senses.title: Writing code as an activity
senses.definition: the work of writing, testing and correcting the instructions a computer runs
senses.definitionCN: 编写、测试与修正计算机所执行指令的工作
senses.example: Programming takes patience as much as mathematical skill.
senses.exampleCN: 编程需要的耐心不亚于数学能力。
senses.why: the gerund turns the product into a process, so the word names the doing rather than the finished code.
senses.whyCN: 动名词把成品变成过程，因此这个词命名的是「做」这件事，而不是写好的代码。

senses.title: The code already written
senses.definition: the programs held by a machine or a system, taken as a body of code
senses.definitionCN: 机器或系统里所存程序的总和，被当作一整套代码
senses.example: The programming on that old machine is out of date.
senses.exampleCN: 那台旧机器里的程序已经过时了。
senses.why: English often uses a gerund for a collective product, as in clothing or building, and code stored in a device is treated the same way.
senses.whyCN: 英语常用动名词指集合性的产物，如衣物、建筑，存放在设备里的代码也这样处理。

senses.title: The field of study
senses.definition: the discipline taught in schools and researched as a subject in its own right
senses.definitionCN: 在学校教授、并作为独立学科被研究的领域
senses.example: She teaches programming to first-year engineering students.
senses.exampleCN: 她给一年级工科学生教编程。
senses.why: once the activity acquired methods and a body of theory, the gerund became the name of a school subject.
senses.whyCN: 当这项活动有了方法与理论体系，动名词就成了课程名称。

senses.title: Arranging a schedule of events
senses.definition: the planning work that decides which events happen and in what order
senses.definitionCN: 决定哪些活动举行、按什么顺序进行的设计工作
senses.example: Festival programming begins a full year before the first concert.
senses.exampleCN: 音乐节的节目编排在第一场音乐会前整整一年就开始了。
senses.why: this is the older, non-computing sense: a person programs a season by deciding its order, without any machine involved.
senses.whyCN: 这是更早的非计算机义：人通过决定顺序来编排一个演出季，完全不涉及机器。

senses.title: Planning what a channel airs
senses.definition: the work of choosing and ordering the shows a station broadcasts
senses.definitionCN: 挑选并安排电台或电视台播出节目的工作
senses.example: Channel programming now reacts to what viewers watch live.
senses.exampleCN: 频道编排如今会随观众实时观看的情况调整。
senses.why: broadcasting kept the scheduling sense and gave it a permanent home in the industry.
senses.whyCN: 广播保留了「排顺序」这层意思，并让它在行业里安了家。

senses.title: Setting a device's timed actions
senses.definition: entering times and conditions so that a device acts automatically
senses.definitionCN: 输入时间与条件，使设备自动动作
senses.example: The programming of the heating system took only a few minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 给供暖系统做设定只花了几分钟。
senses.why: a timer also holds a small plan, so the gerund covers the act of loading that plan.
senses.whyCN: 定时器也存着一份小计划，因此动名词也涵盖装入这份计划的动作。

senses.title: Instructing a non-computer machine
senses.definition: writing the control sequence for a robot, a lathe or other industrial machine
senses.definitionCN: 为机器人、车床或其他工业机器编写控制序列
senses.example: Robot programming now uses visual blocks instead of typed lines.
senses.exampleCN: 机器人编程如今用可视化积木而不是敲代码行。
senses.why: the machine does not need to be a general computer for the same word to apply, as long as it follows a written sequence.
senses.whyCN: 机器不必是通用计算机，只要它遵循写好的序列，同一个词就照样适用。

senses.title: Behaviour built into a device
senses.definition: the fixed sequence of responses designed into a product
senses.definitionCN: 产品中被设计好的固定反应序列
senses.example: The toy's programming makes it sing whenever it is shaken.
senses.exampleCN: 这个玩具的内置程序使它一被摇动就唱歌。
senses.why: when the sequence is sealed inside a product, the gerund names the behaviour rather than the writing of it.
senses.whyCN: 当序列被封在产品内部，动名词指的就是行为本身，而不是编写它的过程。

intro.en: Programming is English through and through: the Greek-derived noun program plus the English gerund ending -ing. Its scheduling sense is older than its computing sense. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: programming 是地道的英语构词：希腊来源的名词 program 加英语动名词词尾 -ing。它的「排日程」义比计算机义更早。年代均为约数。

items.en: The base noun program goes back to Greek programma, a public written notice built from pro-, before, and graphein, to write.
items.cn: 基础名词 program 可追到希腊语 programma「公开书面通告」，由 pro-「在前」与 graphein「书写」构成。

items.en: The ending -ing is native English: it turns a verb into the name of its activity, and it has done so since Old English.
items.cn: 词尾 -ing 是英语本族语素：它把动词变成该活动的名称，这一用法自上古英语时期就有。

items.en: In the nineteenth century programming meant drawing up the programme of a concert, a season or a course, with no reference to machinery.
items.cn: 十九世纪时 programming 指排定音乐会、演出季或课程的节目顺序，与机器无关。

items.en: From the 1940s and 1950s the same gerund named the new work of preparing instructions for an electronic computer, and that sense soon dominated.
items.cn: 自 1940 至 1950 年代，同一个动名词开始指为电子计算机准备指令的新工作，这一义很快占了主导。

items.en: Radio and television kept the older scheduling sense alive: programming is what a channel planner does, distinct from writing software.
items.cn: 广播与电视让较早的「排顺序」义活了下来：programming 是频道编排者做的事，与写软件不同。

items.en: The base noun and the native gerund ending are both documented, and the formation is transparent. Only the earliest recorded dates of the scheduling and computing senses are approximate, and any deeper Indo-European root for graphein is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 首见年代不确定：基础名词与英语本族动名词词尾都有文献依据，构词关系清楚；只是「排日程」义与计算机义的最早记录年代为约数，为 graphein 提出的更早印欧语词根属于重构形式。

note.en: The first group is the same stem in its other roles; the second group names the neighbouring activities of coding, building software and scheduling.
note.cn: 第一组是同一词干的其他角色；第二组是与写代码、做软件、排日程相邻的说法。

entries.definition: One finished set of instructions, or the plan behind it; programming is the work that produces it.
entries.definitionCN: 指一套写好的指令或背后的计划；programming 是产出它的工作。

entries.definition: The person doing the work; it is the agent noun built with -er on the same base.
entries.definitionCN: 指从事这项工作的人；它是同一词干加 -er 构成的施事名词。

entries.definition: The British spelling of the noun, and the usual word for the printed order of a performance.
entries.definitionCN: 名词的英式拼写，也常指演出的印刷节目单。

entries.definition: Able to receive and hold a new sequence; it describes a capacity, not the work of writing the sequence.
entries.definitionCN: 指能够接收并保存新序列；它描述能力，不指编写序列的工作。

entries.definition: The hands-on writing of code, often used for the practical side; programming also covers design, testing and reasoning.
entries.definitionCN: 指动手写代码，常指实务那面；programming 还包括设计、测试与推理。

entries.definition: The whole process of building software, including requirements, design, testing and maintenance; programming is its central craft.
entries.definitionCN: 指构建软件的全过程，含需求、设计、测试与维护；programming 是其中的核心手艺。

entries.definition: Writing short programs that automate a task, usually in an interpreted language; narrower and more task-bound than programming.
entries.definitionCN: 指编写自动完成某任务的短程序，多用于解释型语言；比 programming 更窄、更贴任务。

entries.definition: Arranging times and dates; it overlaps with the older sense of programming but says nothing about content or code.
entries.definitionCN: 指安排时间与日期；与 programming 较早的词义有交集，但不涉及内容或代码。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real base noun, the real ending and the real phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的基础名词、真实的词尾与真实的搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Program plus -ing: the ending turns the product into the ongoing work.
normal.cn: program 加 -ing：词尾把成品变成正在进行的工作。

normal.en: The family runs program, programming, programmer, programmable and reprogram.
normal.cn: 同族词有 program、programming、programmer、programmable 与 reprogram。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the computing sense: programming language, pair programming, programming model.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出计算机义：编程语言、结对编程、编程模型。

normal.en: The same word still means arranging a festival or a channel, which is why a concert hall can have a programmer too.
normal.cn: 这个词仍指编排音乐节或频道，所以音乐厅也会有节目编排者。

normal.en: A gerund can name a body of material, so the code stored in a machine is simply its programming.
normal.cn: 动名词可以指一整套材料，所以机器里存的代码就叫它的程序。

abstract.en: Picture a note that keeps being rewritten while the machine reads it aloud.
abstract.cn: 想象一张笔记，机器一边朗读，它一边被改写。

abstract.en: Picture a garden whose planting order is decided years before the first seed.
abstract.cn: 想象一座花园，播种顺序在第一粒种子之前几年就定好了。

abstract.en: Picture a thermostat humming a small tune it was taught once and never forgets.
abstract.cn: 想象一台恒温器哼着一支被教会一次就再没忘记的小调。

examples.en: Programming is now taught alongside mathematics in many schools.
examples.cn: 如今许多学校把编程与数学一起教。

examples.en: The programming in this device cannot be changed by the user.
examples.cn: 这台设备里的程序用户无法更改。

examples.en: Her festival programming put new composers beside old ones.
examples.cn: 她的音乐节编排把新作曲家与老作曲家放在一起。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑（pro）来（gram）明（ming）」——事先把步骤写明白，就是编程

root: 希腊 pro-「在前」+ graphein「书写」→ programma → 法语 programme → 英语 program；再加英语动名词词尾 -ing 构成 programming。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses split into two eras: first the arranging of events, then the writing, storing, teaching, setting and embedding of machine instructions.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项分属两个时期：先是对活动的编排，后是对机器指令的编写、存储、教学、设定与内置。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a written sequence of steps, either held by a planner or loaded into a machine.
core.cn: 核心意象：一份写好的步骤序列，或握在编排者手里，或被装进机器。

branches.en: WORK AND PRODUCT: the same gerund names the doing and the code that results from it.
branches.cn: 工作与成品：同一个动名词既指「做」，也指由此产生的代码。

branches.en: DISCIPLINE: methods and theory turn the activity into a taught subject.
branches.cn: 学科：方法与理论把这项活动变成可教的科目。

branches.en: SCHEDULING: a festival and a channel are both programmed by deciding order, with no machine in sight.
branches.cn: 排期：音乐节与频道都靠决定顺序来编排，完全不涉及机器。

branches.en: SETTING MACHINES: the sequence is entered into a timer, a robot or a lathe, none of which is a general computer.
branches.cn: 设定机器：序列被输入定时器、机器人或车床，它们都不是通用计算机。

branches.en: BUILT-IN BEHAVIOUR: once sealed inside a product, the sequence is the behaviour itself.
branches.cn: 内置行为：序列一旦封进产品，它就是行为本身。

intro.en: The word is a Greek-derived noun wearing a native English ending: programma supplies the base, -ing supplies the sense of ongoing activity.
intro.cn: 这个词是希腊来源的名词戴着英语本族词尾：programma 提供词干，-ing 提供「持续活动」的意思。

latinIntro.en: Latin contributes only programma, the learned noun that reached English through French; the working parts of programming itself are Greek and English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语只贡献了 programma 这个经法语进入英语的学术名词；programming 本身的构件则来自希腊语与英语。

items.exampleCN: 基础名词提供了「书面计划」的意象。

items.example: The verb is the oldest layer of the family.
